ingredients: 1.6 kg (3.5 lb) whole chicken, cut into 8 pieces
1 litre (4 cups) peanut oil or lard, for frying
steps: Mix the buttermilk, hot sauce and 1 tsp salt, add the chicken pieces, cover and refrigerate overnight (at least 8 hours).
Whisk the flour with the remaining salt, pepper, paprika, garlic powder and onion powder in a wide bowl or paper bag.
Lift each piece from the buttermilk, let excess drip off, then press firmly into the seasoned flour until well coated; rest on a rack for 10 minutes so the coating sets.
Heat the oil to 165°C (325°F) in a heavy cast-iron skillet or Dutch oven, filled about 4 cm (1.5 in) deep.

Fry the chicken in batches without crowding, turning once, for 12–15 minutes for breasts and wings and 15–18 minutes for thighs and drumsticks, until deep golden and the thickest part reads 74°C (165°F).
Drain on a rack set over a tray, salt lightly while hot, and serve with biscuits, collard greens and mashed potatoes.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.4 kg (3 lb) bone-in chicken thighs and breasts
250 g (2 cups) all-purpose flour, plus extra for rolling
60 g (4 tbsp) cold butter or lard
180 ml (3/4 cup) whole milk or buttermilk
steps: Simmer the chicken with the water, onion, celery, carrots, bay leaf and 1 tsp salt over low heat for 45 minutes until the meat is tender and cooked through.
Lift out the chicken, shred the meat off the bones and discard skin and bones; strain the broth back into the pot, keeping the carrots.
For the "rolled" dumplings, mix the flour, baking powder and 1/2 tsp salt, rub in the butter, then stir in the milk to form a soft dough.
Roll the dough 3 mm (1/8 in) thick on a floured board and cut into 3 x 5 cm (1 x 2 in) strips.
Bring the broth to a steady simmer, drop in the strips one by one, stir gently, cover and cook for 15 minutes until the dumplings are tender and the broth has thickened.
Return the chicken, season with pepper and salt, and serve hot in bowls.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 bone-in pork chops, about 2 cm (3/4 in) thick
60 ml (1/4 cup) vegetable oil or bacon drippings
steps: Season the chops with the Creole salt and pepper, then dredge in half the flour, shaking off the excess.
Heat the oil in a large cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat and brown the chops for 3–4 minutes per side; set aside.

Lower the heat to medium, cook the onion in the drippings for 8 minutes until soft and golden, add the garlic for 1 minute, then sprinkle in the remaining flour and stir for 3 minutes until it becomes a light brown roux.
Whisk in the stock and thyme gradually until smooth and bring to a simmer.
Return the chops, cover and simmer on low for 30–35 minutes until tender and the gravy coats a spoon; the pork must reach at least 63°C (145°F).
Serve smothered in the onion gravy over white rice or mashed potatoes.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 catfish fillets, about 170 g (6 oz) each
1 litre (4 cups) peanut or vegetable oil, for frying
steps: Soak the catfish in the buttermilk and hot sauce for 30 minutes in the fridge.
Combine the cornmeal, flour, Cajun seasoning and salt in a shallow dish.
Heat the oil to 175°C (350°F) in a deep skillet or Dutch oven.
Drain each fillet, coat thoroughly in the cornmeal mix and fry 2 at a time for 5–6 minutes, turning once, until golden and the fish flakes easily.
Drain on a rack and serve hot with lemon, tartar sauce, hush puppies and coleslaw.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2.3 kg (5 lb) frozen pre-cleaned pork chitterlings, thawed
2 tsp hot sauce, plus extra to serve
steps: Even if sold pre-cleaned, rinse the chitterlings in several changes of cold water, pulling off any remaining fat, membrane or debris piece by piece; work on a sanitised surface and wash hands and counters well afterwards.
Place the cleaned chitterlings in a large pot, cover with fresh water and bring to a boil for 5 minutes, then drain and refill with fresh water (this reduces the odour).
Add the onion, bell pepper, garlic, vinegar, salt, pepper flakes and bay leaves, bring back to a boil, then lower to a gentle simmer.
Simmer covered for 3–3 1/2 hours, topping up with water as needed, until very tender.
Drain, cut into bite-size pieces and serve hot with hot sauce, vinegar, collard greens, potato salad and cornbread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.4 kg (3 lb) beef oxtails, cut into pieces
steps: Season the oxtails with seasoned salt and pepper, then dust with flour.
Heat the oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat and brown the oxtails on all sides in batches, about 8 minutes per batch; set aside.
Cook the onion and bell pepper in the drippings for 6 minutes until soft, add the garlic for 1 minute, then pour in the stock, Worcestershire, thyme and bay leaves, scraping up the browned bits.
Return the oxtails, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low (or bake at 160°C / 325°F) for 3–3 1/2 hours until the meat falls from the bone and the gravy is thick.
Skim off excess fat and serve over white rice with cabbage or collard greens.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 litre (4 cups) peanut oil, for frying
120 ml (1/2 cup) maple syrup or cane syrup, warmed
steps: Marinate the chicken overnight in 240 ml (1 cup) buttermilk with 1 tsp seasoned salt.
Dredge the chicken in 250 g (2 cups) flour mixed with the remaining seasoned salt and pepper, then fry at 165°C (325°F) for 12–15 minutes until golden and 74°C (165°F) inside; drain on a rack.
For the waffles, whisk the remaining flour, sugar and baking powder, then mix in the remaining buttermilk, eggs and melted butter until just combined.
Cook the batter in a hot greased waffle iron for 4–5 minutes per waffle until crisp and golden.
Stir the hot sauce into the warm syrup and serve the chicken on top of the waffles with butter and the spicy syrup.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 cans (418 g / 14.75 oz each) pink salmon, drained, skin and large bones removed
40 g (1/4 cup) green bell pepper, finely chopped
1 tsp Old Bay or Creole seasoning
80 ml (1/3 cup) vegetable oil, for shallow frying
steps: Flake the salmon in a bowl, mashing in the soft bones for calcium if you like.
Mix in the egg, onion, bell pepper, cornmeal, flour, seasoning and pepper until the mix holds together.
Shape into 8 patties about 2 cm (3/4 in) thick and chill for 10 minutes to firm up.
Heat the oil in a cast-iron skillet over medium heat and fry the patties for 3–4 minutes per side until crisp, golden and hot through.
Drain on paper towels and serve with grits, rice or biscuits for a classic Sunday breakfast.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 slices (about 450 g / 1 lb) dry-cured country ham, 6 mm (1/4 in) thick
240 ml (1 cup) strong black brewed coffee
steps: If the ham is very salty, soak the slices in warm water for 10 minutes and pat dry; snip the fat edge in a few places so it doesn't curl.
Melt the lard in a cast-iron skillet over medium heat and fry the ham for 3–4 minutes per side until browned at the edges; transfer to a warm platter.
Pour the coffee and water into the hot skillet, add the sugar if using, and scrape up all the browned bits.
Boil for 3–4 minutes until slightly reduced; the gravy stays thin, with an "eye" of fat floating on top.
Season with pepper, spoon the red-eye gravy over the ham and serve with grits and buttermilk biscuits.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 160 g (1 cup) stone-ground white or yellow grits (not instant)
950 ml (4 cups) water, or half water and half milk
steps: Bring the water and salt to a boil in a heavy saucepan.
Slowly whisk in the grits to prevent lumps, then reduce to low.
Cook for 25–30 minutes, stirring often and adding a splash of hot water if they get too thick, until creamy and the grains are tender.
Remove from the heat and stir in the butter, cheddar, cream and pepper until melted and smooth.
Serve hot alongside eggs, or as a base for shrimp and grits.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.2 kg (2.5 lb) bone-in chicken thighs and drumsticks
1 litre (4 cups) peanut oil or lard, for frying
steps: Marinate the chicken overnight in the buttermilk, hot sauce and 1 tsp salt.
Dredge in the flour seasoned with the remaining salt, then fry at 165°C (325°F) for 15–18 minutes until golden and 74°C (165°F) inside; drain on a rack.
Carefully ladle 120 ml (1/2 cup) of the hot frying oil into a heatproof bowl and whisk in the cayenne, brown sugar, paprika and garlic powder to make the hot paste.
Brush the spicy oil generously all over the hot fried chicken.
Serve each piece on a slice of white bread, topped with pickle chips, the traditional Nashville way.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 racks pork baby back ribs (about 2 kg / 4.5 lb)
120 ml (1/2 cup) cider vinegar mixed with 120 ml (1/2 cup) water, for mopping
steps: Pull the thin membrane off the bone side of each rack and pat dry.
Mix all the dry spices into a rub, reserve 3 tbsp, and coat the ribs all over; rest for 1 hour at room temperature or overnight in the fridge.
Set a smoker or covered grill for indirect heat at 110–120°C (225–250°F) with hickory wood.
Smoke the ribs bone-side down for 4–5 hours, mopping with the vinegar mix every hour, until the meat pulls back from the bones and a toothpick slides in easily.
Sprinkle with the reserved rub just before serving; Memphis "dry" ribs come without sauce, with slaw and beans on the side.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 480 ml (2 cups) tomato-based Memphis barbecue sauce
120 ml (1/2 cup) pasta water or chicken stock
steps: Cook the spaghetti in well-salted boiling water for 1 minute less than the package says; reserve some pasta water and drain.
Heat the oil in a large pan over medium heat and sauté the onion and bell pepper for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the barbecue sauce, pasta water and dry rub, and simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in the pulled pork until heated through, then toss with the spaghetti for 2 minutes over low heat until well coated.
Serve as a side with ribs or as a main, with extra sauce and coleslaw.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 3.6 kg (8 lb) bone-in pork shoulder (Boston butt)
4 tbsp Memphis dry rub (paprika, brown sugar, salt, pepper, garlic)
240 ml (1 cup) cider vinegar mixed with 120 ml (1/2 cup) apple juice, for spritzing
steps: Rub the pork with mustard, coat generously with the dry rub and refrigerate overnight.
Smoke over hickory at 110–120°C (225–250°F) for 10–12 hours, spritzing every 2 hours, until it reaches 90–95°C (195–203°F) inside and the bone wiggles free.
Wrap in foil and rest for 30–60 minutes, then pull the meat into shreds with forks, discarding fat and bone.
Toss the pork with a little barbecue sauce.
Pile the pork on the buns, top with coleslaw (the Memphis way) and serve with extra sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 480 g (3 cups) yellow cornmeal (Delta tamales use cornmeal, not masa)
120 ml (1/2 cup) lard or vegetable oil
48 dried corn husks, or parchment strips
steps: Soak the corn husks in hot water for 30 minutes until pliable.
Mix the beef with half the spices, 1 tsp salt and the garlic; roll into finger-sized logs, about 2 tbsp each.
Mix the cornmeal, remaining salt, half the remaining spices, lard and 360 ml (1 1/2 cups) hot stock into a soft paste.
Spread a thin layer of cornmeal paste on each husk, place a meat log on top, roll up and fold the bottom; tie in bundles of 6.
Stand the bundles upright in a deep pot, add the rest of the stock and spices to come two-thirds up, cover and simmer gently for 1 1/2–2 hours until the meat is cooked through.
Serve the tamales hot in their husks with a ladle of the spicy simmering liquid and saltine crackers.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Melt the butter in a large Dutch oven over medium heat and cook the onion for 6 minutes until soft.
Add the tomatoes, stock, barbecue sauce, Worcestershire, vinegar and hot sauce and bring to a simmer.
Stir in the pork, chicken, lima beans and corn.
Simmer uncovered on low for 1–1 1/2 hours, stirring often so it doesn't stick, until thick enough to hold a spoon.
Season to taste and serve with saltines or cornbread alongside barbecue.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 smoked ham hock or smoked turkey wing (about 450 g / 1 lb)
900 g (2 lb) collard or turnip greens, stemmed and chopped
steps: Simmer the ham hock in the water for 1 hour to make a smoky broth.
Add the greens, onion, garlic and pepper flakes and simmer for 45–60 minutes until the greens are silky.
Pull the meat from the hock and return it to the pot; season with salt and vinegar.
Ladle the nutrient-rich broth (the "pot likker") into bowls with some greens and meat, and serve with cornbread for dunking.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.4 kg (3 lb) collard greens, washed, stemmed and sliced into ribbons
1 smoked turkey leg or ham hock (about 450 g / 1 lb)
1.2 litres (5 cups) chicken stock or water
2 tbsp bacon drippings or vegetable oil
steps: Simmer the smoked turkey in the stock for 45 minutes to build flavour.
In a separate large pot, heat the drippings over medium heat and cook the onion for 5 minutes, then the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the greens a handful at a time, letting them wilt, then pour in the smoky stock and turkey.
Add the vinegar, sugar, pepper flakes and salt, cover and simmer on low for 1–1 1/2 hours until very tender.
Shred the turkey meat back into the pot and serve with the pot likker, hot sauce and cornbread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 450 g (1 lb) dried black-eyed peas, soaked overnight and drained
1.5 litres (6 cups) water or chicken stock
steps: Simmer the ham hock in the water for 30 minutes.
Add the soaked peas, onion, celery, garlic, bay leaf and pepper flakes and bring back to a simmer.
Cook gently, partly covered, for 45–60 minutes until the peas are creamy but still whole.
Shred the hock meat into the pot, season with salt and serve with rice and greens; eaten on New Year's Day for luck.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 900 g (2 lb) fresh or frozen butter beans (baby limas)
115 g (4 oz) salt pork or thick bacon, diced
1 litre (4 cups) chicken stock or water
steps: Fry the salt pork in a saucepan over medium heat for 6 minutes until the fat renders.
Add the onion and cook for 4 minutes until soft.
Add the butter beans and stock, bring to a boil, then simmer gently for 45–50 minutes until tender and the liquid turns creamy.
Stir in the butter, salt and pepper and serve with cornbread and sliced tomatoes.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.4 kg (3 lb) orange sweet potatoes (called "yams" in the US), peeled and sliced 1.5 cm (1/2 in) thick
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F) and layer the sweet potatoes in a baking dish.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, stir in both sugars, spices and salt and simmer for 3 minutes until syrupy; stir in the vanilla.
Pour the syrup over the sweet potatoes, cover with foil and bake for 35 minutes.
Uncover, baste with the syrup and bake another 20–25 minutes until tender and glazed.
Serve warm as a holiday or Sunday dinner side.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Soul Food Baked Macaroni and Cheese

ingredients: 450 g (4 cups) sharp cheddar, grated, divided
225 g (2 cups) Colby or Monterey Jack, grated
1 can (354 ml / 12 fl oz) evaporated milk
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and butter a 23 x 33 cm (9 x 13 in) dish.
Boil the macaroni in salted water for 2 minutes less than the package says, drain and toss with the melted butter.
Whisk the eggs, evaporated milk, whole milk, salt and pepper.
Layer half the macaroni with half the cheeses, repeat, then pour the egg-milk mixture over and top with the last of the cheddar and the paprika.
Bake for 35–40 minutes until set and bubbly with a golden crust; rest 10 minutes before cutting into squares.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 240 g (1 1/2 cups) stone-ground yellow or white cornmeal
4 tbsp bacon drippings or butter, divided
steps: Put 2 tbsp drippings into a 25 cm (10 in) cast-iron skillet and heat in a 220°C (425°F) oven for 10 minutes until smoking hot.
Whisk the cornmeal, flour, baking powder, soda and salt; in another bowl whisk the eggs, buttermilk and remaining melted drippings.
Combine wet and dry with a few strokes until just mixed.
Pour the batter into the sizzling skillet and bake for 20–25 minutes until golden with a crisp crust.
Turn out and serve hot with butter, greens or beans.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 240 g (1 1/2 cups) fine white or yellow cornmeal
240 ml (1 cup) vegetable oil, for frying
steps: Mix the cornmeal, salt and sugar in a bowl and add the butter.
Pour in the boiling water, stirring, until a thick, moldable dough forms; rest for 5 minutes.
With wet hands, shape the dough into small oval patties about 1.5 cm (1/2 in) thick.
Heat the oil in a cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat and fry the patties for 3–4 minutes per side until crisp and golden.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with greens, beans or pot likker.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 240 ml (1 cup) hot water or buttermilk
3 tbsp vegetable oil or butter, for the griddle
steps: Mix the cornmeal, salt and baking powder in a bowl.
Stir in the hot water and melted butter to make a thick pourable batter; rest for 5 minutes.
Heat a cast-iron griddle over medium heat, film with oil and drop 2 tbsp batter per cake, spreading to 8 cm (3 in) rounds.
Cook for 2–3 minutes per side until lacy, crisp and golden.
Serve hot with butter and cane syrup or alongside greens.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 315 g (2 1/2 cups) soft Southern all-purpose flour (e.g. White Lily), plus extra
115 g (1/2 cup) cold unsalted butter, cubed
steps: Heat the oven to 230°C (450°F) and line a baking sheet or butter a cast-iron skillet.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, soda, salt and sugar, then cut in the cold butter until pea-size pieces remain.
Stir in the buttermilk just until a shaggy dough forms, turn onto a floured board and fold it over itself 4 times.
Pat to 2.5 cm (1 in) thick and cut straight down with a floured cutter without twisting; place the biscuits touching.
Bake for 12–15 minutes until tall and golden, brush with melted butter and serve hot with butter, honey or sausage gravy.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F) and butter a 2-litre (2-quart) baking dish.
Bring the milk to a simmer, whisk in the cornmeal and cook for 3–4 minutes, stirring, until thick like porridge; remove from the heat and stir in the butter, salt and sugar.
Cool for 5 minutes, then beat in the egg yolks and baking powder.
Whip the egg whites to soft peaks and fold gently into the cornmeal mixture.
Bake for 35–40 minutes until puffed, golden and just set in the centre; serve at once with a spoon, like a soufflé.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 litre (4 cups) vegetable or peanut oil, for frying
steps: Whisk the cornmeal, flour, baking powder, salt and sugar.
Stir in the onion, egg and buttermilk to make a thick batter; rest for 10 minutes.
Heat the oil to 175°C (350°F) and drop in heaped teaspoons of batter, a few at a time.
Fry for 3–4 minutes, turning, until deep golden and cooked through.
Drain and serve hot with fried catfish and tartar sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 firm green (unripe) tomatoes, sliced 1 cm (1/3 in) thick
2 eggs beaten with 60 ml (1/4 cup) buttermilk
30 g (1/2 cup) panko or fine breadcrumbs
240 ml (1 cup) vegetable oil, for shallow frying
steps: Salt the tomato slices and let them drain on paper towels for 10 minutes; pat dry.
Set up three dishes: flour; egg-buttermilk; cornmeal mixed with breadcrumbs and cayenne.
Dredge each slice in flour, dip in egg and press into the cornmeal coating.
Heat the oil in a cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat and fry for 2–3 minutes per side until golden and crisp.
Drain and serve hot with comeback sauce or remoulade.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 450 g (1 lb) fresh okra, sliced into 1.5 cm (1/2 in) rounds
480 ml (2 cups) vegetable oil, for frying
steps: Toss the okra in the buttermilk and let sit for 10 minutes.
Mix the cornmeal, flour, salt, pepper and cayenne in a bag or bowl.
Lift the okra out with a slotted spoon, add to the cornmeal and shake to coat well.
Heat the oil to 175°C (350°F) in a skillet and fry in batches for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until golden and crisp.
Drain, salt again lightly and serve hot as a side or snack.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 900 g (2 lb) yellow summer squash, sliced
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and butter a 2-litre (2-quart) baking dish.
Simmer the squash and onion in a little salted water for 10 minutes until tender; drain very well and mash lightly.
Mix in the eggs, sour cream, cheddar, 2 tbsp melted butter, salt and pepper, and spread in the dish.
Toss the crushed crackers with the remaining melted butter and scatter over the top.
Bake for 30–35 minutes until set and golden; serve as a summer or Thanksgiving side.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Bake the sweet potatoes at 200°C (400°F) for 45–55 minutes until very soft; cool slightly, peel and mash.
Reduce the oven to 180°C (350°F) and beat the mash with the sugar, eggs, melted butter, milk, vanilla and salt until smooth; spread in a buttered baking dish.
Rub the brown sugar, flour and cold butter together into crumbs and mix in the pecans.
Scatter the pecan streusel over the top.
Bake for 30 minutes until set and the topping is crisp; serve at Thanksgiving.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.4 kg (3 lb) russet or Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and cubed
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 12–15 minutes until fork-tender but not falling apart; drain and cool.
Whisk the mayonnaise, mustard, relish, salt and pepper.
Fold the potatoes, eggs, celery and onion into the dressing, mashing a few potatoes for creaminess.
Chill for at least 1 hour, dust with paprika and serve with barbecue or fried chicken.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 can (567 g / 20 oz) pineapple chunks, drained
1 can (312 g / 11 oz) mandarin oranges, drained
steps: Pat the drained fruit dry so the salad isn't watery.
Fold the sour cream into the whipped cream.
Gently fold in the pineapple, oranges, cherries, marshmallows, coconut and pecans.
Chill for at least 2 hours so the marshmallows soften, and serve cold at holidays and potlucks.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Cover the eggs with cold water, bring to a boil, then cover, remove from the heat and stand for 12 minutes.
Cool in ice water, peel and halve lengthwise.
Mash the yolks with the mayonnaise, mustard, relish, salt and pepper until smooth.
Pipe or spoon the filling into the whites, dust with paprika and chill until serving.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 jar (680 g / 24 oz) dill pickle chips, drained and patted dry
1 egg beaten with 120 ml (1/2 cup) buttermilk
30 g (1/4 cup) flour, extra for the coating
1 litre (4 cups) vegetable oil, for frying
120 ml (1/2 cup) ranch dressing, to serve
steps: Dry the pickles thoroughly on paper towels.
Toss in the flour, dip in the egg-buttermilk, then coat in the cornmeal mixed with the extra flour and Cajun seasoning.
Heat the oil to 190°C (375°F) and fry in batches for 2–3 minutes until golden.
Drain and serve hot with ranch dressing.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 900 g (2 lb) chicken gizzards, cleaned and trimmed
1 litre (4 cups) peanut oil, for frying
steps: Simmer the gizzards in the salted water for 1 hour until tender (they are tough otherwise); drain and cool.
Soak the gizzards in the buttermilk and hot sauce overnight in the fridge.
Dredge in the flour mixed with seasoned salt and pepper.
Fry at 175°C (350°F) for 4–5 minutes until crisp and golden.
Drain and serve hot with hot sauce and white bread or fries.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 900 g (2 lb) raw "green" peanuts in the shell (or dried raw peanuts, soaked overnight)
steps: Rinse the peanuts well in cold water, removing any debris.
Put them in a large pot with the water, salt and spices; weigh them down with a plate so they stay submerged.
Bring to a boil, then simmer partly covered for 4–6 hours (dried peanuts may need 8+), topping up with water, until the shells are soft and the nuts are tender like cooked beans.
Turn off the heat and let them soak in the brine for another hour for more flavour.
Drain and serve warm in paper cups, shelling as you eat, like at roadside stands across Georgia and South Carolina.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 900 g (2 lb) watermelon rind, green skin and pink flesh removed, cut into 2.5 cm (1 in) pieces
steps: Dissolve the salt in the water, add the rind and soak overnight in the fridge; drain and rinse.
Simmer the rind in fresh water for 10–15 minutes until just translucent but still firm; drain.
Boil the vinegar, sugar and spices for 5 minutes to make the syrup.
Add the rind and simmer for 30–40 minutes until clear and glossy.
Pack into clean jars with the syrup, cool and refrigerate for up to 1 month; serve with ham or fried chicken.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 60 ml (1/4 cup) chili sauce or ketchup
1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce (use a vegetarian brand to keep it anchovy-free)
steps: Whisk all the ingredients together in a bowl until smooth and emulsified.
Chill for at least 1 hour so the flavours meld.
Serve as a dip for fried pickles, fries, onion rings and crackers, or on salads and burgers; keeps 1 week refrigerated.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Whisk all the ingredients until smooth; it should be thin enough to drizzle.
Chill for at least 1 hour.
Brush onto smoked chicken during the final minutes of cooking and serve extra on the side, as in northern Alabama.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Boil the whole sweet potatoes in their skins for 40–50 minutes until very soft; cool, peel and mash.
Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F).
Beat the warm mash with the butter until smooth, then beat in the sugar, evaporated milk, eggs, vanilla, spices and salt.
Pour into the crust and bake for 55–60 minutes until the centre is just set with a slight jiggle.
Cool completely and serve with whipped cream at Thanksgiving or Sunday dinner.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 240 ml (1 cup) light corn syrup or cane syrup
steps: Heat the oven to 175°C (350°F).
Whisk the syrup, brown sugar, eggs, butter, vanilla and salt until smooth.
Spread the pecans in the crust and pour the filling over.
Bake for 55–60 minutes, covering the edges with foil if they brown too fast, until the centre is set but slightly wobbly.
Cool for at least 2 hours before slicing; serve with vanilla ice cream.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Heat the oven to 175°C (350°F).
Whisk the sugar and flour, then beat in the eggs, butter, buttermilk, lemon juice and vanilla until smooth.
Pour into the crust and dust with nutmeg.
Bake for 50–55 minutes until golden on top and set with a gentle jiggle in the centre.
Cool completely before serving; it has a tangy, custardy, chess-pie texture.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

Whisk the flour, remaining sugar, milk and vanilla into a smooth egg-free batter and pour it over the melted butter without stirring.

240 ml (1 cup) heavy cream, whipped with 2 tbsp sugar
steps: Whisk the sugar, flour and salt in a saucepan, then whisk in the milk and egg yolks.

1 batch cream cheese frosting (450 g / 16 oz cream cheese, 225 g / 1 cup butter, 480 g / 4 cups powdered sugar)
steps: Heat the oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease and flour three 23 cm (9 in) round pans.
Whisk the flour, sugar, soda, cinnamon and salt.

steps: Heat the oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease two 23 cm (9 in) pans; cream 170 g (3/4 cup) butter with the sugar, beat in the eggs, then add the flour, baking powder and salt alternately with the milk and 1 tsp vanilla.

steps: Heat the oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease three 23 cm (9 in) pans; cream 170 g (3/4 cup) butter with 300 g (1 1/2 cups) sugar, add the flour mix alternately with the milk and vanilla, then fold in the egg whites.

steps: Heat the oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease a 23 x 33 cm (9 x 13 in) pan; whisk the flour, sugar and soda.

Pour the warm icing over the hot cake and cool before cutting into squares.

steps: Heat the oven to 175°C (350°F) and press the crumb mixture into a 23 cm (9 in) pie dish; bake for 8 minutes.

steps: Simmer the dried fruit in the water for 20–25 minutes until soft and the liquid is absorbed; mash with the sugar and cinnamon and cool.

ingredients: 180 g (1 cup) stone-ground white grits (or coarse polenta as a substitute)
1 L (4 cups) water or light chicken stock, plus milk to loosen
115 g (1 cup) grated sharp white cheddar
680 g (1.5 lb) large local shrimp, peeled and deveined
115 g (4 oz) thick-cut bacon or tasso ham, diced
1 small onion and 1 small green bell pepper, finely diced
240 ml (1 cup) chicken or shrimp stock, 1 tbsp lemon juice and a dash of hot sauce
4 scallions, sliced, salt and black pepper
steps: Bring the water or stock to a boil with 1 tsp salt, whisk in the grits slowly, then simmer on low heat for 35–45 minutes, stirring often and adding splashes of milk, until thick, creamy and no longer gritty; stir in 2 tbsp butter and the cheddar.

Pour in the stock, lemon juice and hot sauce, swirl in the remaining butter, and simmer 2 minutes until a light gravy forms; return the bacon and season.
Spoon the hot grits into shallow bowls, top with the shrimp and gravy, and scatter with scallions.

ingredients: 80 g (1/2 cup) Old Bay or Lowcountry seafood boil seasoning
1.2 kg (2.5 lb) small red new potatoes
900 g (2 lb) smoked pork or beef sausage (kielbasa), cut in 5 cm (2 in) pieces
6 ears fresh corn, shucked and halved
115 g (1/2 cup) melted butter and cocktail sauce, to serve
steps: Bring the water, seasoning, lemons and onion to a rolling boil in a very large stockpot over high heat.

Add the sausage and corn and boil 8–10 minutes more until the corn is bright and tender.

ingredients: 1 small onion and 1 celery stalk, very finely minced
450 g (1 lb) lump blue crab meat, picked over for shell
2 tbsp crab roe (traditional "she-crab" roe; substitute 2 crumbled hard-cooked egg yolks if unavailable)
1/2 tsp ground mace, 1/2 tsp Worcestershire sauce and a pinch of white pepper
60 ml (1/4 cup) dry sherry, plus more to serve
steps: Melt the butter in a heavy saucepan over medium-low heat and soften the onion and celery for 5 minutes without browning.
Stir in the flour and cook 2 minutes, then gradually whisk in the milk and cream and simmer gently for 10 minutes until slightly thickened, never letting it boil hard.
Add the crab meat, roe, mace, Worcestershire and white pepper and heat through for 5–8 minutes over low heat.
Stir in the sherry, season with salt, and serve in warmed bowls with a small splash of extra sherry at the table.

ingredients: 450 g (1 lb) beef shank or smoked turkey wing
450 g (1 lb) fresh okra, sliced into rounds
800 g (28 oz) canned or fresh chopped tomatoes
140 g (1 cup) fresh or frozen corn kernels
140 g (1 cup) fresh or frozen lima beans (butter beans)
2 bay leaves, 1 tsp dried thyme, salt and black pepper
Cooked long-grain white rice, to serve
steps: Simmer the beef or smoked turkey with the water, onion and bay leaves, partly covered, over low heat for 60 minutes until the meat is tender.
Lift out the meat, pull it from the bone in bite-size pieces, discard the bones and return the meat to the pot.
Add the okra, tomatoes, corn, lima beans and thyme and simmer 30 minutes until the okra is soft and the soup has thickened.
Season with salt, pepper and hot sauce, and serve ladled over or alongside white rice, as in Gullah Geechee homes.

2 celery stalks and 1 green bell pepper, chopped (the "trinity")
370 g (2 cups) long-grain white rice (Carolina Gold if available)
1 bay leaf, 1/2 tsp red pepper flakes, salt and black pepper
steps: Soak the peas overnight in plenty of cold water, then drain.
Simmer the ham hock in the water with the onion, celery, pepper, garlic and bay leaf for 30 minutes, then add the peas and cook 30–40 minutes until just tender.
Remove the hock, shred the meat and return it; measure about 720 ml (3 cups) of liquid in the pot (top up with water or ladle off extra), season well with salt, pepper and pepper flakes.
Stir in the rice, bring to a boil, cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 20 minutes until the rice is tender and the liquid absorbed.
Rest covered 5 minutes, fluff with a fork and serve topped with scallions, traditionally with collards and cornbread on New Year's Day.

370 g (2 cups) long-grain white rice (Carolina Gold if available)

steps: Heat the oven to 175°C (350°F) and fry the bacon in an ovenproof Dutch oven over medium heat for 6 minutes until crisp.

Stir in the tomato paste and cook 2 minutes until brick red, then add the crushed tomatoes, stock, sugar, cayenne, salt and pepper and bring to a boil.
Stir in the rice, cover tightly and bake 45–50 minutes, stirring once halfway, until the rice is tender and each grain is stained red.
Fluff and serve hot as a side to fried chicken or shrimp.

ingredients: 115 g (4 oz) smoked sausage or bacon, chopped
370 g (2 cups) long-grain rice (Carolina Gold if available)
1 tsp salt and 1 tsp black pepper
steps: Simmer the chicken in the water with the onion, celery, bay leaf, salt and pepper, covered, for 30 minutes until cooked through to 74°C (165°F).
Lift out the chicken, remove skin and bones, shred the meat and measure 960 ml (4 cups) of the broth.
Brown the sausage in the pot over medium heat for 5 minutes, then add the broth, thyme, shredded chicken and rice and bring to a boil.
Cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 20 minutes until the rice is tender and dry, Lowcountry pilau-style with separate grains.
Rest 5 minutes, fluff and scatter with parsley.

2 tsp salt, 1 1/2 tsp black pepper, 1/2 tsp poultry seasoning
steps: Simmer the chicken with the onion, celery and salt in the water, covered, for 50–60 minutes until falling off the bone.
Remove the chicken, pick the meat into small pieces, discard skin and bones, and measure 1.2 L (5 cups) of broth back into the pot.
Add the sausage, butter, pepper and poultry seasoning and bring to a boil.
Stir in the rice and chicken, cover and simmer on low heat for 20–25 minutes until the rice is soft and the dish is moist and "boggy" rather than dry.
Stir well and serve in bowls, as at Pee Dee region church suppers and the Loris Bog-Off.

450 g (1 lb) medium shrimp, peeled and deveined

steps: Fry the bacon in a heavy saucepan over medium heat for 6 minutes until crisp and lift it out, leaving the fat.

Add the rice and stir 1 minute to coat, then add the stock, cayenne, salt and pepper, bring to a boil, cover and simmer on low heat for 15 minutes.
Tuck the shrimp into the rice, cover again and cook 5–6 minutes more until the shrimp are pink and opaque and the rice is tender.

1 tbsp lemon juice and 2 tbsp chopped parsley

steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F); melt half the butter in a skillet over medium heat and soften the onion and pepper for 5 minutes.

2 tsp salt, 1 tsp black pepper and 1 tsp paprika

Hushpuppies, coleslaw and tartar sauce, to serve

1.2 kg (2.5 lb) firm white fish fillets (rockfish/striped bass or drum), cut in large pieces

ingredients: 1 bone-in pork shoulder (Boston butt plus picnic), about 4.5 kg (10 lb), as a home-scale stand-in for a whole hog
Hickory or oak wood (charcoal plus wood chunks)
720 ml (3 cups) Eastern Carolina vinegar sauce, divided
White bread or hushpuppies, slaw and Brunswick stew, to serve
steps: Rub the pork all over with salt, pepper and pepper flakes and rest while you light a smoker or kettle grill for indirect heat at 110–120°C (225–250°F) with hickory or oak.
Smoke the pork skin-side up for 8–10 hours, adding fuel as needed, until the internal temperature reaches 90–95°C (195–203°F) and the bone pulls free.
In the last hour, mop the meat with some vinegar sauce every 20 minutes and, if you like, crisp the skin directly over hotter coals.
Rest 30 minutes, then chop the meat with cleavers, mixing in bits of crisp skin, and season with more vinegar sauce and salt.
Serve on white bread or with hushpuppies, coleslaw and Brunswick stew.

ingredients: 1 bone-in pork shoulder (Boston butt), about 3.6 kg (8 lb)
2 tbsp coarse salt and 1 tbsp black pepper
2 tbsp brown sugar and 1 tsp red pepper flakes
Hamburger buns and Lexington red slaw, to serve
steps: Season the shoulder with salt and pepper and smoke it over hickory at 110–120°C (225–250°F) for 8–9 hours until it reaches 90–95°C (195–203°F) inside.
Meanwhile simmer the vinegar, ketchup, brown sugar, pepper flakes and 1 tsp salt for 5 minutes to make the Piedmont "dip".
Rest the pork 30 minutes, discard the bone and excess fat, and finely chop the meat with the dark "outside brown" bark mixed through.
Moisten the chopped pork with the dip to taste and serve on buns topped with red slaw, or on a tray with slaw and hushpuppies.

ingredients: 1.4 kg (3 lb) boneless pork shoulder, cubed
450 g (1 lb) pork liver (optional, traditional) or more shoulder
450 g (1 lb) potatoes, peeled and cubed
60 g (4 tbsp) butter, 2 tsp black pepper, 1 tsp cayenne, salt to taste
Cooked long-grain white rice, to serve

Return to the pot with the mustard, ketchup, vinegar, butter, pepper and cayenne, adding broth to make a thick, spoonable gravy.
Simmer 45–60 minutes over low heat, stirring often to prevent sticking, until dark and thick; season with salt.
Serve ladled over white rice, as at South Carolina Midlands barbecue houses.

ingredients: 1 medium green cabbage, about 900 g (2 lb), finely chopped

steps: Simmer the ketchup, vinegar, sugar, salt, pepper, pepper flakes and hot sauce for 3–5 minutes until the sugar dissolves, then cool.

2 tsp salt and 1 1/2 tsp black pepper

2 tbsp lard or oil, for frying
steps: Simmer the liver and pork in the water, covered, over low heat for 90 minutes until very tender; reserve the broth.

Slice 1 cm (1/2 in) thick and fry in lard over medium heat for 4–5 minutes per side until crisp and brown; serve with eggs, grits or on a sandwich with mustard, as in western North Carolina.

steps: Toast the sesame seeds in a dry skillet over medium heat for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until golden and fragrant, then cool.

Whisk the melted butter, brown sugar, milk and vanilla, then stir in the flour, baking powder, salt and sesame seeds.

ingredients: 1 tart apple (such as Granny Smith), peeled and finely chopped
steps: Heat the oven to 165°C (325°F) and butter a 23 x 33 cm (9 x 13 in) baking dish.

ingredients: 115 g (1/2 cup) butter or vegetable shortening, melted
100 g (1/2 cup) packed dark brown sugar
1 tbsp ground ginger and 1 tbsp ground cinnamon
1 tsp ground cloves and 1/2 tsp ground nutmeg
1 tsp baking soda and 1/2 tsp salt
steps: Stir the molasses, melted butter and brown sugar together until smooth.
Mix in the flour, spices, baking soda and salt to make a stiff dough, wrap and refrigerate overnight so the spices mellow.
Heat the oven to 175°C (350°F); roll small pieces of dough paper-thin, about 1–2 mm (1/16 in), on a floured cloth and cut into rounds.
Bake 5–7 minutes until just firm and fragrant, watching closely as they burn easily, then cool on racks until crisp; they are a Winston-Salem Christmas tradition.

ingredients: 1 medium russet potato, peeled, boiled and mashed (about 120 g / 1/2 cup)
240 ml (1 cup) warm potato cooking water
500 g (4 cups) all-purpose flour and 1 tsp salt
Topping: 220 g (1 cup) packed light brown sugar, 115 g (1/2 cup) cold butter and 2 tsp cinnamon
steps: Mix the mashed potato, warm potato water, yeast, sugar, melted butter and eggs, then beat in the flour and salt to make a soft, sticky dough.
Cover and let rise in a warm place for 1–1 1/2 hours until doubled.
Spread the dough into a greased 25 x 38 cm (10 x 15 in) pan and let rise again for 45 minutes until puffy.
Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F); poke deep holes all over with a finger, fill them with pinches of cold butter, then sprinkle with the brown sugar and cinnamon.
Bake 20–25 minutes until golden and the sugar pools are bubbling, and serve warm with coffee, Winston-Salem style.

ingredients: 1.2 kg (6 cups) sliced peaches, blackberries or sweet potatoes (cooked) in season
Batter crust: 125 g (1 cup) self-rising flour, 100 g (1/2 cup) sugar, 240 ml (1 cup) milk and 60 g (4 tbsp) melted butter
Milk "dip": 480 ml (2 cups) milk, 100 g (1/2 cup) sugar, 1 tbsp cornstarch and 1 tsp vanilla
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F); toss the fruit with sugar, flour and cinnamon, spread in a deep buttered baking dish and dot with butter.
Whisk the self-rising flour, sugar, milk and melted butter into a thin batter and pour over the fruit.
Bake 45–50 minutes until the crust is golden and the juices bubble thickly at the edges.
Meanwhile simmer the milk, sugar and cornstarch over medium heat, stirring, for 5 minutes until lightly thickened, then add the vanilla.
Serve the sonker warm in bowls with the "dip" poured over, as in Surry County, North Carolina.

ingredients: 1 1/2 sleeves saltine crackers, about 170 g (6 oz), coarsely crushed
400 g (14 oz) can sweetened condensed milk
120 ml (1/2 cup) fresh lemon or lime juice, or a mix
Whipped cream and flaky sea salt, to serve
steps: Heat the oven to 175°C (350°F); knead the crushed saltines with butter and sugar until it holds together, press into a 23 cm (9 in) pie pan and chill 15 minutes.
Bake the crust 15–18 minutes until golden, then cool slightly.
Beat the egg yolks into the condensed milk, then whisk in the citrus juice until thick and smooth.
Pour into the crust and bake 16–18 minutes until the filling is set at the edges but still slightly wobbly in the centre.
Cool, refrigerate at least 3 hours, and serve topped with whipped cream and a sprinkle of sea salt, as at North Carolina beach seafood restaurants.

ingredients: 450 g (1 lb) dried pinto beans, soaked overnight
1 smoked ham hock or 115 g (4 oz) salt pork
1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper
Cornbread: 240 g (1 1/2 cups) white or yellow cornmeal, 1 tsp baking soda, 1/2 tsp salt
3 tbsp bacon drippings, for the skillet
Chopped raw onion and chow-chow relish, to serve
steps: Soak the beans overnight in plenty of cold water, then drain and rinse.

Simmer the beans with the ham hock and water, partly covered, over low heat for 2 1/2–3 hours, stirring occasionally, until creamy and soft, mashing a few against the pot to thicken the "soup"; season with salt and pepper.
For the cornbread, heat the oven to 230°C (450°F) with the bacon drippings in a 25 cm (10 in) cast-iron skillet until smoking hot.
Mix the cornmeal, soda, salt, buttermilk and egg, swirl most of the hot fat into the batter, pour it into the skillet (it should sizzle) and bake 20 minutes until crusty and golden.
Serve the beans in bowls with the shredded hock meat, wedges of cornbread, raw onion and chow-chow.

ingredients: 250 g (2 cups) self-rising soft wheat flour (such as White Lily), plus more for dusting
85 g (6 tbsp) cold butter or lard, cubed
450 g (1 lb) bulk breakfast pork sausage
1 tsp coarse black pepper and salt to taste
steps: Heat the oven to 230°C (450°F); cut the butter into the self-rising flour until pea-sized, then stir in the buttermilk just until a shaggy dough forms.
Pat out 2 cm (3/4 in) thick on a floured board, fold twice, cut into rounds without twisting, and bake close together for 12–15 minutes until tall and golden.
Brown the sausage in a cast-iron skillet over medium heat for 8–10 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains.
Sprinkle the flour over the sausage and its fat and cook 2 minutes, then whisk in the milk and simmer 5–8 minutes until thick, seasoning generously with pepper and salt.
Split the hot biscuits and smother with the gravy.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: Hot buttermilk biscuits made with butter, to serve
steps: Whisk the sugar, cocoa, flour and salt together in a cold saucepan until no lumps remain.
Gradually whisk in the milk, then cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, for 6–8 minutes until it bubbles and thickens to a pourable pudding-like gravy.
Remove from the heat and stir in the butter and vanilla.
Spoon over split hot biscuits for a Sunday breakfast, as in the Tennessee and Kentucky hills.

ingredients: 480 ml (2 cups) heavy cream or whole milk
60 g (1/2 cup) grated Pecorino Romano, plus extra to top
8 slices thick Texas toast or white bread, crusts trimmed and toasted
450 g (1 lb) sliced roast turkey breast
steps: Melt the butter over medium heat, whisk in the flour for 2 minutes, then whisk in the cream and simmer 3–4 minutes until thick; stir in the Pecorino and season to make a Mornay sauce.
In each of four oven-safe dishes lay 2 toast slices and pile on the turkey.
Pour the Mornay over generously, add tomato slices and an extra sprinkle of Pecorino.
Broil 15 cm (6 in) below a hot broiler for 3–4 minutes until bubbly and spotted brown.
Top with two crossed slices of bacon, dust with paprika and parsley and serve at once, as created at Louisville's Brown Hotel.

ingredients: 900 g (2 lb) bone-in pork shoulder or mutton
285 g (2 cups) each corn kernels and lima beans, plus 225 g (8 oz) sliced okra
120 ml (1/2 cup) Worcestershire sauce and 60 ml (1/4 cup) cider vinegar
1 tbsp black pepper, 1 tsp cayenne and salt to taste
steps: Simmer all the meats in the water, covered, over low heat for 2 hours until falling off the bone.
Lift out the meat, discard bones and skin, shred everything and return it to the broth.
Add the onions, potatoes, tomatoes, corn, lima beans, Worcestershire, vinegar, pepper and cayenne and simmer uncovered 1 1/2–2 hours, stirring often, until thick enough for a spoon to stand up.
Add the okra in the last 30 minutes and season with salt.
Serve in bowls with cornbread or crackers, as at Kentucky Derby parties and church picnics.

ingredients: 1 bone-in mutton or lamb shoulder, about 3 kg (6.5 lb)
2 tbsp salt and 1 tbsp black pepper
Black dip: 480 ml (2 cups) water, 240 ml (1 cup) Worcestershire sauce, 240 ml (1 cup) cider vinegar
2 tbsp brown sugar, 1 tsp allspice and 1 tsp black pepper (for the dip)
White bread, pickles and raw onion, to serve
steps: Simmer the dip ingredients and lemon juice for 5 minutes and cool; this thin black Worcestershire mop is the Owensboro signature.
Season the mutton with salt and pepper and smoke over hickory at 110–120°C (225–250°F), mopping with dip every hour, for 7–8 hours until it reaches 90°C (195°F) and pulls apart.
Rest 20 minutes, then pull or chop the meat, discarding fat and bone.
Toss with more warmed dip and serve on white bread with pickles and onion, as at Owensboro's barbecue houses.

ingredients: 4 thick slices, 1 cm (1/2 in), all-beef or ring bologna
4 slices white bread or 2 hamburger buns
2 slices raw onion and 2 lettuce leaves
steps: Cut a small slit from the edge to the centre of each bologna slice so it stays flat while frying.
Fry the bologna in butter in a cast-iron skillet over medium heat for 2–3 minutes per side until browned and crisp at the edges.
Stack two slices per sandwich and lay cheese on top for the last 30 seconds to melt.
Build on bread spread with mustard or mayo, add onion and lettuce and serve hot.

ingredients: 225 g (8 oz) tender leaf lettuce, washed and dried
1/2 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper
steps: Tear the lettuce into a heatproof bowl and scatter with the green onions.
Fry the bacon in a skillet over medium heat for 6–8 minutes until crisp.
Add the vinegar, sugar, salt and pepper to the hot fat and bring to a sputtering boil for 30 seconds.
Immediately pour the hot dressing and bacon over the lettuce so it wilts or is "kilt", toss and serve at once with soup beans and cornbread.

ingredients: 680 g (1.5 lb) waxy potatoes, sliced thin
2 bunches ramps (wild leeks), about 225 g (8 oz), cleaned (substitute leeks plus garlic)
1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper
steps: Trim the ramp roots, separate the white bulbs from the green leaves, and slice both.
Fry the bacon in a large cast-iron skillet over medium heat until crisp, then add the drippings and potatoes and cook 15 minutes, turning occasionally, until tender and browned.
Add the ramp bulbs and cook 3 minutes, then add the leaves and cook 1–2 minutes until wilted.
If you like, push aside and scramble in the eggs until set; season and serve, as at West Virginia spring ramp suppers.

ingredients: 225 g (8 oz) leather britches (green beans strung and air-dried in the pod; or bought dried green beans)
1 smoked ham hock or 115 g (4 oz) salt pork
1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper
steps: Rinse the dried beans and soak them overnight in cold water, then drain.
Put the beans, ham hock, onion and fresh water in a heavy pot and bring to a boil.
Simmer covered over low heat for 2 1/2–3 hours, topping up water as needed, until the beans are tender with a smoky, earthy flavour.
Season with salt, pepper and sugar and serve with cornbread, a winter mainstay of the Appalachian table.

ingredients: 4 tart cooking apples (such as Winesap or Granny Smith), cored and sliced
steps: Melt the butter in a cast-iron skillet over medium heat.
Add the apple slices and cook 5 minutes, turning, until they begin to soften and colour.
Sprinkle with brown sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg and salt, add the water, cover and cook 8–10 minutes until tender.
Uncover and cook 2–3 minutes more until syrupy and lightly caramelised; serve with biscuits or as a side.

ingredients: 450 g (1 lb) fresh morel mushrooms ("dry-land fish" or "molly moochers")
125 g (1 cup) all-purpose flour or saltine cracker crumbs
1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper
120 ml (1/2 cup) vegetable oil or butter, for frying
steps: Halve the morels lengthwise, swish in lightly salted water to remove grit and insects, then dry well on towels; only eat morels positively identified by an expert, and never raw.
Beat the eggs with the milk, and season the flour with salt and pepper.
Dip each morel in the egg wash, then dredge in the flour.
Fry in hot oil over medium-high heat for 2–3 minutes per side until golden and cooked through; drain and salt lightly while hot.

ingredients: 320 g (2 cups) white cornmeal (stone-ground if possible)
45 g (3 tbsp) butter or vegetable shortening, for the skillet
steps: Heat the oven to 230°C (450°F) with the butter or shortening in a cast-iron skillet.
Stir the cornmeal, salt and soda together, scald with the boiling water, then mix in the buttermilk to a stiff batter.
Shape into oval pones with wet hands, about 2 cm (3/4 in) thick, and lay them in the hot fat.
Bake 25–30 minutes until the bottoms are deeply browned and crusty; serve hot with soup beans or greens.

ingredients: 2 medium potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
30 g (2 tbsp) butter or vegetable shortening, melted
steps: Put the potatoes, cornmeal, sugar and salt in a jar, cover with boiling water, cover loosely and keep very warm, about 40°C (105°F), for 12–16 hours until foamy with the distinctive cheesy aroma; this traditional starter uses no yeast.
Strain off the liquid, discard the potatoes, and mix the liquid with the warm milk, soda, butter and about 500 g (4 cups) flour into a sponge; keep warm 2 hours until bubbly.
Work in enough remaining flour to make a smooth, stiff dough, knead 10 minutes, shape into two loaves and place in greased loaf pans.
Let rise in a warm place for 2–3 hours until risen about 2.5 cm (1 in) above the pans.
Bake at 190°C (375°F) for 40–45 minutes until golden and hollow-sounding; it is best sliced and toasted with butter.

ingredients: 500 g (4 cups) all-purpose or bread flour
225 g (8 oz) pepperoni stick, cut into thin sticks or slices
115 g (1 cup) grated pepper jack or provolone (optional)
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, salt, milk and butter, knead 8 minutes until smooth, then cover and rise 1 hour until doubled.
Divide into 12 pieces, flatten each into a rectangle, lay pepperoni (and cheese, if using) down the middle, and roll up, pinching the seams closed.
Place seam-side down on a lined baking sheet, cover and rise 30 minutes.
Brush with egg and bake at 190°C (375°F) for 18–20 minutes until golden; the pepperoni oil soaks into the bread, as in the coal-miner lunches of north-central West Virginia.

ingredients: Chili: 225 g (8 oz) ground beef, 1 small onion minced, 120 ml (1/2 cup) tomato sauce, 1 tbsp chili powder, 1/2 tsp cumin, 120 ml (1/2 cup) water
Slaw: 300 g (3 cups) very finely chopped cabbage
115 g (1/2 cup) mayonnaise, 1 tbsp sugar and 1 tbsp cider vinegar
Yellow mustard and chopped raw onion
steps: For the slaw, mix the cabbage with mayonnaise, sugar, vinegar and a pinch of salt and chill.

For the chili, cook the beef and onion in a pan over medium heat, breaking it into fine crumbs, for 8 minutes until browned, then add the tomato sauce, spices and water and simmer 25–30 minutes until thick and saucy.
Grill or simmer the hot dogs until heated through, and warm the buns.
Assemble in West Virginia order: hot dog in bun, mustard, chili, onion, and a cold heap of slaw on top.

ingredients: 450 g (1 lb) extra-sharp cheddar, grated, at room temperature
180 ml (3/4 cup) flat lager beer, at room temperature
steps: Put the cheese, garlic, mustard, cayenne, hot sauce and salt in a food processor and pulse until finely crumbled.
With the motor running, pour in the beer gradually and process until smooth and spreadable.
Pack into a crock and refrigerate at least 2 hours, ideally overnight, to let the bite develop.
Serve cool with crackers, pretzels and celery sticks, as in the Kentucky River town of Winchester.

ingredients: 1/4 tsp salt and a pinch of cayenne
steps: Grate the cucumber and squeeze it firmly in a towel to remove as much liquid as possible.
Squeeze the grated onion likewise to keep just the pulp and juice.
Beat the cream cheese, mayonnaise, cucumber, onion, salt, cayenne and food colouring until smooth and pale green.
Chill 1 hour and serve on crustless tea sandwiches or with crackers, as invented by Louisville caterer Jennie Benedict.

ingredients: 2.7 kg (6 lb) mixed cooking apples, cored and quartered
400 g (2 cups) sugar or brown sugar
1/2 tsp ground cloves and 1/2 tsp allspice
steps: Simmer the apples with the cider in a heavy pot, covered, for 30–40 minutes until completely soft.
Pass through a food mill or blend to a smooth sauce and return it to the pot.
Stir in the sugar and spices and cook uncovered over very low heat, or in a 150°C (300°F) oven, for 3–4 hours, stirring often, until dark brown and thick enough to hold a mound on a spoon.
Stir in the lemon juice and spoon into sterilised jars; store in the fridge or process in a water bath, and serve on biscuits.

ingredients: 1.2 L (5 cups) water, 200 g (1 cup) brown sugar and 2 tsp cinnamon (for the filling)
1 tsp baking soda, 2 tsp baking powder and 1 tsp salt
115 g (1/2 cup) butter or vegetable shortening, softened
200 g (1 cup) sugar and 340 g (1 cup) sorghum syrup or molasses
steps: Simmer the dried apples in the water for 45 minutes until very soft, mash with the brown sugar and cinnamon, and cool to a thick filling.
Cream the butter and sugar, beat in the sorghum and eggs, then mix in the dry ingredients alternately with buttermilk to make a soft cookie-like dough.
Divide into 6–7 pieces, pat each into a 23 cm (9 in) round on parchment, and bake at 190°C (375°F) for 10–12 minutes until just firm.
Stack the cooled layers with a thick layer of apple filling between each, finishing with a plain layer.
Wrap and rest for 1–2 days so the layers soften, then slice thinly; traditionally neighbours each brought a layer to a wedding.

ingredients: 1 unbaked 23 cm (9 in) pie crust made with butter
60 ml (1/4 cup) buttermilk and 1 tbsp white vinegar
steps: Heat the oven to 175°C (350°F).
Whisk the butter and sugar, then beat in the eggs one at a time.
Whisk in the cornmeal, flour, buttermilk, vinegar, vanilla and salt until smooth.
Pour into the crust and bake 45–50 minutes until golden with a crackly top and just a slight jiggle in the centre.
Cool completely before slicing so the custard sets.

ingredients: 1 unbaked 23 cm (9 in) pie crust made with butter
1 tsp vanilla extract and 1/4 tsp ground nutmeg
steps: Heat the oven to 175°C (350°F).
Whisk the melted butter, sugar, flour and salt, then beat in the eggs, cream and vanilla until glossy.
Pour into the crust and grate nutmeg over the top.
Bake 45–50 minutes until the top is golden and the filling barely trembles in the middle.
Cool fully before slicing; it is a signature of Maysville, Kentucky, bakeries.

ingredients: 1 unbaked 23 cm (9 in) pie crust made with butter
1 tsp vanilla and 1/4 tsp ground nutmeg
steps: Heat the oven to 175°C (350°F).
Whisk the butter, sugar, flour and salt, then beat in the eggs, vinegar and vanilla until smooth.
Pour into the crust and dust with nutmeg.
Bake 45–50 minutes until set at the edges, golden on top and slightly wobbly in the centre; the vinegar gives a lemony tang from the days when fresh fruit was scarce.
Cool completely and serve with whipped cream.

ingredients: 1 unbaked 23 cm (9 in) pie crust made with butter
115 g (1/2 cup) butter, melted and cooled
2 tbsp Kentucky bourbon (optional) and 1 tsp vanilla
steps: Heat the oven to 175°C (350°F).
Beat the eggs and sugar, then stir in the melted butter, flour, bourbon and vanilla.
Fold in the chocolate chips and walnuts and pour into the crust.
Bake 40–45 minutes until golden and set with a slightly soft centre.
Cool 1 hour and serve warm with whipped cream, as on Kentucky Derby day.

ingredients: 115 g (1 cup) pecans, very finely chopped
steps: Soak the chopped pecans in the bourbon for at least 1 hour or overnight.
Beat the butter with the powdered sugar and bourbon-soaked pecans to a firm dough, roll into 2.5 cm (1 in) balls and chill 30 minutes until firm.
Melt the chocolate with the shortening over a pan of barely simmering water, stirring, for about 5 minutes until smooth.
Dip each ball in chocolate, set on parchment, press a pecan half on top and chill until set; these are a Frankfort, Kentucky, holiday candy for adults.

ingredients: 1/4 tsp salt and 1 tsp vanilla extract
steps: Combine the sugar, cream, butter, corn syrup and salt in a heavy saucepan and cook over medium heat, stirring gently, until it reaches 118°C (245°F), firm-ball stage, about 20 minutes.
Remove from the heat, stir in the vanilla and let cool for 5 minutes until slightly thickened.
Using a fork, dip each marshmallow in the caramel to coat completely, letting excess drip off, and set on buttered parchment.
Cool until firm, then wrap each in wax paper; this Louisville candy was named after actress Helena Modjeska.

ingredients: 480 ml (2 cups) pawpaw pulp, seeds and skin removed (substitute mashed ripe banana plus a little mango)
1 tsp baking powder and 1/4 tsp salt
steps: Heat the oven to 165°C (325°F) and butter a 20 x 20 cm (8 x 8 in) baking dish.
Whisk the pawpaw pulp, sugar, eggs, milk and melted butter until smooth.
Stir in the flour, baking powder, salt and spices to make a loose batter.
Bake 45–50 minutes until set and dark golden at the edges with a soft, custardy middle.
Serve warm with whipped cream; pawpaws are native to Appalachian river bottoms and ripen in September.

ingredients: 10 fresh spearmint leaves, plus a large sprig to garnish
75 ml (2 1/2 oz) Kentucky bourbon, bought from a licensed producer
steps: Gently press the mint leaves with the simple syrup in a chilled silver julep cup or old-fashioned glass to release their oils without shredding them.
Pack the cup with crushed ice, pour in the bourbon and stir until the outside of the cup frosts.
Top with more ice in a dome, tuck in a slapped mint sprig, dust with powdered sugar and serve with a short straw, as at Churchill Downs on Derby Day.

ingredients: 1 large onion, 1 green bell pepper and 3 celery ribs, diced (the "holy trinity")
2 l (8 cups) shrimp or seafood stock, hot
450 g (1 lb) Gulf shrimp, peeled and deveined
450 g (1 lb) blue crab claws or lump crabmeat
1 pint (about 450 g) shucked oysters with their liquor
200 g (7 oz) fresh okra, sliced (or 1 tsp filé powder at the table instead)
2 bay leaves, 1 tsp dried thyme, 1 tsp cayenne
2 tsp salt, plus hot sauce and sliced green onions to serve
steps: Make a dark roux: heat the oil in a heavy Dutch oven over medium heat, whisk in the flour and stir constantly for 30–45 minutes until it is the color of milk chocolate and smells nutty; do not let it scorch.
Add the trinity and cook 8 minutes, stirring, until soft, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Whisk in the hot stock a ladle at a time, add the okra, bay, thyme, cayenne and salt, and simmer uncovered for 1 hour, skimming the oil from the top.
Add the crab and simmer 10 minutes, then add the shrimp and the oysters with their liquor and cook 4–5 minutes until the shrimp are pink and the oyster edges curl.
Remove the bay leaves, adjust salt and serve over white rice with green onions, hot sauce and filé powder on the side.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.2 kg (2 1/2 lb) bone-in chicken thighs, skin removed
450 g (1 lb) smoked andouille sausage, sliced 1 cm (1/2 in) thick
1 large onion, 1 green bell pepper and 3 celery ribs, diced
1 tsp cayenne, 2 tsp Cajun seasoning, salt to taste
4 green onions and a handful of parsley, chopped
steps: Season the chicken with Cajun seasoning, brown it in 2 tbsp of the oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat, then brown the andouille and set both aside.
Add the remaining oil and flour and stir over medium heat for 40–50 minutes to a deep chocolate-brown roux.
Stir in the trinity for 8 minutes, then the garlic, then slowly whisk in the stock until smooth.
Return the chicken and sausage with the bay, thyme and cayenne and simmer gently, partly covered, for 1 1/2 hours until the chicken falls off the bone (at least 74°C / 165°F).
Pull the chicken from the bones, return the meat, skim the fat, stir in green onions and parsley, and serve over rice with filé and potato salad on the side, Cajun-style.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2.5 kg (5 1/2 lb) mixed greens: collards, mustard, turnip greens, spinach, cabbage, beet tops, watercress, parsley
450 g (1 lb) smoked hot sausage or andouille, sliced
450 g (1 lb) beef brisket or stew beef, cubed
80 ml (1/3 cup) vegetable oil and 45 g (1/3 cup) flour for a light roux
2 onions, diced, and 6 garlic cloves, minced
2 bay leaves, 1 tsp dried thyme, 1 tsp cayenne
2 tsp salt and 1 tsp filé powder
steps: Wash the greens well, simmer them in 4 l (4 quarts) water for 30 minutes, then lift out, chop finely (or pulse in a food processor) and save the green cooking liquid.
In a large pot brown the beef, ham and sausage in a little oil over medium-high heat; remove.
Make a light peanut-butter-colored roux with the oil and flour over medium heat (about 15 minutes), then add the onions and garlic and cook 5 minutes.
Whisk in 2 l (8 cups) of the greens liquid, add the meats, chopped greens, bay, thyme, cayenne and salt, and simmer 1 1/2 hours until the beef is tender.
Off the heat stir in the filé and serve over rice; this is the traditional Holy Thursday gumbo of New Orleans, made with an odd number of greens for luck.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 900 g (2 lb) farm-raised turtle meat, diced (substitute ground veal or beef chuck)
115 g (1/2 cup) butter and 65 g (1/2 cup) flour
1 onion, 1 green bell pepper and 2 celery ribs, finely diced
60 ml (1/4 cup) lemon juice and 2 tbsp Worcestershire sauce
120 ml (1/2 cup) dry sherry, plus more to serve
3 hard-boiled eggs, chopped, and 1 bunch spinach, chopped
1 tsp thyme, 2 bay leaves, 1 tsp cayenne, salt
steps: Brown the turtle meat in 2 tbsp of the butter in a heavy pot over medium-high heat; remove.
Melt the remaining butter, add the flour and stir over medium heat 10–12 minutes to a light brown roux, then add the vegetables and garlic and cook 6 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, stock, meat, Worcestershire, thyme, bay and cayenne and simmer 1 hour, stirring now and then, until the meat is tender.
Stir in the spinach, lemon juice, sherry and eggs, simmer 5 minutes and season with salt.
Serve in bowls with a small jug of dry sherry for each diner to add a splash, as at Commander's Palace.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 900 g (2 lb) Louisiana crawfish tails with their fat (substitute langoustine or shrimp)
115 g (1/2 cup) butter and 65 g (1/2 cup) flour
1 onion, 1 green bell pepper and 2 celery ribs, finely diced
60 g (1 cup) fresh breadcrumbs, 1 egg and 2 green onions, for stuffed heads (optional)
steps: Chop one third of the crawfish tails and mix with the breadcrumbs, egg and green onions; roll into small balls (traditionally stuffed into cleaned crawfish heads) and bake at 190°C (375°F) for 15 minutes.
Make a medium-brown roux with the butter and flour over medium heat (about 15 minutes), then add the trinity and garlic and cook 8 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste, whisk in the stock and simmer 30 minutes; blend half the soup smooth for body.
Add the remaining crawfish tails and their fat, the cream, cayenne and paprika and simmer 10 minutes without boiling hard.
Drop in the stuffed balls, warm through 5 minutes, season with salt and serve over a spoon of rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 680 g (1 1/2 lb) medium shrimp, peeled (shells kept for stock)
600 g (4 cups) fresh corn kernels, scraped with their milk (about 6 ears)
60 g (1/4 cup) butter and 30 g (1/4 cup) flour
1 onion, 1/2 green bell pepper and 2 celery ribs, diced
1.2 l (5 cups) shrimp stock made from the shells
1 tsp Cajun seasoning, salt, sliced green onions

steps: Brown the andouille and chicken in the oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat for 8 minutes.

steps: Season the meat with salt, cayenne and pepper and brown it hard in the lard in a cast-iron pot over medium-high heat for 15 minutes, letting a dark crust (fond) build on the bottom — this gives the "brown" Cajun color, with no tomato.

2 tbsp bacon fat or vegetable oil

2 tsp salt, and hot cooked white rice to serve

Add the beans, ham hock, water, bay, thyme and cayenne, bring to a boil and boil hard 10 minutes.
Lower the heat and simmer, partly covered, 2 1/2–3 hours, stirring occasionally, until the beans are very soft.
Mash about a cup of beans against the side of the pot and stir until the pot liquor turns creamy; pull the meat from the ham hock and return it, then salt to taste.
Serve over rice — the traditional New Orleans Monday wash-day supper — with hot sauce and French bread.

soft French bread, coleslaw and pickles, to serve

Cold-smoke-then-hot-smoke over pecan or sugarcane-wood smoke, holding the smoker at 70–80°C (160–175°F) for 5–6 hours until the internal temperature reaches 68°C (155°F) and the skins are dark mahogany.

steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, add the water, evaporated milk, egg and butter and knead 6 minutes to a soft dough.
Cover and let rise 2 hours until doubled.
Roll 6 mm (1/4 in) thick and cut into 6 cm (2 1/2 in) squares.
Fry at 180°C (360°F) for 1 minute per side until puffed and golden.
Drain and bury under powdered sugar; serve hot with café au lait, Café du Monde-style.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g (2 cups) cooked long-grain rice, cold
2 tsp baking powder and 1/4 tsp salt
powdered sugar or cane syrup, to serve
steps: Mash the rice lightly and beat in the eggs, sugar, vanilla and nutmeg.
Fold in the flour, baking powder and salt to a thick batter.
Drop tablespoons into oil at 180°C (350°F) and fry 2–3 minutes, turning, until deep golden and cooked through.
Drain and dust with powdered sugar — the Creole rice fritters once sold by street vendors crying "Belles calas, tout chauds!"
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 120 ml (1/2 cup) heavy cream or evaporated milk
steps: Line trays with parchment; combine sugars, cream, butter and salt in a heavy saucepan over medium heat and stir until dissolved.
Boil without stirring to the soft-ball stage, 116°C (240°F) on a candy thermometer.
Remove from heat, stir in the pecans and vanilla and beat 2–3 minutes until the mixture thickens and turns slightly cloudy.
Quickly drop spoonfuls onto the parchment to form 5 cm (2 in) patties and cool 20 minutes until set.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 ripe bananas, halved lengthwise and crosswise
steps: Melt the butter, brown sugar and cinnamon in a flambé pan or skillet over medium heat until bubbling, about 2 minutes.
Add the banana liqueur and bananas and cook 2 minutes per side until softened and glazed.
Off the flame add the rum, return to the heat and carefully ignite with a long lighter, spooning sauce until the flames die (keep back and away from anything flammable).
Serve immediately over vanilla ice cream, as invented at Brennan's in 1951.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 day-old New Orleans French bread loaf (about 450 g / 1 lb), torn
for sauce: 115 g (1/2 cup) butter, 200 g (1 cup) sugar, 1 egg, 60 ml (1/4 cup) bourbon
steps: Soak the bread in the milk 15 minutes, then beat in the eggs, sugar, vanilla, cinnamon and raisins.
Pour the butter into a 23x33 cm (9x13 in) dish, add the bread mixture and bake at 175°C (350°F) for 50–60 minutes until set and golden.
For the sauce, melt the butter and sugar in a saucepan over low heat, whisk a little into the beaten egg, return to the pan and whisk 2 minutes until thick and just below a simmer.
Off the heat stir in the bourbon and pour warm over squares of pudding.

ingredients: 100 g (1/2 cup) sugar and 1 tsp salt
180 ml (3/4 cup) warm milk and 2 eggs
1 tsp lemon zest and 1/2 tsp nutmeg
for filling: 110 g (1/2 cup) brown sugar, 2 tsp cinnamon, 60 g (1/4 cup) butter
for icing: 240 g (2 cups) powdered sugar, 3 tbsp milk, purple, green and gold sanding sugar
1 small plastic baby or a dried bean
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, salt, nutmeg and zest, add the milk, eggs and butter and knead 8 minutes to a soft, smooth dough; let rise 1 1/2 hours until doubled.
Roll into a 25x75 cm (10x30 in) rectangle, spread with soft butter and sprinkle with cinnamon sugar, roll up from the long side and join into an oval ring on a baking sheet.
Let rise 45 minutes, then bake at 175°C (350°F) for 25–30 minutes until golden; cool.
Tuck the baby (or bean) into the underside, drizzle with icing and sprinkle stripes of purple, green and gold sugar; whoever finds the baby hosts the next Carnival party.

ingredients: 340 g (2 3/4 cups) cake flour, 1 tbsp baking powder and 1/2 tsp salt
for chocolate custard: 1 l (4 cups) milk, 200 g (1 cup) sugar, 60 g (1/2 cup) cornstarch, 4 egg yolks, 170 g (6 oz) dark chocolate
for ganache: 340 g (12 oz) dark chocolate, 240 ml (1 cup) heavy cream
steps: Cream the butter and sugar 4 minutes until fluffy, beat in the eggs and vanilla, then fold in the dry ingredients alternately with the buttermilk.
Divide among three 23 cm (9 in) pans and bake at 175°C (350°F) for 22–25 minutes; cool and split each layer in half to make 6 thin layers.
For the custard whisk milk, sugar, cornstarch and yolks in a saucepan over medium heat until boiling and thick, then stir in chopped chocolate; chill 2 hours.
Stack the cake layers with custard between each, then chill 1 hour.
Heat the cream, pour over chopped chocolate, stir smooth and pour over the cake to cover; chill until set — Beulah Ledner's New Orleans adaptation of the Hungarian Dobos torte.

ingredients: 250 g (2 cups) flour, 1 tsp baking powder and a pinch of salt
720 ml (3 cups) whole milk for custard
150 g (3/4 cup) sugar and 45 g (1/3 cup) cornstarch
steps: Make the sweet-dough crust: cream the butter and sugar, beat in the egg and milk, then mix in the flour, baking powder and salt; chill 20 minutes.
For the bouillie (custard), whisk milk, sugar, cornstarch and yolks in a saucepan over medium heat until thick and bubbling, 8 minutes; stir in vanilla and cool slightly.
Press two thirds of the dough into a 23 cm (9 in) pie pan, pour in the custard and lattice the top with strips of the remaining dough.
Bake at 175°C (350°F) for 35–40 minutes until the crust is golden; cool completely before slicing — a Cajun farmhouse custard pie.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tsp flavoring extract (nectar, strawberry, wedding cake or spearmint) and food coloring
1 kg (8 cups) finely shaved ice (made in a block-ice shaver)
120 ml (1/2 cup) sweetened condensed milk (optional, "stuffed" or "cream" style)
steps: Boil the sugar and water 3 minutes until clear, cool and stir in the flavoring and coloring to make the syrup.
Shave block ice as fine and fluffy as snow — finer than a snow cone — into cups.
Pour the syrup slowly over the ice so it soaks through.
Top with condensed milk if you like; nectar cream, as at Hansen's Sno-Bliz, is the classic.

ingredients: 720 ml (3 cups) strong hot coffee, New Orleans chicory blend
60 ml (1/4 cup) orange liqueur (Grand Marnier or Cointreau)
peel of 1 orange and 1 lemon, in long strips
steps: Warm the brandy, orange liqueur, citrus peels, cinnamon, cloves and sugar in a brûlot bowl or saucepan over low heat until the sugar dissolves.
Carefully ignite with a long lighter and ladle the flaming liquor for 1 minute (keep hair and sleeves back).
Slowly pour in the hot coffee to extinguish the flames and stir.
Ladle into demitasse cups, as served tableside at Antoine's and Arnaud's.

ingredients: 60 ml (2 fl oz) rye whiskey (or cognac for the original style)
1 sugar cube or 1 tsp simple syrup
1 tsp absinthe or Herbsaint, for rinsing
steps: Chill an old-fashioned glass with ice, then discard the ice and swirl the absinthe to coat the inside, pouring out the excess.
In a mixing glass muddle the sugar with the bitters, add the rye and ice, and stir 30 seconds until cold.
Strain into the rinsed glass with no ice, express the lemon peel over the top and discard it; this is New Orleans' official cocktail, made with bought spirits.

ingredients: 60 ml (2 fl oz) London dry gin
15 ml (1/2 fl oz) each lemon juice and lime juice
1 fresh egg white (use pasteurized if preferred)
30 ml (1 fl oz) cold soda water
steps: Dry-shake the gin, citrus, syrup, cream, egg white and orange flower water without ice for 30 seconds.
Add ice and shake hard for at least 1–2 minutes until frothy and very cold.
Strain into a tall Collins glass, rest 1 minute, then slowly pour soda down the center so the foam rises above the rim — Henry Ramos' 1888 New Orleans fizz.
