ingredients: 60 ml (2 fl oz) passion fruit juice or syrup
1 orange slice and a maraschino cherry, to garnish
steps: Fill a cocktail shaker with ice and add both rums, the juices and grenadine.
Shake 15 seconds until cold.
Strain over fresh ice in a hurricane glass and garnish with orange and cherry, as at Pat O'Brien's.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 5.5–6.5 kg (12–14 lb) whole packer beef brisket (point and flat), USDA Choice or Prime
post oak wood splits or chunks (substitute hickory or other oak)
240 ml (1 cup) beef tallow or reserved fat, melted
white bread, sliced onions and pickles, to serve
steps: Trim the hard fat and leave a 6 mm (1/4 in) fat cap; mix salt and pepper (the Central Texas "Dalmatian rub") and coat all sides evenly, then rest 1 hour at room temperature.
Bring an offset smoker to 120–135°C (250–275°F) with clean post oak smoke and lay the brisket fat side up, point toward the firebox.
Smoke 6–8 hours, spritzing occasionally, until the bark is dark and set and the internal temperature reaches about 74°C (165°F).
Wrap tightly in butcher paper brushed with tallow and cook 3–4 hours more until a probe slides in like butter, about 95–98°C (203–208°F).

Rest wrapped in an insulated cooler for at least 1 hour, then slice across the grain about the width of a pencil and serve on butcher paper with white bread, onions and pickles, as at Franklin or Kreuz Market.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 rack beef plate short ribs (3 bones, IMPS 123A), about 2.3 kg (5 lb)
2 tbsp yellow mustard or hot sauce, as binder
120 ml (1/2 cup) water mixed with 120 ml (1/2 cup) apple cider vinegar, for spritzing
steps: Trim the loose surface fat and silverskin off the top of the rack, brush with the binder and coat heavily with salt, pepper and garlic.
Smoke bone side down at 120–135°C (250–275°F) over post oak for 8–9 hours, spritzing every hour after the first 3 hours.
Cook until the bark is black and crusty and a probe slides in with no resistance between bones, about 96–98°C (205–208°F).
Rest 30–45 minutes loosely tented, then slice between the bones — each "dino rib" serves one hungry person.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.8 kg (4 lb) beef chuck, cubed and well chilled
450 g (1 lb) pork fat or fatty pork shoulder, chilled
1 tsp Instacure No. 1 (pink curing salt) — measure exactly
1 tbsp cayenne and 1 tbsp crushed red chili flakes
4.5 m (15 ft) hog casings (32–35 mm), soaked
steps: Grind the beef and pork fat through a coarse 6 mm (1/4 in) plate while very cold.
Mix with salt, curing salt, spices and ice water for 2 minutes until tacky, then stuff into casings and twist into 20 cm (8 in) links.
Refrigerate uncovered overnight so the casings dry.
Smoke over post oak at 110–120°C (225–250°F) for 2–3 hours until the internal temperature reaches 68°C (155°F) and the casings snap.
Serve hot on butcher paper with saltine crackers, pickles and onions, as at Southside Market in Elgin, the Czech-German "hot guts" of Central Texas.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 900 g (2 lb) smoked brisket, including fatty point and bark
60 ml (1/4 cup) brisket drippings or beef stock
dill pickle chips and sliced white onion
steps: Chop the brisket finely on a board with a heavy knife, mixing lean, fat and bark.
Warm the barbecue sauce, drippings, Worcestershire and hot sauce in a skillet over medium heat for 3 minutes.
Add the chopped beef and stir 5–8 minutes until hot through and coated in sticky sauce.
Pile onto toasted buns and top with pickles and onions — the East Texas style sauced at the pit, unlike Central Texas.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 beef cube steaks (tenderized round), about 170 g (6 oz) each
2 tsp salt, 2 tsp black pepper, 1 tsp paprika, 1/2 tsp garlic powder
2 eggs beaten with 240 ml (1 cup) buttermilk
240 ml (1 cup) vegetable oil or lard, for shallow frying
3 tbsp of the flour and 600 ml (2 1/2 cups) whole milk, for gravy
1 tsp coarse black pepper, for gravy
mashed potatoes and green beans, to serve
steps: Season the flour; dredge each steak in flour, dip in the egg-buttermilk, then press firmly in flour again for a shaggy crust.
Heat the oil in a cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat to 175°C (350°F) and fry the steaks 3–4 minutes per side until deep golden and cooked through; drain and keep warm.
Pour off all but 3 tbsp fat, keeping the browned bits, whisk in 3 tbsp flour and cook 2 minutes.
Slowly whisk in the milk and simmer 4–5 minutes until thick, then season with salt and plenty of black pepper.
Smother the steaks with the white cream gravy and serve with mashed potatoes — a Texas diner staple from Lamesa to Dallas.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 680 g (1 1/2 lb) beef cube steak, cut in 2 cm (3/4 in) strips
1 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tsp black pepper, 1 tsp paprika
cream gravy, Texas toast and fries, to serve
steps: Whisk the buttermilk and egg; mix the flour with salt, pepper and paprika.
Dip the strips in flour, then buttermilk, then flour again.
Deep-fry at 175°C (350°F) for 3–4 minutes until golden and crisp; drain.
Serve with cream gravy for dipping, Texas toast and fries, as in Texas school cafeterias and Dairy Queens.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Chili con Carne (Texas Bowl of Red)

ingredients: 1.4 kg (3 lb) beef chuck, cut in 1 cm (1/2 in) cubes
6 dried ancho chiles and 4 dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded
2 dried chiles de árbol (optional, for heat)
3 tbsp beef tallow or vegetable oil
1 onion, finely chopped, and 6 garlic cloves, minced
1 tbsp ground cumin and 2 tsp Mexican oregano
2 tbsp masa harina mixed with 60 ml (1/4 cup) water
2 tsp salt and 1 tsp cider vinegar
steps: Toast the dried chiles in a dry skillet over medium heat 30 seconds per side, soak in hot water 20 minutes, then blend with 240 ml (1 cup) soaking water to a smooth paste.
Brown the beef in batches in the tallow in a Dutch oven over high heat; remove.
Cook the onion 5 minutes, add the garlic, cumin and oregano for 1 minute, then return the beef with the chile paste and stock.
Simmer gently, partly covered, 2 1/2–3 hours until the beef is tender.
Stir in the masa slurry, salt and vinegar and simmer 10 minutes to thicken; true Texas red has no beans or tomatoes — serve with saltines and chopped onion.

ingredients: 1 kg (2 1/4 lb) cooked chicken, shredded (rotisserie is fine)
1 onion and 1 green bell pepper, diced
285 g (10 oz) can diced tomatoes with green chiles (Ro-Tel)
300 g (10 1/2 oz) can each cream of chicken and cream of mushroom soup
1 tsp chili powder and 1 tsp ground cumin
225 g (2 cups) shredded Cheddar or Colby-Jack cheese
steps: Melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion and pepper 6 minutes until soft.
Stir in the Ro-Tel, soups, stock, chili powder and cumin and heat until smooth.
In a greased 23x33 cm (9x13 in) dish layer one third of the tortillas, half the chicken, a third of the sauce and a third of the cheese; repeat, then finish with tortillas, sauce and cheese.
Bake at 175°C (350°F) for 40–45 minutes until bubbling and golden, and rest 10 minutes before serving.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 450 g (1 lb) spaghetti, broken in thirds
1 onion and 1 green bell pepper, diced
285 g (10 oz) can Ro-Tel tomatoes with green chiles
300 g (10 1/2 oz) can cream of chicken soup
225 g (8 oz) Velveeta or American cheese, cubed
1 tsp chili powder, salt and pepper
steps: Cook the spaghetti in the chicken stock topped up with salted water until just tender; drain, saving 240 ml (1 cup) of the liquid.
Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion and pepper 6 minutes.
Add the Ro-Tel, soup, Velveeta, chili powder and reserved liquid and stir until the cheese melts smooth.
Fold in the chicken and spaghetti, spread in a 23x33 cm (9x13 in) dish, top with Cheddar and bake at 175°C (350°F) for 25–30 minutes until bubbly.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 900 g (2 lb) beef chuck, cubed (traditionally fresh calf: heart, tongue, sweetbreads, liver and marrow gut)
450 g (1 lb) beef heart and 225 g (8 oz) sweetbreads, cleaned and cubed (optional, or use more chuck)
2 onions, chopped, and 4 garlic cloves, minced
1.5 l (6 cups) beef stock or water
2 tsp salt, 1 tsp black pepper, 1 tsp chili powder
steps: Brown the chuck and heart in the tallow in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat in batches.
Add the onions, garlic and chiles and cook 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, stock and seasonings, cover and simmer 2 1/2 hours until tender.
Add the sweetbreads and liver for the last 20 minutes and cook until fully done; season and serve with sourdough biscuits — the old trail-drive chuckwagon stew made the day a calf was butchered.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 single-serve bags Fritos corn chips (about 30 g / 1 oz each), or 170 g (6 oz) from a large bag
700 ml (3 cups) hot Texas chili con carne, without beans
steps: Heat the chili in a saucepan over medium heat until bubbling.
Split each Fritos bag lengthwise along the side (or fill bowls with chips).
Ladle the hot chili over the chips and top with cheese, onion and jalapeños.
Eat with a plastic fork straight from the bag, as at Friday-night football games.

ingredients: 2 tbsp sugar, 2 tsp baking powder and 1 tsp salt
8 wooden skewers and yellow mustard, to serve
steps: Whisk the cornmeal, flour, sugar, baking powder and salt, then beat in the egg and buttermilk to a thick batter; pour into a tall glass.
Insert a skewer into each hot dog and dust lightly with flour.
Dip each dog into the batter to coat completely and fry at 175°C (350°F) for 3–4 minutes, turning, until deep golden.
Drain and serve with mustard, the Fletcher's way at the State Fair of Texas.

ingredients: 450 g (1 lb) dried pinto beans, soaked overnight
225 g (8 oz) bacon or salt pork, diced (or 450 g / 1 lb ground beef)
1 onion, chopped, and 4 garlic cloves, minced
4 dried ancho chiles, soaked and blended, or 3 tbsp chili powder
2 tsp ground cumin and 1 tsp Mexican oregano
1 tbsp cider vinegar and 1 tbsp brown sugar
2 l (8 cups) water or beef stock
steps: Brown the bacon in a Dutch oven over medium heat, add the onion and garlic and cook 5 minutes.
Add the drained beans, chile purée, tomatoes, cumin, oregano and water and bring to a boil.
Simmer, partly covered, 2 1/2–3 hours, stirring occasionally, until the beans are tender and the chili gravy is thick.
Stir in the vinegar, sugar and salt and simmer 10 minutes; serve alongside brisket or chicken-fried steak.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 cans (425 g / 15 oz each) black-eyed peas, drained and rinsed
1 red and 1 green bell pepper, diced
80 ml (1/3 cup) olive oil, 60 ml (1/4 cup) red wine vinegar and 1 tsp sugar
1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp black pepper
steps: Whisk the oil, vinegar, sugar, cumin, salt and pepper into a dressing.
Combine the peas, peppers, onion, jalapeños, corn, tomatoes and cilantro in a bowl.
Toss with the dressing and refrigerate at least 2 hours to marinate.
Serve cold with tortilla chips — Helen Corbitt's 1940s Neiman Marcus dip, traditional at New Year's.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 8 slices thick-cut white bread, about 2 cm (3/4 in) thick
2 garlic cloves, minced (or 1 tsp garlic powder)
steps: Beat the butter with garlic, parsley and salt.
Spread both sides of each slice with garlic butter.
Griddle in a skillet over medium heat 2–3 minutes per side until golden and crisp outside but soft inside (or broil 2 minutes per side).
Serve hot alongside chicken-fried steak, steak fingers or barbecue.

ingredients: 75 g (1/3 cup) vegetable shortening (lard is traditional)
steps: Mix the flour, baking powder, salt and sugar and rub in the shortening until crumbly.
Stir in the milk to a soft dough and knead briefly 1 minute.
Pat into a round about 1.5 cm (1/2 in) thick to fit a greased cast-iron skillet or Dutch oven.

Bake at 200°C (400°F) for 20–25 minutes (or in a Dutch oven over campfire coals) until golden; brush with butter and serve warm in wedges — the official state bread of Texas, from South Texas vaquero camps.

ingredients: 70 g (1/3 cup) sugar and 1 tsp salt
300 g (1 cup) fruit filling: apricot, prune, cherry or poppy seed (mák)
225 g (8 oz) cream cheese beaten with 50 g (1/4 cup) sugar and 1 tsp lemon zest (egg-free cheese filling)
posipka crumb: 30 g (1/4 cup) flour, 50 g (1/4 cup) sugar, 2 tbsp butter
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, add the milk and 85 g (6 tbsp) of the melted butter and knead 6 minutes to a soft, egg-free dough; let rise 1 hour until doubled.
Divide into 18 balls, set on a greased tray, brush with butter and rise 45 minutes.
Press a deep well in each with two fingers and fill with fruit or sweet cheese; rub the posipka ingredients together and sprinkle over.
Bake at 190°C (375°F) for 15–18 minutes until golden, then brush the edges with the remaining butter — the Czech pastry of West, Texas, and the Texas Czech belt.

ingredients: 50 g (1/4 cup) sugar and 1 tsp salt
8 smoked Czech-style sausages or kielbasa links, halved (16 pieces)
115 g (1 cup) shredded Cheddar and sliced jalapeños (optional)
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, add the milk, egg and 60 g (4 tbsp) butter and knead 6 minutes to a soft dough; let rise 1 hour.
Divide into 16 pieces, flatten each into an oval, place a sausage piece (with cheese and jalapeño if you like) on top and wrap and pinch the seam closed.
Set seam side down on a greased tray and rise 30 minutes.
Bake at 190°C (375°F) for 15–18 minutes until golden and brush with the remaining butter; Texans often call these "kolaches," though the Czech-Texan name is klobasníky.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tsp baking soda and 1/2 tsp salt
225 g (1 cup) butter plus 115 g (1/2 cup) for frosting
25 g (1/4 cup) cocoa powder plus 25 g (1/4 cup) for frosting
2 eggs, 120 ml (1/2 cup) buttermilk and 1 tsp vanilla
450 g (4 cups) powdered sugar and 80 ml (1/3 cup) milk, for frosting
120 g (1 cup) pecans, chopped and toasted
steps: Whisk the flour, sugar, soda and salt in a bowl; boil 225 g butter, 25 g cocoa and the water in a saucepan, then pour over the dry mix and stir.
Beat in the eggs, buttermilk and vanilla and pour into a greased 33x46 cm (13x18 in) sheet pan.
Bake at 175°C (350°F) for 18–20 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.
While it bakes, bring the frosting butter, cocoa and milk to a boil, whisk in the powdered sugar and pecans, and pour over the hot cake so it sets into a thin fudge layer; cool before cutting.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g (1/2 cup) sugar and 1/4 tsp salt
240 ml (1 cup) light corn syrup or cane syrup
60 g (1/4 cup) butter, melted, and 2 tsp vanilla
steps: Pulse the flour, sugar, salt and cold butter to crumbs, press into a parchment-lined 23x33 cm (9x13 in) pan and bake at 175°C (350°F) for 18–20 minutes until lightly golden.
Whisk the eggs, syrup, brown sugar, melted butter and vanilla, then stir in the pecans.
Pour over the hot crust and bake 25–30 minutes until the filling is set at the edges and barely jiggles in the center.
Cool completely, then chill 1 hour before cutting into bars — pecan is the Texas state tree.

ingredients: 450 g (1 lb) processed American cheese or Velveeta, cubed
115 g (4 oz / 1 cup) Monterey Jack, grated
1 can (285 g / 10 oz) diced tomatoes with green chiles (Ro-Tel style), undrained
60 ml (1/4 cup) milk, plus more to thin
steps: Melt the butter in a heavy saucepan over medium heat and soften the onion and jalapeño for 4–5 minutes until translucent; stir in the cumin for 30 seconds.
Turn the heat to low, add the processed cheese, milk and tomatoes with their juice, and stir constantly for 6–8 minutes until the cheese melts smoothly.
Stir in the Monterey Jack a handful at a time until glossy, adding a splash more milk if it is too thick to dip.
Keep warm in a small slow cooker or over very low heat and serve with tortilla chips; if you cannot find processed cheese, use all Jack plus 1 tsp cornstarch tossed through it to stop it splitting.

ingredients: 225 g (8 oz) sturdy corn tortilla chips, or 12 corn tortillas cut in quarters and fried
400 g (1 can / 15 oz) refried pinto beans, vegetarian
225 g (2 cups) longhorn Cheddar or Colby-Jack, grated
1 ripe avocado, mashed with lime and salt (guacamole)
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F) and warm the refried beans in a small pan with a splash of water until spreadable.

In the original Piedras Negras style, spread each chip with a little beans, top with cheese and a jalapeño ring, and arrange in one layer on a baking sheet; or layer chips, dollops of beans and cheese loosely for party nachos.
Dust lightly with chili powder and bake 6–8 minutes until the cheese is fully melted and bubbling at the edges.
Serve immediately topped with pico de gallo, sour cream and guacamole.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 450 g (1 can / 16 oz) refried beans, vegetarian
1 tbsp taco seasoning (chili powder, cumin, garlic, oregano)
3 ripe Hass avocados, mashed with 1 tbsp lime juice and salt
240 g (1 cup) mild tomato salsa, drained
170 g (1 1/2 cups) Cheddar or Mexican-blend cheese, grated
4 green onions, sliced, and 60 g (1/2 cup) sliced black olives
steps: Stir the taco seasoning into the refried beans and spread them evenly over the base of a 20 x 30 cm (8 x 12 in) glass dish.
Spread the guacamole over the beans to the edges to seal it, then a smooth layer of sour cream, then the drained salsa.
Scatter over the cheese, diced tomatoes, olives and green onions in even layers.
Cover and chill at least 30 minutes so the layers firm up, and serve cold with tortilla chips, scooping down through all seven layers.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 700 g (1 1/2 lb) beef skirt steak (arrachera), membrane trimmed
2 tbsp vegetable oil, plus 1 tbsp for the vegetables
1 tsp ground cumin, 1 tsp chili powder and 1 tsp salt
2 bell peppers and 1 large onion, sliced into strips
Pico de gallo, guacamole and sour cream, to serve
steps: Mix the lime juice, oil, garlic, cumin, chili powder, salt and Worcestershire, coat the skirt steak and marinate in the fridge for 2–4 hours (not longer, or the lime turns it mushy).
Heat a cast-iron skillet or charcoal grill until very hot; pat the steak dry and sear 3–4 minutes per side for medium (internal 57–63°C / 135–145°F).
Rest the beef 5 minutes, meanwhile cooking the peppers and onion in the remaining oil over high heat for 5–6 minutes until charred at the edges but still crisp.
Slice the steak thinly against the grain, pile onto the sizzling vegetables and serve straight from the pan with warm flour tortillas and the garnishes.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 700 g (1 1/2 lb) beef skirt or flank steak
3 tbsp lime juice and 2 tbsp orange juice
1 tsp ground cumin, 1 tsp dried Mexican oregano, 1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper
8 flour tortillas (or corn), warmed on the grill
1 small onion, finely chopped, and a handful of cilantro, chopped
Salsa roja and lime wedges, to serve
steps: Mix the citrus juices, oil, garlic and spices, rub over the steak and marinate in the fridge for 1–2 hours.
Light a charcoal grill (carbón means charcoal) and let it burn down to glowing coals with a light ash coating, or heat a grill pan until smoking.
Grill the beef 3–4 minutes per side until well charred outside and pink within, then rest 5 minutes and chop into small pieces.
Warm the tortillas on the edge of the grill for 20 seconds per side, fill with the beef, onion and cilantro, and serve with salsa and lime.

dishes.name: Tex-Mex Cheese Enchiladas with Chili Gravy

ingredients: 60 ml (1/4 cup) vegetable oil or lard, for softening
450 g (4 cups) mild yellow Cheddar or Longhorn Colby, grated
600 ml (2 1/2 cups) chili gravy (beef-fat roux gravy, see Chili Gravy recipe)
Shredded iceberg lettuce and diced tomato, to serve
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and warm the chili gravy in a saucepan; spread a ladle of it over the base of a baking dish.
Heat the oil in a small skillet over medium heat and dip each tortilla for 5–10 seconds per side just to soften, then drain on paper towels.
Fill each tortilla with a heap of cheese and a pinch of onion, roll tightly and lay seam-side down in the dish.
Pour the remaining gravy over, sprinkle with the rest of the cheese, onion and the cumin, and bake 15–20 minutes until bubbling and the cheese is melted.
Serve on hot plates, Texas café-style, with rice, refried beans, and a little lettuce and tomato on the side.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 ml (1 1/4 cups) warm water and 1/2 tsp salt
1 small onion and 2 garlic cloves, minced
2 tsp chili powder and 1 tsp ground cumin
1 medium potato, finely diced (optional, San Antonio style)
Vegetable oil, for deep frying (about 1 litre / 4 cups)
Shredded lettuce, diced tomato and grated Cheddar, to serve
steps: Brown the beef with the onion and garlic in a skillet over medium-high heat for 8 minutes, add the potato, chili powder, cumin and 120 ml (1/2 cup) water, and simmer 12 minutes until the potato is tender and the beef is cooked through.
Mix the masa harina, salt and warm water into a soft, play-dough-like dough, divide into 12 balls and keep covered.
Press each ball between plastic sheets in a tortilla press to about 3 mm (1/8 in) thick; do not cook them first.

Heat the oil to 190°C (375°F), slide in a raw tortilla; it puffs within seconds, so immediately press the center down with a spatula to form a U-shape and fry 40–60 seconds until golden and crisp, then drain.
Fill straight away with the beef picadillo, lettuce, tomato and cheese, and eat at once before they soften.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tbsp chili powder, 1 tsp ground cumin, 1/2 tsp paprika and 1 tsp salt
120 ml (1/2 cup) tomato sauce or water
12 corn tortillas, or ready-made taco shells
Shredded iceberg lettuce, diced tomato and grated Cheddar, to serve
steps: Brown the beef with the onion in a skillet over medium-high heat for 7–8 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains; spoon off excess fat.
Stir in the garlic and spices for 1 minute, add the tomato sauce and simmer 5 minutes until thick and saucy.
Heat 1 cm (1/2 in) oil to 180°C (350°F), fry each tortilla a few seconds until pliable, fold in half with tongs holding a gap, and fry each side 30–45 seconds until crisp; drain upside down.
Fill each shell with beef, then cheese, lettuce and tomato, and serve with hot sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 350 g (12 oz) cooked shredded chicken or seasoned ground beef
Salsa or pickled jalapeños, to serve
steps: Heat 1 cm (1/2 in) of oil to 180°C (350°F) and fry the flat tortillas 45–60 seconds per side until crisp and golden; drain.
Warm the refried beans with a splash of water and reheat the meat until steaming hot (at least 74°C / 165°F).
Spread each crisp tortilla with beans, top with meat and cheese, and broil 2–3 minutes until the cheese melts.
Pile on lettuce, tomato and a spoon of guacamole and serve flat, Texas style, with salsa.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.2 kg (2 1/2 lb) pork shoulder, in large chunks
6 dried ancho or guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded
4 garlic cloves and 1 tsp ground cumin
900 g (2 lb / about 7 cups) masa harina for tamales (or fresh masa preparada)
2 tsp baking powder and 2 tsp salt
1 litre (4 cups) warm pork cooking broth
40 dried corn husks (hojas), soaked in hot water 1 hour
steps: Simmer the pork in salted water for 2 hours until fork-tender; reserve the broth and shred the meat.
Soak the chiles in hot water 20 minutes, blend with garlic, cumin and 240 ml (1 cup) broth until smooth, then simmer with the pork for 10 minutes until thick.
Beat the lard until fluffy, then beat in the masa harina, baking powder, salt and enough warm broth to make a soft dough; a small ball should float in water.
Spread 2–3 tbsp masa thinly over the wide half of each drained husk, add 1 tbsp pork filling, roll up and fold the narrow end under.
Stand the tamales upright in a steamer over simmering water, cover with extra husks and steam 75–90 minutes until the masa pulls cleanly away from the husk.
Rest 10 minutes before serving, traditionally at Christmas by the dozen with chile con queso or salsa.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.1 kg (2 1/2 lb) beef chuck, in 2 cm (3/4 in) cubes
1 onion and 1 green bell pepper, diced
1 tomato, chopped, or 120 ml (1/2 cup) tomato sauce
1 tbsp chili powder, 2 tsp ground cumin and 1 tsp salt
steps: Season the beef with salt and brown it in batches in the hot oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat, 5 minutes per batch.
Add the onion, pepper and jalapeño and cook 5 minutes, then stir in the garlic, spices and flour and cook 2 minutes to toast the flour.
Stir in the tomato and broth, scraping up the browned bits, bring to a boil then cover and simmer on low for 1 3/4–2 hours until the beef is very tender and the gravy coats a spoon.
Adjust the salt and serve ladled into warm flour tortillas, or with rice and refried beans.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2.3 kg (5 lb) beef cheeks (cachete), trimmed (or beef chuck as substitute)
2 tsp ground cumin and 1 tbsp kosher salt
Corn tortillas, chopped onion, cilantro and salsa verde, to serve
steps: Rub the beef cheeks all over with salt, pepper and cumin.
Place in a heavy Dutch oven or slow cooker with the garlic, onion, bay leaves and water, wrap tightly (traditionally in maguey leaves in a pit) and cover.
Cook at 135°C (275°F) in the oven, or on low in a slow cooker, for 7–8 hours until the meat falls apart and the connective tissue has melted.
Shred the meat and moisten it with some of the rendered juices, then serve Sunday-morning style in warm corn tortillas with onion, cilantro and salsa.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tbsp chili powder, 1 tsp ground cumin and 1 tsp salt
1 head iceberg or romaine lettuce, shredded
400 g (1 can / 15 oz) pinto or kidney beans, drained
4 large flour tortillas, for shell bowls (or 2 cups crushed tortilla chips)
120 ml (1/2 cup) salsa and 120 ml (1/2 cup) sour cream
steps: Brown the beef in a skillet over medium-high heat for 8 minutes until cooked through, drain the fat, then add the spices and 60 ml (1/4 cup) water and simmer 3 minutes.
For bowls, press each flour tortilla into an oven-safe bowl and bake at 190°C (375°F) for 10–12 minutes until crisp and golden.
Fill the bowls with lettuce, beans and tomato, then top with warm beef and cheese.
Finish with salsa and sour cream and serve straight away.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 dried pasilla or ancho chiles, toasted and seeded
8 corn tortillas, cut in strips and fried crisp
1 avocado, Monterey Jack, sour cream and lime wedges, to serve
steps: Fry the onion and garlic in oil for 5 minutes until soft, then blend with the tomatoes, chiles and 240 ml (1 cup) broth until smooth.
Return the purée to the pot and fry it over medium heat for 5 minutes until darkened, then add the remaining broth, cumin and chicken.
Simmer 20–25 minutes until the chicken is cooked through (74°C / 165°F), then lift it out, shred it and return to the pot; season with salt.
Put crisp tortilla strips in each bowl, ladle over the hot soup and top with avocado, cheese, sour cream and a squeeze of lime.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 6 large eggs, beaten with a pinch of salt
225 g (8 oz) Mexican chorizo or bacon
Salsa roja or salsa verde, to serve
steps: Fry the potatoes in oil over medium heat for 12–15 minutes, covered for the first half, until tender and browned.
Cook the chorizo (casing removed) in a separate skillet for 6–7 minutes until fully cooked and crumbly, or fry the bacon crisp and chop.
Scramble the eggs in the chorizo fat over low heat until just set.
Warm the tortillas on a dry comal, fill with eggs, potato and chorizo or bacon, top with cheese and serve wrapped in foil with salsa, Austin and San Antonio style.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 450 g (2 cups) cooked pinto beans, with some liquid
2 tbsp vegetable oil or butter (no lard, to keep it vegetarian)
1/2 tsp ground cumin and salt to taste
115 g (1 cup) Cheddar or Monterey Jack, grated
steps: Soften the onion in the oil over medium heat for 4 minutes, then add the beans and cumin.
Mash the beans in the pan with a potato masher, adding bean liquid, and cook 6–8 minutes until thick, creamy refried beans; season.
Warm the tortillas on a dry hot comal for 20–30 seconds per side.
Spread each with a thick layer of beans, sprinkle with cheese so it melts, fold and serve with salsa.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 6 corn tortillas, cut into strips (or 2 cups stale tortilla chips)
8 large eggs, beaten with 1/2 tsp salt
85 g (3/4 cup) Monterey Jack or Cheddar, grated
Flour tortillas and salsa, to serve
steps: Fry the tortilla strips in the oil over medium-high heat for 3–4 minutes until crisp at the edges; drain on paper towels, leaving 1 tbsp oil.
Sauté the onion and jalapeño in the pan for 3 minutes, add the tomato for 1 minute, then return the tortilla strips.
Pour in the eggs, reduce the heat to medium-low and stir gently for 2–3 minutes until softly set.
Fold in the cheese, and serve with refried beans, warm flour tortillas and salsa.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 450 g (1 lb / 2 1/3 cups) dried pinto beans, soaked overnight
115 g (4 oz) Mexican chorizo or ham, diced (optional)
1 tsp ground cumin and salt to taste
steps: Drain the soaked beans, cover with 2 litres (8 cups) fresh water and simmer gently for 1 1/2–2 hours until tender.
Meanwhile, fry the bacon (and chorizo) in a skillet over medium heat for 8 minutes until the fat renders and the meat is cooked.
Add the onion, garlic, chiles and tomato to the fat and cook 5 minutes until soft.
Stir the mixture into the beans with the cumin, simmer 20 minutes more uncovered, season with salt and stir in the cilantro; serve brothy in bowls alongside barbecue or fajitas.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 450 g (1 lb) dried pinto beans, soaked overnight
60 g (1/4 cup) lard or bacon drippings
60 g (1/2 cup) Monterey Jack or queso fresco, to garnish
steps: Drain the beans and simmer them with the onion half and garlic in 2 litres (8 cups) water for 1 1/2–2 hours until very soft, salting in the last 30 minutes; reserve the liquid.
Heat the lard in a wide heavy skillet over medium heat until shimmering.
Add the beans in ladlefuls with a little liquid and mash vigorously with a potato masher, stirring for 10–15 minutes until thick and creamy; add cumin and salt.
Serve topped with cheese, the standard side for enchilada and combination plates.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tsp ground cumin and 1 tsp salt
steps: Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat and fry the dry rice, stirring, for 6–8 minutes until it turns golden and smells toasty.
Add the onion and garlic and cook 2 minutes, then stir in the tomato sauce, broth, cumin, salt and bouillon.
Bring to a boil, cover tightly, reduce heat to low and cook 20 minutes without lifting the lid.
Rest off the heat 5 minutes, fluff with a fork and serve with enchiladas or fajitas.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 60 g (1/4 cup) beef tallow, lard or vegetable oil
1 tsp garlic powder and 1/2 tsp dried oregano
600 ml (2 1/2 cups) beef or chicken broth
steps: Melt the fat in a saucepan over medium heat, whisk in the flour and cook 2–3 minutes to a light brown roux.
Whisk in the chili powder, cumin, garlic powder and oregano for 30 seconds until fragrant, without letting them scorch.
Slowly whisk in the broth until smooth, bring to a simmer and cook 10–15 minutes until thick enough to coat a spoon.
Season with salt and use hot over Tex-Mex cheese enchiladas, tamales or chili-topped plates.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 180 ml (6 fl oz / 3/4 cup) blanco tequila (bought, from licensed producers)
90 ml (3 fl oz) orange liqueur (triple sec or Cointreau)
120 ml (4 fl oz / 1/2 cup) fresh lime juice
60 ml (2 fl oz / 1/4 cup) simple syrup or agave syrup
Coarse salt and lime wedges, for the rims
steps: Rub the rims of four glasses with lime and dip in coarse salt.
Blend the tequila, orange liqueur, lime juice, syrup and ice on high for 30–45 seconds until smooth and slushy.

Taste and add more syrup or lime to balance, then pour into the glasses and garnish with lime; this Dallas-born slushy is served alongside Tex-Mex plates and should be enjoyed responsibly by adults only.

ingredients: 1 loaf Cuban bread (about 60 cm / 24 in), or a soft Italian loaf
450 g (1 lb) mojo-marinated roast pork (lechón asado), thinly sliced
225 g (8 oz) sweet glazed ham, thinly sliced
115 g (4 oz) Genoa salami, sliced (Tampa style, optional)
steps: Cut the bread into four lengths and split each horizontally; spread the insides with mustard.
Layer ham, roast pork, salami if using (as in Tampa), Swiss cheese and pickles, then close the sandwiches.
Butter the outsides and press in a sandwich press (plancha) or a heavy skillet weighted with another pan over medium heat for 3–4 minutes per side.
Cook until the bread is flat and crackly and the cheese has melted, then cut diagonally and serve hot.

ingredients: 225 g (8 oz) ground pork or fresh Spanish chorizo
1 tsp sweet paprika and 1/2 tsp ground cumin
2 garlic cloves, grated, and 1 tbsp grated onion
4 Cuban rolls or soft hamburger buns
2 large potatoes, cut in very fine shoestrings and fried (papitas), or canned potato sticks
75 g (1/2 cup) diced onion and 120 ml (1/2 cup) ketchup-based sauce
steps: Mix the meats with paprika, cumin, garlic, onion, salt and breadcrumbs and shape into 4 thin patties a little wider than the buns.
Cook on a very hot griddle over medium-high heat for 3–4 minutes per side until fully cooked (71°C / 160°F) and well crusted.
Toast the buns on the griddle, spread with the ketchup sauce, add the patty and the diced onion.
Pile on a generous handful of crisp shoestring potatoes and serve at once, Little Havana style.

ingredients: 1 long dried palmetto frond strip, or kitchen string, soaked (for the seam)
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, salt, lard and water and knead 8–10 minutes until smooth and elastic; cover and let rise 1 hour until doubled.
Divide into two, shape each into a long log about 60 cm (24 in) and place on a baking sheet dusted with cornmeal.
Lay a damp palmetto leaf (or string) along the top of each loaf to create the signature split, then let rise 45–60 minutes.
Bake at 200°C (400°F) with a pan of hot water on the lower shelf for 20–25 minutes until golden and hollow-sounding; remove the leaf and cool before slicing for Cubanos.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 450 g (1 lb) blue crab meat, picked over
1 onion, 1 green bell pepper and 3 garlic cloves, finely chopped
2 tbsp tomato paste loosened with 60 ml (1/4 cup) water
1 tsp hot pepper flakes or minced datil pepper, and 1 tsp salt
600 g (5 cups) stale Cuban bread, soaked in water and squeezed
2 large eggs, beaten with 2 tbsp milk (egg wash)
steps: Fry the onion, pepper and garlic in olive oil for 6 minutes, stir in the tomato paste, chili and salt, cook 3 minutes, then fold in the crab and cook 5 minutes; cool.
Knead the squeezed bread into a smooth dough with a pinch of salt and paprika.
Flatten a handful of dough in your palm, place 2 tbsp crab filling in the center and wrap into a torpedo-shaped croquette.
Dip in egg wash then breadcrumbs, and deep fry at 180°C (350°F) for 4–5 minutes until deep golden and hot through.
Drain and serve with hot sauce and a squeeze of lime, as in Ybor City.

ingredients: 1.4 kg (3 lb) cooked, chilled Florida stone crab claws (always sold pre-cooked)
1 tbsp dry mustard powder (or 1 tbsp Dijon)
2 tsp Worcestershire sauce and 1 tsp A1-style steak sauce
Lemon wedges and melted butter, to serve
steps: Stone crab claws are cooked at the dock right after harvest; keep them refrigerated and serve cold within 2 days (season mid-October to May).
Whisk the mustard, mayonnaise, Worcestershire, steak sauce and cream into a smooth mustard sauce and chill.
Crack each claw by wrapping it in a towel and tapping the shell sharply with the back of a heavy spoon at the knuckle and claw middle, leaving the black tip intact as a handle.
Serve on ice with the mustard sauce, melted butter and lemon wedges, with hash browns or coleslaw on the side.

ingredients: 4 grouper fillets, 170 g (6 oz) each (or snapper/mahi-mahi as substitute)
120 g (1 cup) all-purpose flour seasoned with 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp paprika and 1/2 tsp cayenne
2 large eggs, beaten with 60 ml (1/4 cup) milk
4 soft Kaiser rolls or brioche buns
steps: Pat the fillets dry, dredge in seasoned flour, dip in egg and press into the panko.
Heat 1.5 cm (1/2 in) oil to 180°C (350°F) and fry the fish 3–4 minutes per side until golden and flaky (63°C / 145°F inside).
Toast the buns and spread with tartar sauce.
Add lettuce, tomato and the hot grouper, and serve with fries and coleslaw, Gulf Coast style; the fillets may also be grilled or blackened.

ingredients: 680 g (1 1/2 lb) rock shrimp, peeled and deveined (Cape Canaveral catch; small shrimp as substitute)
1 tsp salt, 1 tsp Old Bay or Cajun seasoning and 1/2 tsp black pepper
Cocktail sauce and lemon wedges, to serve
steps: Soak the rock shrimp in buttermilk for 10 minutes.
Mix the flour, cornmeal and seasonings, then lift the shrimp out of the buttermilk and toss well in the coating.
Deep fry in batches at 185°C (365°F) for 1 1/2–2 minutes until golden and just opaque inside; they turn rubbery if overcooked.
Drain, salt lightly and serve hot with cocktail sauce and lemon.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 fresh striped mullet fillets, skin on, about 170 g (6 oz) each
1 1/2 tsp salt and 1 tsp black pepper
Vegetable oil or lard, for frying
Lemon wedges, hushpuppies and grits, to serve
steps: Mullet must be very fresh; trim away the dark bloodline for milder flavor, score the skin lightly and pat dry.
Mix the cornmeal, flour and seasonings and press the fillets firmly into the mixture.
Fry in 2 cm (3/4 in) oil at 180°C (350°F) for 3–4 minutes per side until crisp and the flesh flakes (63°C / 145°F).
Drain and serve, Panhandle fish-camp style, with lemon, grits, coleslaw and hushpuppies.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 900 g (2 lb) frog legs (about 12 pairs), from a seafood supplier
1 tsp salt, 1 tsp garlic powder, 1 tsp paprika and 1/2 tsp cayenne
Peanut or vegetable oil, for deep frying
Lemon wedges and tartar sauce, to serve
steps: Separate the legs into singles, then soak in buttermilk with hot sauce in the fridge for 1 hour.
Combine the flour with the seasonings and dredge the legs, shaking off excess.
Deep fry at 175°C (350°F) for 5–7 minutes until golden and the meat is white and pulls from the bone (63°C / 145°F); fry in batches.
Drain and serve hot, Lake Okeechobee style, with lemon and tartar sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 450 g (1 lb) conch meat, cleaned and ground (frozen imported; chopped clams or calamari as substitute)
1 large egg and 180 ml (3/4 cup) milk
1/2 onion, 1/2 green bell pepper and 1 celery stalk, finely diced
1 Scotch bonnet or 2 datil peppers, minced
1 tsp salt and 1 tsp Old Bay
Key lime aioli or cocktail sauce, to serve
steps: Tenderize the conch by pounding or grinding it, then chop fine.
Whisk the egg and milk, stir in the flour, baking powder and seasonings, then fold in the conch and vegetables to make a thick batter.
Drop tablespoons of batter into oil at 180°C (350°F) and fry 3–4 minutes, turning, until deep golden and cooked through.
Drain and serve hot, Key West style, with key lime aioli (mayonnaise, key lime juice and garlic).
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 680 g (1 1/2 lb) farm-raised alligator tail meat, in 2.5 cm (1 in) cubes
150 g (1 1/4 cups) all-purpose flour and 30 g (1/4 cup) cornmeal
2 tsp Cajun seasoning and 1 tsp salt
Datil pepper sauce or remoulade, to serve
steps: Trim any sinew from the alligator and soak the cubes in buttermilk and hot sauce in the fridge for 2 hours to tenderize.
Mix the flour, cornmeal, Cajun seasoning and salt; drain the meat and toss to coat.
Fry in oil at 180°C (350°F) for 3–4 minutes until golden and cooked through (71°C / 160°F); do not overcook or it gets chewy.
Drain and serve hot with remoulade or datil pepper sauce and lemon wedges.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 450 g (1 lb) smoked mullet, kingfish or mahi-mahi, skin and bones removed
1 tbsp lemon or key lime juice
1 tsp Worcestershire sauce and a few dashes hot sauce
2 green onions and 1 celery stalk, finely chopped
Saltine crackers, jalapeño slices and lemon, to serve
steps: Flake the smoked fish carefully with a fork, checking for pin bones.
Beat the cream cheese, mayonnaise and sour cream until smooth, then add the lime juice, Worcestershire and hot sauce.
Fold in the fish, green onions and celery, keeping some texture; season with black pepper.
Chill at least 1 hour and serve with saltines, pickled jalapeños and lemon wedges, as at Gulf Coast fish shacks.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 450 g (1 lb) conch meat, cleaned and ground or finely chopped (clams as substitute)
1 onion, 1 green bell pepper and 2 celery stalks, diced
1 can (400 g / 14 oz) crushed tomatoes and 2 tbsp tomato paste
1.2 litres (5 cups) fish or clam stock
1 whole Scotch bonnet pepper and 2 bay leaves
1 tsp dried thyme and 1 tbsp key lime juice
steps: Cook the bacon in a large pot over medium heat for 6 minutes until crisp, then sauté the onion, pepper, celery and garlic in the fat for 6 minutes.
Add the conch, tomato paste and tomatoes, stir 2 minutes, then pour in the stock with the bay, thyme and whole Scotch bonnet.
Simmer gently, partly covered, for 45 minutes until the conch is tender, then add the potatoes and cook 20 minutes more.
Remove the bay leaves and chili, season with salt, stir in the lime juice and serve Key West style with a dash of sherry pepper sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 900 g (2 lb) fresh clams, scrubbed, or 2 cans (185 g / 6.5 oz each) chopped clams with juice
115 g (4 oz) salt pork or bacon, diced
1 onion, 1 green bell pepper and 2 celery stalks, diced
2–3 datil peppers, minced (or 1 habanero as substitute)
1 tsp dried thyme, 2 bay leaves and salt
960 ml (4 cups) clam juice or water
steps: If using fresh clams, steam them in 480 ml (2 cups) water for 6–8 minutes until opened, discard any that stay closed, chop the meat and strain the liquid.
Render the salt pork in a pot over medium heat for 6 minutes, then sauté the onion, pepper, celery, garlic and datil for 6 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, clam liquid, thyme and bay, and simmer 25 minutes until the base is rich and red.
Add the potatoes and cook 15 minutes until tender, then stir in the clams and simmer 3 minutes; season and serve this spicy St. Augustine chowder with crackers.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 450 g (1 lb) dried garbanzo beans (chickpeas), soaked overnight
1 ham hock and 1.5 litres (6 cups) water
225 g (8 oz) cured Spanish chorizo, sliced
1 tbsp olive oil and 1 onion, chopped
1 green bell pepper, chopped, and 3 garlic cloves, minced
1/2 tsp saffron threads and 1 tsp sweet paprika
steps: Drain the chickpeas and simmer with the ham hock in the water for 1 hour, skimming the foam.
Fry the chorizo, onion, pepper and garlic in olive oil over medium heat for 8 minutes, then add the paprika and crumbled saffron.
Add this sofrito and the potatoes to the soup and simmer 30–40 minutes until the chickpeas and potatoes are very tender.
Pull the meat from the ham hock, return it to the pot, season, and serve with Cuban bread, as in Tampa's Ybor City.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 115 g (4 oz) baked ham, cut in julienne strips
115 g (4 oz) Swiss cheese, cut in julienne strips
60 g (1/2 cup) pimiento-stuffed green olives, sliced
4 garlic cloves, minced, 2 tsp dried oregano, 1 tbsp Worcestershire and 2 tbsp lemon juice
120 ml (1/2 cup) Spanish olive oil and 60 ml (1/4 cup) white wine vinegar
steps: Whisk the garlic, oregano, Worcestershire, lemon juice and vinegar, then slowly whisk in the olive oil; season with salt and pepper.
Combine the lettuce, tomato, ham, Swiss cheese and olives in a large bowl.
Pour the dressing over and toss well, ideally tableside.
Finish with the grated Romano and serve at once, the way Tampa's oldest Spanish restaurant made it famous.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 900 g (2 lb) sabal palm hearts (swamp cabbage), sliced; or canned hearts of palm as substitute
115 g (4 oz) salt pork or bacon, diced
1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper
steps: Fresh sabal palm heart should be bought from licensed growers (harvesting on public land is restricted); canned hearts of palm work well.
Render the salt pork in a heavy pot over medium heat for 8 minutes until crisp, then add the onion and cook 5 minutes.
Add the palm heart, tomatoes, water, salt, pepper and sugar and simmer covered for 45 minutes (20 minutes if canned) until tender.
Serve as a side to fried fish or barbecue, as at the LaBelle Swamp Cabbage Festival.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 8–10 fresh datil peppers, stemmed and minced (or habanero as substitute)
steps: Wear gloves to handle the datils, St. Augustine's signature Minorcan pepper, and soften them with the onion in the oil over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Add the tomato paste, ketchup, vinegar, sugar and salt with 120 ml (1/2 cup) water and simmer 20 minutes, stirring, until thick.
Blend smooth if you like, bottle in sterilized jars, cool and refrigerate up to 1 month; use on fried shrimp, chowder and gator bites.

ingredients: 1 can (397 g / 14 oz) sweetened condensed milk
120 ml (1/2 cup) key lime juice (fresh or bottled; Persian lime as substitute)
240 ml (1 cup) heavy cream, whipped with 2 tbsp sugar
steps: Heat the oven to 175°C (350°F); mix the crumbs, butter and sugar, press into a 23 cm (9 in) pie plate and bake 10 minutes.
Whisk the egg yolks and zest until pale, whisk in the condensed milk, then the key lime juice until it thickens slightly.
Pour into the crust and bake 15 minutes until set at the edges but slightly wobbly in the center.
Cool, chill at least 3 hours, and serve cold topped with whipped cream (or meringue, Key West style).

ingredients: 30 g (4 tbsp) dark-roast Cuban-style espresso, finely ground
steps: Fill a stovetop moka pot (cafetera) with water and coffee and set over medium heat.
Put the sugar in a small pitcher; as soon as the first few drops of coffee emerge, pour them onto the sugar and beat vigorously for 1–2 minutes into a thick pale paste.
When the pot finishes brewing, pour the rest of the coffee slowly into the sugar paste and stir to make the creamy foam (espumita).
Serve in tiny demitasse cups, Miami ventanita style; add steamed milk to make a cortadito.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 450 g (1 lb) jumbo lump blue crab meat, picked over for shell
2 tbsp butter, melted, and lemon wedges
steps: Whisk the egg, mayonnaise, mustard, Worcestershire, Old Bay and parsley, then fold in the crushed crackers.
Gently fold in the crab without breaking up the lumps, shape into 4 tall cakes and chill 1 hour to firm.
Heat the oven broiler, place the cakes on a buttered tray and brush with melted butter.
Broil 6 inches (15 cm) from the heat for 10–12 minutes until golden on top and hot through (or pan-fry in butter 4 minutes per side); serve with lemon, saltines and tartar or cocktail sauce.

dishes.name: Steamed Blue Crabs with Old Bay

ingredients: 24 live Chesapeake blue crabs (about 1 bushel-quarter / 3–4 kg)
120 g (1/2 cup) Old Bay or J.O. crab seasoning
360 ml (1 1/2 cups) water or lager beer
Melted butter, extra cider vinegar and Old Bay, to serve
steps: Use only crabs that are alive and lively; discard any dead ones.
Bring the vinegar and water (or beer) to a boil in a large steamer pot with a rack set above the liquid.
Layer the crabs on the rack, sprinkling each layer heavily with Old Bay and salt; cover tightly and steam 20–25 minutes until the shells are bright red-orange all over.
Dump onto a newspaper-covered table and serve with wooden mallets, knives, melted butter and vinegar for picking, alongside corn on the cob and cold drinks.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 450 g (1 lb) lump blue crab meat
1 tsp Dijon mustard and 1 tsp lemon juice
1 tsp Worcestershire sauce and 1 tsp Old Bay
2 tbsp finely diced red bell pepper (pimiento) and 1 tbsp parsley
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F).
Whisk half the mayonnaise with the yolk, mustard, lemon, Worcestershire, Old Bay, pepper and parsley, then gently fold in the crab.
Divide among 4 buttered ramekins or cleaned crab shells, spread the remaining mayonnaise thinly on top and dust with paprika.
Bake 15–20 minutes until bubbling and golden-brown on top, finishing under the broiler for 1–2 minutes if needed, and serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 live soft-shell blue crabs (in season May–August), cleaned
1 tsp Old Bay and 1/2 tsp salt
240 ml (1 cup) milk, with 1 egg beaten in
4 slices soft white bread or soft rolls, toasted
steps: Clean each crab by snipping off the face, removing the gills under each side of the top shell and pulling off the apron; pat dry.
Dip the crabs in the egg-milk, then dredge in the seasoned flour.
Pan-fry in 1 cm (1/2 in) oil at 180°C (350°F) shell-side down for 3 minutes per side until crisp and red-orange (they will spatter, so use a splatter guard).
Serve whole, legs and all, on toasted bread with tartar sauce, lettuce and tomato.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 450 g (1 lb) backfin or claw blue crab meat
1 tbsp lemon juice and 1 tsp Worcestershire sauce
2 tsp Old Bay, plus extra for the top
Crackers or a toasted bread round, to serve
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F).
Beat the cream cheese, sour cream, mayonnaise, lemon, Worcestershire and Old Bay until smooth, then fold in half the Cheddar and the crab.
Spread in a baking dish, top with the rest of the Cheddar and a dusting of Old Bay.
Bake 20–25 minutes until bubbling and golden, and serve hot with crackers or in a hollowed-out bread round.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.5 litres (6 cups) beef or crab stock
450 g (1 lb / 4 cups) mixed vegetables: corn, green beans, lima beans, peas, carrots
450 g (1 lb) claw or backfin blue crab meat
2 cleaned crab bodies or claws (optional, for flavor)
steps: Bring the stock, tomatoes, onion, celery and Old Bay to a boil in a large pot.
Add the potatoes and mixed vegetables (and crab bodies), and simmer 35–40 minutes until all the vegetables are tender.
Stir in the crab meat and simmer 10 minutes; season with more Old Bay and salt.
Serve this tomato-based "vegetable crab soup" hot with saltines.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 1/2 tsp Old Bay and 1/2 tsp salt
450 g (1 lb) lump blue crab meat
2 tbsp dry sherry, plus extra to serve
steps: Melt the butter in a heavy pot over medium heat and soften the onion for 4 minutes without coloring.
Whisk in the flour for 2 minutes, then slowly whisk in the milk and cream; simmer gently 10–12 minutes, stirring, until thickened.
Season with Old Bay and salt, fold in the crab and sherry, and heat through 5 minutes without boiling.
Serve with a splash of sherry at the table; a half-and-half bowl with Maryland crab soup is a Baltimore favorite.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 24 shucked Chesapeake oysters with their liquor (about 480 ml / 2 cups)
2 celery stalks, finely diced, and 1 shallot, minced
1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp white pepper and a pinch of celery salt
Oyster crackers and paprika, to serve
steps: Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium-low heat and soften the celery and shallot for 5 minutes.
Add the milk and cream and heat until steaming, without boiling.
Add the oysters and their liquor and cook gently 3–4 minutes, just until the oyster edges curl and they are cooked through.
Season and serve immediately with a pat of butter, a dusting of paprika and oyster crackers.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 onion and 2 celery stalks, finely chopped
250 g (1 cup) smooth peanut butter (or ground Virginia peanuts)
240 ml (1 cup) light cream or half-and-half
1/2 tsp salt and a pinch of cayenne
70 g (1/2 cup) chopped roasted Virginia peanuts, to garnish
steps: Melt the butter and cook the onion and celery over medium heat for 6 minutes until soft.
Stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the stock and simmer 15 minutes.
Whisk in the peanut butter until smooth, blend or strain for a silky texture, then stir in the cream and heat without boiling.
Season with salt and cayenne and serve hot, Colonial Williamsburg style, topped with chopped peanuts.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 900 g (2 lb) honeycomb beef tripe, well cleaned (or beef shin as substitute)
1 onion, 2 carrots and 2 celery stalks, diced
1 tsp dried thyme, 1 tsp marjoram and 2 bay leaves
30 g (2 tbsp) butter and 2 tbsp flour
steps: Simmer the tripe and bone in salted water for 2 1/2 hours until the tripe is tender; remove, cool and cut the tripe into small squares, keeping the broth.
Make a light roux by cooking the butter and flour for 2 minutes, then whisk in some broth.
Return everything to the pot with the vegetables, herbs and plenty of black pepper and simmer 40 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Season generously (it should be peppery) and serve hot; this Revolutionary-era soup is often finished with small flour dumplings.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 900 g (2 lb) snapping turtle meat, from a licensed supplier (veal shank as common substitute)
60 g (4 tbsp) butter and 40 g (1/3 cup) flour
1 onion, 2 carrots and 2 celery stalks, finely diced
1 tsp dried thyme, 2 bay leaves and 1/2 tsp ground cloves
120 ml (1/2 cup) dry sherry, plus extra to serve
steps: Simmer the turtle meat in the stock with the bay leaves for 2 hours until tender, then remove, dice the meat and strain the stock.
Melt the butter, sauté the vegetables for 8 minutes, stir in the flour and cook 4 minutes to a brown roux.
Whisk in the stock, tomato purée, thyme and cloves and simmer 30 minutes until thickened; return the meat and add the sherry.
Serve with chopped egg on top and a small jug of sherry on the side, as in Philadelphia taverns and the Bookbinders tradition.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.8 kg (4 lb) beef top round roast
1 tbsp black pepper and 1 tbsp paprika
2 tsp garlic powder, 1 tsp onion powder and 1 tsp dried oregano
Tiger sauce: 120 ml (1/2 cup) mayonnaise mixed with 3 tbsp prepared horseradish and 1 tsp lemon juice
steps: Mix the salt and spices, rub all over the beef, wrap and refrigerate overnight (12 hours).
Grill over a hot charcoal fire, turning often, for 45–60 minutes until heavily charred outside and rare to medium-rare inside (52–57°C / 125–135°F).
Rest 15 minutes, then slice paper-thin across the grain.
Pile on Kaiser rolls with raw onion and tiger sauce, Pulaski Highway stand style.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 900 g (2 lb) Atlantic whiting fillets (sold as "lake trout" in Baltimore)
1 tsp salt, 1 tsp Old Bay and 1/2 tsp black pepper
Hot sauce, yellow mustard and sliced onion, to serve
steps: Soak the whiting in the milk for 10 minutes, then dredge in the seasoned flour and cornmeal.
Fry at 180°C (350°F) for 4–5 minutes until golden and the fish flakes (63°C / 145°F).
Drain and lay the hot fish on slices of white bread to soak up the oil.
Serve, carry-out style, with hot sauce, mustard and onion, plus fries.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.6 kg (3 1/2 lb) chicken, cut into 8 pieces
2 tsp salt and 1 tsp black pepper
240 g (1 cup) lard or vegetable shortening, for pan-frying
360 ml (1 1/2 cups) milk, for the cream gravy
2 tbsp of the flour, for the gravy
steps: Season the chicken and dredge it in the seasoned flour (a paper bag shake is traditional).
Brown in hot lard in a heavy cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat for 5 minutes per side.
Reduce the heat, add 60 ml (1/4 cup) water, cover tightly and cook 20–25 minutes, then uncover and crisp 5 minutes until the thickest piece reaches 74°C (165°F).
Pour off all but 2 tbsp fat, whisk in the flour, then the milk, and simmer 3 minutes for a cream gravy; serve the chicken with the gravy poured over or alongside.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 corned (brine-cured) ham, about 5–6 kg (12 lb), bone in
2 bunches green onions and 1 bunch celery tops, chopped
1 tbsp crushed red pepper flakes and 2 tsp black pepper
1 tbsp mustard seed and 1 tsp celery seed
Large piece of cheesecloth, for wrapping
steps: Blanch the kale and cabbage in boiling water for 3 minutes, drain and toss with the onions, celery tops and spices.
Cut deep slits about 5 cm (2 in) long all over the ham, top to bottom, and pack each tightly with the greens, mounding the rest on top.
Wrap the ham tightly in cheesecloth, lower into a large pot of simmering water and simmer 20 minutes per lb (about 4 hours) until it reaches 71°C (160°F).
Cool in the liquid, then refrigerate overnight and serve cold in thin slices, St. Mary's County style, often on white bread at Easter.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 whole Smithfield-style country ham, about 6 kg (13 lb), bought from a licensed producer
2 tbsp bourbon or cider (optional, for the glaze)
steps: Scrub the mold off the ham under running water with a stiff brush, then soak in cold water for 24–48 hours, changing the water often, to draw out salt.
Simmer the ham in fresh water, skin side up, at about 20 minutes per lb (about 4 hours) until the shank bone feels loose and it reaches 71°C (160°F); cool in the liquid.
Remove the skin, leaving a thin layer of fat; score it, stud with cloves and coat with brown sugar mixed with mustard and bourbon.
Bake at 200°C (400°F) for 20 minutes until glazed; slice paper-thin and serve on beaten biscuits or Parker House rolls.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 tsp salt and 1 tsp black pepper
60 g (4 tbsp) cold butter or shortening
240 ml (1 cup) hot chicken broth, for the dough
steps: Simmer the chicken with the vegetables, salt and pepper for 1 1/2 hours until tender; lift out, pick the meat and strain the broth.
Mix the flour, baking powder and 1 tsp salt, cut in the fat, then stir in the hot broth to a stiff dough.
Roll out paper-thin (2 mm / 1/16 in) on a floured board and cut into 5 cm (2 in) squares.
Bring the broth to a rolling boil, drop in the squares a few at a time and simmer 15–20 minutes until tender and slippery; return the chicken, heat through and serve in bowls.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 half-smoke sausages (half pork, half beef, smoked; or smoked spicy kielbasa as substitute)
480 ml (2 cups) beef and bean chili, hot
steps: Split the sausages lengthwise partway and grill or griddle over medium-high heat for 8–10 minutes, turning, until well browned and heated through (71°C / 160°F).
Steam the buns for 1 minute until soft.
Put each sausage in a bun and smother with chili, then mustard and onions (and cheese if wanted).
Serve "all the way", the Washington, D.C. way, as on U Street.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 120 ml (1/2 cup) apricot jam or pineapple juice
1 tsp paprika and 1/2 tsp garlic powder
steps: Combine everything in a small saucepan and whisk smooth.
Simmer over medium-low heat for 10–15 minutes, stirring, until slightly thickened and glossy red-orange.
Cool and refrigerate in a jar up to 2 weeks; pour generously over fried chicken wings and fries, D.C. carry-out style.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 700 g (1 1/2 lb) boneless ribeye steak, partly frozen and shaved paper-thin
225 g (8 oz) Cheez Whiz, mild provolone or American cheese
4 Amoroso-style Italian hoagie rolls (soft long rolls)
1/2 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper
Sweet or hot peppers and ketchup, optional
steps: Freeze the ribeye 30 minutes, then slice as thinly as possible.
Cook the onion in half the oil on a griddle or large skillet over medium heat for 6–8 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the remaining oil, raise the heat to high and cook the beef 2–3 minutes, chopping with two spatulas, until no pink remains; season and mix in the onions ("wit").
Divide into four piles, lay provolone or American on top to melt (or warm the Whiz and spoon onto the rolls), then scoop each pile into a split roll and serve.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 tbsp chopped rosemary and 1 tbsp fennel seeds
2 tsp salt and 1 tsp black pepper
480 ml (2 cups) chicken stock and 120 ml (1/2 cup) dry white wine
2 tbsp olive oil and a pinch of chili flakes
steps: Rub the pork with garlic, rosemary, fennel, salt and pepper, set in a roasting pan with the stock and wine, cover with foil and roast at 160°C (325°F) for 3–3 1/2 hours until very tender.
Rest, then slice or pull thinly and keep it soaking in the pan juices.
Blanch the broccoli rabe 2 minutes, then sauté in olive oil with garlic and chili flakes for 5 minutes.
Layer sharp provolone in the rolls, add juicy pork and broccoli rabe, and spoon over extra jus, South Philly style.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 long Italian hoagie rolls, preferably seeded
115 g (4 oz) Genoa salami, thinly sliced
115 g (4 oz) capicola (hot coppa), thinly sliced
115 g (4 oz) prosciutto cotto or boiled ham
Shredded iceberg lettuce, sliced tomato and thinly sliced onion
60 ml (1/4 cup) olive oil and 2 tbsp red wine vinegar
1 tsp dried oregano, salt, pepper and hot pepper relish (optional)
steps: Split the rolls lengthwise without cutting all the way through.
Layer the provolone, then the salami, capicola and ham, overlapping slices along the roll.
Top with lettuce, tomato and onion, and add hot peppers if you like.
Drizzle with oil and vinegar, season with oregano, salt and pepper, fold closed and cut in half to serve.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 225 g (8 oz) thinly sliced turkey or corned beef
225 g (8 oz) thinly sliced tongue or roast beef
steps: Lay out 3 slices of rye per double-decker sandwich (2 sandwiches per 6 slices).
Spread the first slice with Russian dressing and coleslaw, then add a layer of meat and Swiss; add the second slice and repeat with the other meat.
Top with the third slice, press gently and cut into 3 or 4 finger strips.
Serve cold on a platter, the deli-party way it is made in Maplewood and South Orange.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 rounds of pizza bread (or 4 large pita pockets)
2 large potatoes, cut in 1 cm (1/2 in) slices or wedges
1 large onion and 2 bell peppers, sliced
Yellow mustard or ketchup, to serve
steps: Fry the potato slices in oil at 175°C (350°F) for 8–10 minutes until golden and tender; drain and salt.
In the same oil (or a skillet), fry the onions and peppers 6–8 minutes until soft and lightly charred.
Deep fry the hot dogs for 3–4 minutes until blistered and hot through.
Cut the pizza bread in half and open into pockets, stuff each with two hot dogs (or one in a half), the potatoes, and peppers and onions, and serve with mustard.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 6 slices Taylor ham / pork roll, about 5 mm (1/4 in) thick
steps: Cut a small slit from the edge toward the center of each pork roll slice so it lies flat while cooking.
Fry the pork roll in a skillet over medium heat for 2–3 minutes per side until browned at the edges.
Fry the eggs in butter until the whites are set, add the cheese on top to melt over the last minute.
Stack the pork roll and cheesy egg on the toasted roll and finish with salt, pepper and ketchup, Jersey deli style.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 900 g (2 lb) pork shoulder and pork liver or pork offal mix (or just bone-in pork shoulder)
2 tsp salt, 1 tsp black pepper, 1 tsp dried sage and 1/2 tsp thyme
steps: Simmer the pork and onion in the water for 2 hours until the meat falls apart; strain, reserving 1.4 litres (6 cups) broth, and finely mince the meat.
Bring the broth back to a boil and whisk in the cornmeal and buckwheat flour gradually, then the meat and seasonings, and cook stirring 20–30 minutes until very thick.
Pour into a greased loaf pan, smooth, cool and refrigerate overnight (or at least 6 hours) until firm.
Slice 1 cm (1/2 in) thick and fry in butter over medium-high heat 4–5 minutes per side until deeply crisp; serve with eggs and apple butter, ketchup or maple syrup, Pennsylvania Dutch style.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 litres (8 cups) water with 120 g (1/2 cup) baking soda, for the bath
Coarse pretzel salt and yellow mustard, to serve
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, salt, butter and water, knead 8 minutes until smooth, cover and rise 1 hour until doubled.
Divide into 8, roll each into a 60 cm (24 in) rope and shape into the Philly figure-eight, side-by-side pretzel; heat the oven to 230°C (450°F).
Boil each pretzel in the baking soda bath for 30 seconds, drain, set on parchment and sprinkle with coarse salt.
Bake 12–14 minutes until deep mahogany brown, and eat warm with yellow mustard.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 900 g (2 lb) russet potatoes, cut into thick fries (or frozen steak fries)
steps: Fry the potatoes at 160°C (325°F) for 5 minutes, drain, then fry again at 190°C (375°F) for 3–4 minutes until crisp and golden; salt.
Heat the beef gravy until simmering.
Pile the fries in an ovenproof dish, cover with mozzarella and broil 2 minutes until melted.
Pour the hot gravy over and serve at once, late-night New Jersey diner style.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 7 g (2 1/4 tsp) instant yeast and 1 1/2 tsp salt
60 ml (1/4 cup) olive oil, plus extra for the pan
2 garlic cloves, minced, 1 tsp dried oregano and 1 tbsp sugar
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, salt, water and 2 tbsp oil, knead 5 minutes, then press into a well-oiled 33 x 46 cm (13 x 18 in) sheet pan and let rise 2 hours until puffy.
Simmer the tomatoes with garlic, oregano, sugar, the remaining oil and salt for 25 minutes until thick; cool.
Spread the sauce over the dough to the edges and bake at 230°C (450°F) for 25–30 minutes until the base is crisp and golden underneath.
Cool to room temperature, dust with Romano and serve in rectangles, as from South Philly and Norristown bakeries; it has no mozzarella.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 g (1 tsp) instant yeast and 1 tsp salt
300 g (1 1/4 cups) crushed San Marzano-style tomatoes, seasoned with salt and oregano
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, salt and water, knead 5 minutes and let rise 2 hours; place a pizza stone in the oven and heat to 260°C (500°F) for 45 minutes.
Stretch the dough into a thin 35 cm (14 in) round on a floured peel.
Scatter the mozzarella over the dough first, then spoon the crushed tomatoes on top in dollops (cheese under the sauce is the Trenton way).
Drizzle with oil, slide onto the stone and bake 10–12 minutes until the crust is crisp and charred in spots; dust with Romano and serve, as at De Lorenzo's-style pie shops.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 450 g (3 3/4 cups) all-purpose flour, 2 tsp baking powder and 1/2 tsp salt
Fudge icing: 400 g (2 cups) sugar, 240 ml (1 cup) evaporated milk, 115 g (4 oz) unsweetened chocolate and 115 g (1/2 cup) butter
steps: Heat the oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease and flour 3 or more 23 cm (9 in) cake pans (you will bake 8–10 thin layers in rounds).
Cream the butter and sugar 4 minutes, beat in the eggs one at a time, then alternate the flour mix with the evaporated milk and vanilla.
Spread about 180 ml (3/4 cup) batter thinly in each pan and bake 8–10 minutes until just golden; cool briefly, turn out and repeat to make 8–10 layers.
For the icing, boil the sugar and evaporated milk for 2–3 minutes, remove from heat and stir in the chocolate and butter until glossy.
Stack the layers, spreading warm icing between each one, then pour the rest over the top and sides; let set and serve Maryland's official state dessert.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 1/2 tsp baking powder and 1/4 tsp salt
Fudge topping: 340 g (2 cups) semisweet chocolate chips, 240 ml (1 cup) heavy cream, 2 tbsp corn syrup and 300 g (2 1/2 cups) powdered sugar
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F); cream the butter and sugar, beat in the egg and vanilla, then alternate in the flour mix and milk to a soft dough.
Scoop 24 tablespoon mounds onto lined sheets, flatten slightly and bake 8–10 minutes until just set and pale with golden bottoms; cool.
Heat the cream and corn syrup until steaming, pour over the chocolate and stir smooth, then whisk in the powdered sugar to a thick fudge.
Spoon a very thick mound of fudge over the flat side of each cookie and let set 1 hour, Baltimore bakery style.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Beat the cream cheese, butter and vanilla until smooth, then gradually beat in the powdered sugar.
Stir in the coconut until a firm dough forms; chill 20 minutes if too soft.
Roll into small potato shapes about 2.5 cm (1 in) long, then roll in cinnamon to look like little potatoes (press in a few "eyes" with a skewer).
Chill until firm and keep refrigerated; a Philadelphia St. Patrick's Day treat containing no potato.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 480 ml (2 cups) fresh lemon juice (about 10 lemons), or 450 g (1 lb) puréed strawberries or mango
steps: Heat the sugar and water until the sugar dissolves, then cool completely.
Stir in the lemon juice (or fruit purée), zest and salt.
Pour into a shallow metal pan and freeze, scraping and stirring with a fork every 30 minutes for 3–4 hours, until smooth and spoonable rather than icy shards.
Scoop into cups and serve, Philly style, on its own or layered with soft-serve as a "gelati".
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 tsp butter, plus extra for greasing
1 tsp vanilla or peppermint extract and a few drops food coloring
steps: Combine the sugar and cornstarch in a heavy saucepan, then stir in the corn syrup, butter, water and salt.
Bring to a boil over medium heat and cook without stirring to the hard-ball stage, 127°C (260°F) on a candy thermometer.
Remove from heat, stir in the flavoring and color, and pour onto a buttered heatproof tray; cool until just safe to handle.

With buttered hands, pull and stretch the taffy repeatedly for 10–15 minutes until it turns light and satiny, then roll into ropes, cut into bite-size pieces and wrap in waxed paper, Atlantic City boardwalk style.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Pennsylvania Dutch Chicken Pot Pie (Bott Boi)

ingredients: 1.6 kg (3.5 lb) whole chicken, cut into pieces
3 medium potatoes (about 600 g / 1.3 lb), peeled and cubed
1/4 tsp saffron threads (optional, traditional in Lancaster County)
250 g (2 cups) all-purpose flour, plus extra for rolling
2 tsp salt, plus pepper to taste
steps: Simmer the chicken in the salted water with the onion and celery over medium-low heat for 60 minutes until the meat falls from the bone; lift out the chicken, shred the meat and discard skin and bones.
Meanwhile make the bott boi dough: rub the lard into the flour with a pinch of salt, then work in the egg and milk to a stiff dough; rest 10 minutes.
Roll the dough very thin (about 3 mm / 1/8 inch) and cut into 5 cm (2 inch) squares.
Bring the broth back to a rolling boil, add the potatoes and saffron, then drop the squares in one at a time, stirring gently so they do not stick.
Cover and simmer 20 minutes until the potatoes are tender and the noodle squares are cooked through and slightly thickened the broth.
Return the chicken, add parsley, season with salt and pepper, and serve in deep bowls with pepper cabbage or chow-chow on the side.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.5 kg (3.3 lb) bone-in pork shoulder or pork loin roast
900 g (2 lb / about 4 cups) sauerkraut, with its juice
1 tart apple (180 g), cored and grated
250 ml (1 cup) water or light beer
1 1/2 tsp salt and 1 tsp black pepper
steps: Heat oven to 160 C (325 F); season the pork all over with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat and brown the pork on all sides, about 8 minutes.
Stir together the sauerkraut, onion, apple, brown sugar and caraway, pack it around the pork, and pour in the water or beer.
Cover and bake 3 hours, until the pork reaches at least 63 C (145 F) and is fork-tender; for pull-apart shoulder go to 90 C (195 F).
Slice or pull the pork and serve on the kraut with mashed potatoes, as is the Pennsylvania New Year's Day tradition for good luck.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg (2.2 lb) smoked ham hock or bone-in smoked ham
200 g (2 cups) dried apple slices (schnitz), sweet or tart
steps: Soak the dried apple schnitz in water overnight to cover.
Simmer the ham in the 2 L water, covered, over low heat for 2 hours until tender.
Add the soaked schnitz with their soaking water and the brown sugar and simmer 30 minutes more.
For the knepp (dumplings), mix flour, baking powder, salt and pepper, then stir in egg, butter and milk to a stiff, sticky batter.
Drop tablespoons of batter onto the simmering liquid, cover tightly and cook 15 to 18 minutes without lifting the lid until the dumplings are fluffy and dry inside.
Slice the ham and serve with apples, dumplings and plenty of the sweet-smoky broth.

ingredients: 1 cleaned pig stomach (hog maw), about 700 g (1.5 lb), from a butcher
700 g (1.5 lb) fresh bulk pork sausage
900 g (2 lb) potatoes, peeled and cut in 1 cm (1/2 inch) cubes
1 small head cabbage (300 g / 3 cups), shredded (optional)
steps: Heat oven to 180 C (350 F); rinse the hog maw inside and out in cold salted water and pat dry; sew or skewer shut all but one opening.
Mix the raw sausage, potatoes, onion, cabbage, parsley, salt and pepper by hand.
Stuff the maw loosely (it shrinks) and sew or skewer the last opening closed.
Set in a roasting pan with the water, cover with foil and bake 2 hours, then uncover and bake 1 hour more, basting, until deep brown and the filling reaches 71 C (160 F).
Rest 10 minutes, slice thick across, and serve with mustard and applesauce.
