ingredients: 1 onion and 2 celery stalks, roughly cut
250 g (2 cups) flour, 1 tbsp baking powder and 1/2 tsp salt, for waffles
80 ml (1/3 cup) melted butter or oil
steps: Simmer the chicken with onion, celery and 2 tsp salt over low heat for 60 minutes until tender; shred the meat and strain the broth.
Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat, whisk in 35 g flour and cook 2 minutes, then whisk in 750 ml (3 cups) of the hot broth and simmer until thickened like gravy, about 5 minutes.
Fold the chicken and parsley into the gravy, season, and keep warm.
Whisk the waffle flour, baking powder and salt with eggs, milk and melted butter, and cook in a hot greased waffle iron until crisp and golden, about 4 minutes each.
Serve the stewed chicken and gravy ladled over the plain waffles, the Lancaster-style dish (not fried chicken).
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 450 g (3 cups) sweet corn kernels, fresh or frozen
125 g (1 cup) flour, 1 egg and 2-3 tbsp milk, for rivels
steps: Simmer the chicken in the water with onion, celery, salt and saffron for 60 minutes; remove, shred the meat and return it to the pot.
Add the corn and simmer 10 minutes.
Rub the flour, egg and milk between your fingers into small crumbly lumps called rivels.
Sprinkle the rivels into the simmering soup while stirring and cook 8 to 10 minutes until they are tender.
Stir in parsley, adjust seasoning and serve topped with chopped egg, the classic church-supper way.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.4 kg (3 lb) russet potatoes, peeled and cut up
6 slices day-old white bread (180 g), cubed (about 4 cups)
1/4 tsp saffron (optional) and 1 1/2 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp pepper
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 20 minutes until soft, drain and mash.
Melt half the butter in a skillet over medium heat, cook onion and celery 6 minutes until soft, then add the bread cubes and toast 5 minutes until golden.
Beat the eggs and warm milk into the mashed potatoes, then fold in the bread mixture, parsley, saffron, salt and pepper.
Spread in a buttered 23 x 33 cm (9 x 13 inch) dish, dot with remaining butter and bake at 180 C (350 F) for 40 minutes until the top is crusty and brown.
Serve alongside roast turkey or chicken, as at a Pennsylvania Dutch holiday table.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g (2 cups) fresh corn kernels, cut from 3 to 4 ears
1/2 tsp salt and pinch of pepper
60 g (4 tbsp) butter or lard, for frying
steps: Mix the corn, yolks, flour, baking powder, sugar, salt, pepper and milk.
Whip the egg whites to soft peaks and fold them into the corn batter.
Heat the butter in a heavy skillet over medium heat and drop in heaping tablespoons of batter.
Fry 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden and set in the middle; drain on paper.
Serve hot with maple syrup or a sprinkle of salt as a summer side.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g (about 1 1/2 cups) dried sweet corn (such as John Cope's dried corn)
750 ml (3 cups) water, plus more as needed
240 ml (1 cup) whole milk or half-and-half
steps: Soak the dried corn in the water for at least 4 hours (or overnight) in the refrigerator.
Bring the corn and soaking water to a simmer over low heat and cook covered for 35 to 40 minutes, stirring now and then, until tender; add a splash of water if it gets dry.
Stir in the milk, butter, sugar, salt and pepper and simmer 5 minutes more until creamy.
Serve warm as a Thanksgiving or Christmas side.

ingredients: 600 g (6 cups) green cabbage, very finely shredded
1 green bell pepper (150 g), finely diced
1 red bell pepper (150 g), finely diced
1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp celery seed
steps: Combine the cabbage, peppers and carrot in a large bowl.
Stir vinegar, sugar, water, salt and celery seed until the sugar dissolves.
Pour the dressing over the vegetables, toss well and chill at least 1 hour.
Serve cold as one of the sweet-and-sour sides on the Pennsylvania Dutch table.

dishes.name: Dandelion Salad with Hot Bacon Dressing

ingredients: 200 g (6 cups) young dandelion greens, washed and torn (substitute frisee or endive)
1/2 tsp salt and pinch of pepper
steps: Fry the bacon in a skillet over medium heat for 8 minutes until crisp; remove and keep the drippings in the pan.
Whisk flour into the drippings, then add sugar, vinegar, water, salt and pepper and simmer until thickened, about 2 minutes.
Temper the beaten egg with a spoonful of the hot dressing, then whisk it back into the pan and stir 1 minute until it thickens, without boiling.
Pour the hot dressing over the greens, toss, and top with the bacon and sliced eggs; serve at once, often over boiled potatoes.

ingredients: 300 g (2 cups) green and red bell peppers, chopped
200 g (1 1/2 cups) cut green beans, blanched
200 g (1 1/2 cups) cooked kidney or lima beans
1 tbsp mustard seed, 1 tsp celery seed and 1 tsp turmeric
steps: Toss the tomatoes, cabbage, peppers and onions with the pickling salt and leave overnight in the refrigerator, then drain and rinse well.
Bring the vinegar, sugar, mustard seed, celery seed and turmeric to a boil in a non-reactive pot.
Add the drained vegetables and beans and simmer 10 minutes until just tender.
Pack into hot sterilised jars, leaving 1 cm (1/2 inch) headspace, and process in a boiling-water bath 10 minutes, or keep refrigerated up to 1 month.
Serve as one of the "seven sweets and seven sours" alongside meats.

ingredients: 3 medium beets (450 g / 1 lb), or 1 can (425 g / 15 oz) sliced beets with juice
240 ml (1 cup) beet cooking liquid or water
4 whole cloves or a small cinnamon stick (optional)
steps: Simmer the whole beets in water for 30 to 40 minutes until tender, reserving 240 ml of the liquid; peel and slice.
Hard-boil the eggs 10 minutes, cool in ice water and peel.
Bring vinegar, beet liquid, sugar, salt and spices to a boil, stirring to dissolve the sugar.
Layer eggs, beets and onion in a jar, pour over the hot brine and refrigerate at least 24 hours (up to 1 week) until the whites turn magenta.
Halve and serve cold with the pickled beets, a fixture of Pennsylvania Dutch picnics.

ingredients: 225 g (8 oz) Lebanon bologna, sliced 3 mm (1/8 inch) thick (a cured, smoked, tangy beef sausage; buy from Lebanon County makers such as Seltzer's or Weaver's)
1 tbsp prepared yellow mustard or sweet pickle relish
8 small sweet gherkins or bread-and-butter pickles
115 g (4 oz) sharp cheddar, cut in cubes
steps: Lebanon bologna is a fermented, smoked semi-dry sausage made by licensed Pennsylvania smokehouses; buy it ready to eat rather than making it at home.
For roll-ups, mix the cream cheese with mustard or relish, spread thinly on each slice, add a pickle and roll tight; chill 30 minutes and slice into pinwheels.
For a hot snack, fry a few slices in a dry skillet over medium heat 1 to 2 minutes per side until edges curl and crisp.
Serve on a platter with cheddar cubes, pickles and crackers.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 15 g (1 tbsp) sugar or malt syrup
2 L (8 cups) water and 60 g (1/4 cup) baking soda, for the bath
steps: Knead flour, yeast, water, sugar, butter and 1 tsp salt to a stiff, smooth dough, about 8 minutes; rest covered 1 hour.
Divide into 24 pieces, roll into thin ropes 40 cm (16 inches) long and twist into pretzel shapes.
Boil the soda bath, dip each pretzel for 20 seconds, lift out onto parchment-lined trays and sprinkle with coarse salt.
Bake at 200 C (400 F) for 15 minutes until deep brown, then lower to 120 C (250 F) and bake 30 minutes more until dry and crunchy throughout.
Cool completely before storing airtight; they are the crunchy Lititz-style snack.

ingredients: 240 ml (1 cup) Amish friendship bread starter (shared from a friend's sweetened milk starter)
200 g (1 cup) sugar, plus 50 g (1/4 cup) for the pans
1 1/2 tsp baking powder and 1/2 tsp baking soda
1 small box (100 g / 3.4 oz) instant vanilla pudding mix
1 tsp vanilla extract and 1/2 tsp salt
steps: Heat oven to 160 C (325 F); grease two 23 x 13 cm (9 x 5 inch) loaf pans and dust with the 50 g sugar mixed with 1 tsp cinnamon.
Whisk the starter, eggs, oil, milk, vanilla and sugar in a large bowl.
Stir in flour, baking powder, soda, salt, remaining cinnamon and pudding mix until just combined.
Divide between the pans, sprinkle a little more cinnamon sugar on top and bake 60 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool 10 minutes before turning out; traditionally you pass on cups of extra starter with the recipe to friends.

ingredients: 50 g (1/4 cup) sugar and 1 tsp salt
120 ml (1/2 cup) dark corn syrup or light molasses
100 g (1 cup) chopped pecans or walnuts (optional)
steps: Knead flour, yeast, milk, egg, sugar, salt and half the butter into a soft dough, about 8 minutes; let rise 1 hour until doubled.
Melt the remaining butter with half the brown sugar and the corn syrup and pour into a 23 x 33 cm (9 x 13 inch) pan; scatter the nuts over.
Roll the dough to a 30 x 45 cm (12 x 18 inch) rectangle, sprinkle with remaining brown sugar and cinnamon, roll up tightly and cut into 12 slices.
Set the slices cut side down in the pan and let rise 45 minutes until puffy.
Bake at 180 C (350 F) for 25 to 30 minutes until golden, then immediately invert onto a tray so the syrup drips over; serve warm for breakfast.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 240 ml (1 cup) dark unsulphured molasses (Grandma's or Golden Barrel)
60 g (4 tbsp) cold butter or shortening
steps: Heat oven to 200 C (400 F); rub flour, brown sugar, butter, salt and cinnamon to coarse crumbs.
Dissolve the baking soda in the boiling water, stir in the molasses, then whisk in the egg.
Pour the liquid into the crust and scatter the crumbs evenly over the top.
Bake 10 minutes, then reduce to 180 C (350 F) and bake 35 to 40 minutes more until the edges are set and the center wobbles slightly (wet-bottom style).
Cool completely and serve with coffee for breakfast or with whipped cream.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 1/4 tsp baking soda and 1/2 tsp salt
115 g (1/2 cup) butter or shortening, softened
115 g (1/2 cup) butter, softened, for the filling
200 g (2 cups / one 7 oz jar) marshmallow creme and 1 tsp vanilla
steps: Heat oven to 180 C (350 F); cream the butter and brown sugar, beat in the egg.
Mix in the dry ingredients alternately with the buttermilk to a thick batter.
Drop 2-tablespoon mounds 5 cm (2 inches) apart on lined sheets and bake 10 to 12 minutes until they spring back; cool fully.
Beat the filling butter, powdered sugar, marshmallow creme and vanilla until fluffy.
Sandwich a generous spoonful of filling between two cakes, flat sides in, and wrap individually as Amish bakeries do.

ingredients: 6 small baking apples (Rome, Stayman or Granny Smith), peeled and cored
225 g (1 cup) cold butter or shortening
120 ml (1/2 cup) ice-cold milk or water
100 g (1/2 cup) sugar mixed with 1 tsp cinnamon, for filling
steps: Cut the cold butter into the flour with a pinch of salt and bind with the cold milk; chill 20 minutes.
Simmer the brown sugar, water and cinnamon 5 minutes to make a syrup.

Roll the pastry 3 mm (1/8 inch) thick and cut into six 18 cm (7 inch) squares; set an apple on each, fill the core with cinnamon sugar and a dot of butter, and fold the corners up to enclose, pinching the seams.
Place in a baking dish, pour the hot syrup around them and bake at 190 C (375 F) for 45 to 50 minutes, basting twice, until golden and the apples are tender when pierced.
Serve warm in a bowl with cold milk poured over, the Lancaster County way.

ingredients: 900 g (2 lb) potatoes, boiled and mashed (about 2 cups), with 240 ml (1 cup) potato water
115 g (1/2 cup) butter or lard, melted
2 L (8 cups) lard or oil, for frying
Powdered or granulated sugar, for dusting
steps: Mix the mashed potato, potato water, milk, butter, sugar, eggs, yeast and salt, then work in the flour to a soft dough; let rise 2 hours until doubled.
Roll 1 cm (1/2 inch) thick and cut into squares or rectangles, slitting each in the center; let rise 30 minutes.
Heat the lard to 180 C (350 F) in a heavy pot.
Fry a few at a time, 1 to 2 minutes per side, until deep golden and cooked through; drain on paper.
Dust with sugar or split and spread with molasses, eaten on Fastnacht Day (Shrove Tuesday) to use up fat before Lent.

ingredients: 1 unbaked 23 cm (9 inch) deep-dish pie crust
100 g (1/2 cup) sugar and 30 g (1/3 cup) cocoa powder, for the chocolate syrup
1 tsp baking powder and 1/4 tsp salt
steps: Heat oven to 180 C (350 F); whisk the cocoa, 100 g sugar, hot water and vanilla to a thin syrup and let cool.
Cream the butter and 150 g sugar, beat in the egg, then add the flour, baking powder and salt alternately with the milk.
Spread the cake batter in the pie shell and gently pour the chocolate syrup over the top; do not stir.
Bake 40 to 45 minutes until the cake springs back; the syrup sinks to form a fudgy layer between crust and cake.
Cool and serve in wedges with coffee.

ingredients: 100 g (1/2 cup) sugar, for bottom layer
1 large egg, plus 1 egg for the topping
150 g (1 1/4 cups) flour, 1 tsp baking soda, 150 g (3/4 cup) sugar, for topping
steps: Heat oven to 190 C (375 F); whisk molasses, 100 g sugar, 1 egg, lemon juice, zest, water and 1 tbsp flour and pour into the crust.
Cream the butter and 150 g sugar, beat in the second egg, then add flour and baking soda alternately with the buttermilk.
Spoon the cake batter gently over the lemon-molasses layer.
Bake 40 to 45 minutes until the top is golden and springs back.
Cool before slicing to show the gooey bottom and cake top; a Montgomery County favourite.

ingredients: Pastry for a double-crust 23 cm (9 inch) pie, made with butter or shortening (no egg wash)
1/2 tsp cinnamon and pinch of salt
steps: Simmer the raisins in 360 ml (1 1/2 cups) of the water for 5 minutes to plump.
Mix the brown sugar, cornstarch, cinnamon and salt with the remaining water, stir into the raisins and cook, stirring, until thick and glossy, about 3 minutes.
Off heat, stir in the lemon juice, zest and butter; cool slightly.
Pour into the bottom crust, cover with a lattice or vented top crust, sprinkle with sugar and bake at 200 C (400 F) for 35 to 40 minutes until golden and bubbling.
Cool before slicing; it was made ahead to bring to families after a funeral because it keeps well.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: Pastry for a double-crust 23 cm (9 inch) pie, made with butter or shortening
steps: Soak the dried apples in the water overnight.
Simmer the apples in their soaking water for 20 minutes until very soft, then mash coarsely.
Stir in sugar, orange juice and zest, cinnamon, cloves and cornstarch, cooking 2 minutes until thick; cool.
Fill the bottom crust, cover with the top crust, cut vents and bake at 200 C (400 F) for 40 minutes until golden.
Serve cool; snitz pie was carried in half-moon "preaching pies" for church Sundays.

ingredients: 2 large eggs, plus 1 egg white for brushing
steps: Cream the butter and sugar, beat in the eggs and vanilla, then mix in the flour and salt.
Wrap and chill the dough at least 2 hours or overnight.
Roll very thin, about 1.5 mm (1/16 inch), on a floured surface and cut into stars, hearts or rounds.
Brush with egg white, sprinkle with cinnamon sugar and press a pecan half in the center.
Bake at 180 C (350 F) for 6 to 8 minutes until edges are barely golden; cool and store in tins for Christmas.

ingredients: 1/2 tsp birch oil or birch beer extract (food-grade; substitute 1/4 tsp wintergreen extract)
2 L (8 cups) chilled seltzer or club soda
steps: Birch beer is a non-alcoholic Pennsylvania soft drink flavored with birch bark oil; this version is a quick syrup mixed with seltzer, no fermentation.
Heat the sugar and water over medium heat until dissolved, about 3 minutes, then cool completely.
Stir in the birch extract and vanilla; refrigerate the syrup in a bottle up to 2 weeks.
For each glass, pour 2 tbsp (30 ml) syrup over ice and top with 240 ml (1 cup) cold seltzer; stir gently and serve, or pour over vanilla ice cream for a float.

ingredients: 500 g (4 cups) bread flour or high-gluten flour
10 g (2 tsp) salt and 1 tsp sugar
400 g (14 oz can) whole peeled tomatoes, crushed by hand
1 tsp dried oregano and 1 garlic clove, grated
340 g (12 oz / 3 cups) low-moisture whole-milk mozzarella, shredded
30 g (1/3 cup) grated Pecorino Romano or Parmesan
steps: Mix flour, water, yeast, salt, sugar and oil and knead 8 minutes until smooth; divide into 2 balls, oil them and cold-ferment in the refrigerator 24 hours for flavor.
For the uncooked sauce, stir the crushed tomatoes with oregano, garlic and a pinch of salt.
Heat a pizza stone or steel on the top rack at the oven's maximum, 260-290 C (500-550 F), for 1 hour.
Hand-stretch each ball into a thin 35 cm (14 inch) round with a slightly thicker rim, spread a thin layer of sauce and cover with mozzarella.
Slide onto the stone and bake 7 to 9 minutes until the cheese is bubbling and the rim is charred in spots.
Sprinkle with grated cheese, cut into 8 large wedges, and eat folded in half, NYC slice style.

ingredients: 80 ml (1/3 cup) extra-virgin olive oil, divided
280 g (10 oz) fresh or low-moisture mozzarella, torn or shredded
400 g (14 oz can) San Marzano-style tomatoes, crushed
1 tsp dried oregano and fresh basil leaves
steps: Mix flour, water, yeast, salt and 1 tbsp oil to a sticky dough; let rise 1 hour.
Pour 4 tbsp oil into a 33 x 45 cm (13 x 18 inch) sheet pan, press the dough toward the corners, rest 20 minutes and press again to fill the pan; rise 30 minutes more.
Heat oven to 250 C (475 F); simmer the tomatoes with garlic, oregano and remaining oil for 10 minutes.
Scatter mozzarella over the dough, then spoon the sauce on top in dollops or stripes.
Bake on the lowest rack 15 to 20 minutes until the bottom is crisp and golden; finish with Pecorino, basil and a drizzle of oil, and cut into squares, the Long Island way.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 large onion (200 g / 1 1/2 cups), finely chopped
steps: Knead the flour, water, yeast and salt 10 minutes to a smooth, firm dough; let rise 2 hours until doubled.
Cook the onion in oil over medium-low heat 10 minutes until soft and lightly golden, then stir in poppy seeds and salt; cool.
Divide the dough into 8 balls, rest 30 minutes, then flatten each into a 12 cm (5 inch) round and press a deep well in the center, leaving a puffy rim.
Fill each well with a spoonful of onion mixture and let rise 20 minutes.
Bake at 240 C (460 F) on a hot stone or sheet 12 to 15 minutes until lightly browned; unlike a bagel it is not boiled. Serve warm with butter or cream cheese, Lower East Side style.

dishes.name: Bagel with Lox and Cream Cheese

ingredients: 4 plain or everything bagels, from a New York-style bakery (boiled and baked)
225 g (8 oz) thinly sliced lox or Nova smoked salmon
1 small red onion, very thinly sliced
steps: Split the bagels and toast lightly if they are not fresh that morning.
Spread each half thickly with cream cheese.
Drape the lox over the bottom halves, then add tomato, red onion and capers.
Sprinkle with dill, close or serve open-faced, as at a Jewish appetizing shop.

dishes.name: Bacon, Egg and Cheese on a Roll

ingredients: Salt, pepper and ketchup, to taste
steps: Fry the bacon in a skillet over medium heat 7 to 8 minutes until crisp; drain.
Melt the butter on a griddle over medium heat, beat 2 eggs per sandwich and cook flat or scrambled until just set, about 2 minutes.
Lay a slice of American cheese on each egg portion to melt, and toast the cut rolls briefly on the griddle.
Stack the egg, cheese and bacon in the roll, season with salt, pepper and ketchup ("SPK"), wrap in foil and serve, bodega style.

ingredients: 8 very fresh large eggs, plus 3 egg yolks for the sauce
170 g (3/4 cup / 1 1/2 sticks) butter, melted and hot
steps: For hollandaise, whisk the 3 yolks with lemon juice in a bowl over barely simmering water until thick and pale, about 2 minutes, then slowly whisk in the hot butter; season with salt and cayenne and keep warm.
Brown the Canadian bacon in a skillet over medium heat 1 to 2 minutes per side; toast the muffins.
Bring a wide pan of water to a gentle simmer with the vinegar and poach the eggs 3 to 4 minutes until the whites are set and yolks runny.
Top each muffin half with bacon and a poached egg, spoon over hollandaise, and garnish with chives; a Delmonico's / Waldorf brunch classic.

ingredients: 680 g (1.5 lb) deli pastrami (cured, spiced, smoked beef navel or brisket), unsliced if possible
8 slices Jewish rye bread with caraway
steps: Set a rack in a pot over the water, bring to a simmer, add the pastrami, cover and steam 15 to 20 minutes until hot through and tender (above 74 C / 165 F).
Hand-slice against the grain about 5 mm (1/4 inch) thick.
Spread mustard on the rye and pile on about 170 g (6 oz) pastrami per sandwich.
Cut in half and serve with pickles on the side, Katz's-deli style; no mayo, no cheese.

ingredients: 1 tsp adobo or seasoned salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper
4 tbsp mayonnaise and ketchup, to taste
steps: Heat a griddle or large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the onion 3 minutes until soft.
Add the beef in patties, season with adobo and pepper, sear 3 minutes, then chop and break it up with a spatula until browned and no pink remains, 5 to 6 minutes.
Divide into 4 piles, lay 2 slices of cheese over each and chop it in until melted.
Toast the split rolls, spread with mayo and ketchup, add lettuce and tomato, and scoop in the beef-cheese mixture; a Harlem/Bronx bodega classic.

ingredients: 900 g (2 lb) boneless skinless chicken thighs
3 tbsp lemon juice, 3 garlic cloves and 1 tbsp dried oregano
1 tsp ground coriander, 1 tsp cumin and 1 1/2 tsp salt
1/2 tsp turmeric and 1/2 tsp cumin, for rice
120 ml (1/2 cup) mayonnaise, 60 ml (1/4 cup) Greek yogurt, 1 tbsp vinegar, 1 tsp sugar, for white sauce
Shredded iceberg lettuce, tomato wedges, pita and hot sauce (harissa-style red sauce), to serve
steps: Marinate the chicken with lemon, garlic, oregano, coriander, cumin, salt and 2 tbsp oil for at least 1 hour.
Melt butter in a saucepan, toast the rice with turmeric and cumin 2 minutes, add stock, cover and simmer on low 15 minutes; rest 10 minutes.
Sear the chicken in the remaining oil over medium-high heat 5 to 6 minutes per side until cooked through (74 C / 165 F), then chop into bite-size pieces and toss back in the pan juices.
Whisk the white sauce ingredients with black pepper and a splash of water until pourable.
Plate rice, chicken, lettuce and tomato, then drizzle generously with white sauce and a little red hot sauce, with warm pita on the side, like the 53rd and 6th cart.

dishes.name: New York Hot Dog with Onion Sauce

ingredients: 8 all-beef frankfurters (natural casing, such as Sabrett)
2 large onions (400 g / 3 cups), thinly sliced
1/2 tsp chili powder and 1/4 tsp cinnamon
Spicy brown mustard and sauerkraut, to serve
steps: Cook the onions in oil over medium heat 8 minutes until soft but not brown.
Stir in tomato paste, chili powder, cinnamon, sugar, salt and water and simmer 15 to 20 minutes until thick and jammy, the red "street-cart" onion sauce.
Simmer the franks in salted water ("dirty water" style) for 5 minutes or griddle until heated through.
Steam or warm the buns, add a frank, mustard and a heap of onion sauce or sauerkraut, and serve.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1/2 tsp baking powder and 1/2 tsp salt
1 large egg, plus 1 egg for the wash
900 g (2 lb) russet potatoes, peeled and boiled
60 ml (1/4 cup) vegetable oil or butter, for onions
1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper
steps: Mix flour, baking powder, salt, 1 egg, oil and water to a soft, elastic dough; knead 3 minutes, oil and rest covered 1 hour.
Fry the onions in oil over medium-low heat 20 minutes until deeply golden; mash with the potatoes, salt and pepper.
Roll the dough very thin into a 30 x 45 cm (12 x 18 inch) rectangle, lay a log of filling along one long edge and roll up; twist off 8 portions with the side of your hand.
Pinch each end closed and flatten slightly into rounds; set on a lined tray and brush with beaten egg.
Bake at 190 C (375 F) for 35 to 40 minutes until golden; serve hot with deli mustard, as on the Lower East Side.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 450 g (1 lb) chicken livers, trimmed and patted dry
3 tbsp schmaltz (rendered chicken fat), or vegetable oil
2 large onions (400 g / 3 cups), thinly sliced
1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper
2 tbsp gribenes (crispy chicken skin cracklings), optional
Rye bread or matzo, to serve
steps: Cook the onions in 2 tbsp schmaltz over medium-low heat 15 to 20 minutes until deep golden.
Push the onions aside, add the remaining schmaltz and sear the livers over medium-high heat 3 to 4 minutes per side until browned outside and no longer pink inside (71 C / 160 F).
Cool slightly, then chop the livers, onions and eggs together by hand or pulse in a food processor to a coarse spread.
Season with salt and pepper, chill 1 hour, and serve with gribenes, rye bread and pickles, deli style.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 450 g (1 lb) whole hot-smoked whitefish (or smoked trout)
60 g (1/4 cup) sour cream or cream cheese
1 celery stalk (50 g / 1/2 cup), finely diced
steps: Peel off the skin and lift the flesh from the bones, carefully removing every pin bone; flake into a bowl.
Mix the mayonnaise, sour cream, lemon juice and pepper.
Fold in the fish, celery, onion and dill, leaving some texture.
Chill 30 minutes and serve on bagels or rye with sliced cucumber, as at an appetizing counter.

60 ml (1/4 cup) seltzer or chicken stock

steps: Heat oven to 190 C (375 F); cream the butter and sugar, beat in eggs, vanilla and lemon, then add flour, baking powder and salt alternately with milk.

ingredients: 1.8 kg (4 lb) littleneck or cherrystone clams (quahogs), scrubbed, or 2 cans (6.5 oz/184 g each) chopped clams plus 480 ml (2 cups) bottled clam juice
120 g (4 oz) salt pork or thick-cut bacon, diced

2 sprigs fresh thyme and 1 bay leaf
480 ml (2 cups) whole milk plus 240 ml (1 cup) heavy cream
1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp black pepper, plus oyster crackers to serve
steps: Put the clams in a large pot with 480 ml (2 cups) water, cover and steam over high heat for 6 to 8 minutes until they open; discard any that stay shut, pull out the meat, chop it, and strain the broth through a paper towel to remove grit.

In a heavy Dutch oven render the salt pork over medium heat for 8 minutes until the fat runs and the bits are golden, then add the butter, onion and celery and cook 6 minutes until soft but not browned.

Stir in the flour and cook 1 minute, then whisk in the strained clam broth (about 720 ml / 3 cups, topped up with bottled clam juice if needed), add potatoes, thyme and bay leaf and simmer 15 minutes until the potatoes are just tender.
Lower the heat, pour in the milk and cream and warm gently for 5 minutes without letting it boil, then add the chopped clams and heat 2 minutes more so they stay tender.
Season with salt and pepper, remove the herbs, and let the chowder rest 10 minutes off the heat to thicken; serve with oyster crackers on top.

ingredients: 120 g (4 oz) salt pork or bacon, diced
700 g (1 1/2 lb) waxy potatoes, cut in 1.5 cm (1/2 in) cubes
2 sprigs fresh thyme and 1 bay leaf
1/4 tsp black pepper, salt to taste (clams are salty)
steps: Steam the quahogs in the water in a covered pot over high heat for 8 to 10 minutes until they open; remove the meat, chop it finely, and strain the broth through a cloth-lined sieve.
Render the salt pork in a soup pot over medium heat for 8 minutes until crisp, then add onion and celery and cook 6 minutes until translucent.
Add the strained clam broth, potatoes, thyme and bay leaf and simmer 15 minutes until the potatoes are tender and some edges have softened into the broth.

Finish with parsley and serve the clear, milk-free broth with clam cakes or saltines alongside, as is done along Narragansett Bay.

720 ml (3 cups) fish stock or water

480 ml (2 cups) whole milk and 240 ml (1 cup) light cream (half-and-half)
1 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp white pepper
Common crackers or oyster crackers, to serve

Add the potatoes, stock, bay leaf and thyme, bring to a boil and simmer 12 minutes until the potatoes are nearly tender.
Lay the fish chunks on top, cover and simmer gently for 6 to 8 minutes until the fish is opaque and flakes easily (63°C / 145°F).
Pour in the milk and cream and heat over low for 5 minutes without boiling, stirring gently so the fish stays in large flakes.

4 New England-style top-split hot dog buns

900 g (2 lb) mussels, scrubbed and debearded

steps: Soak the clams for 1 hour in cold water mixed with the salt and cornmeal so they spit out sand, then lift them out and rinse well, discarding any with cracked shells.
Bring the water, onion and bay leaf to a boil in a large pot, add the clams, cover and steam over high heat for 6 to 8 minutes until the shells open wide; discard any that stay closed.

steps: Rinse the shucked clams under cold water to remove sand and drain well on paper towels.
Whisk the milk with the egg, and in another bowl mix the corn flour, flour, salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a deep heavy pot to 190°C (375°F).
Dip the clams in the milk, then toss them in the flour mix, shaking off the excess, and fry in small batches for 1 1/2 to 2 minutes until golden and crisp.
Drain on a rack, salt lightly while hot, and serve with tartar sauce, lemon wedges, fries and coleslaw in the classic Ipswich style.

ingredients: 4 young cod or haddock fillets (scrod), about 170 g (6 oz) each
60 g (1 cup) crushed Ritz-style butter crackers or panko
1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp black pepper
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F) and butter a baking dish.
Lay the fillets in the dish, season with salt and pepper and sprinkle over the lemon juice and white wine.
Mix the cracker crumbs with the melted butter, parsley and paprika and press a layer over the top of each fillet.
Bake 12 to 15 minutes until the crumbs are golden and the fish flakes easily with a fork (63°C / 145°F); serve with lemon wedges, boiled potatoes and green beans.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 700 g (1 1/2 lb) floury potatoes, peeled and cut in chunks
60 ml (1/4 cup) oil or bacon fat for frying
steps: Soak the salt cod in cold water in the fridge for 12 to 24 hours, changing the water 3 or 4 times, until a nibble tastes only mildly salty.
Simmer the cod in fresh water for 10 minutes until it flakes, drain and flake it, removing any skin and bones; boil the potatoes separately for 15 minutes until tender and mash with the butter.
Mix the cod, mashed potato, onion, egg, parsley and pepper and shape into 8 patties about 2 cm (3/4 in) thick, then dust lightly with flour.
Fry in hot oil or bacon fat over medium-high heat for 3 to 4 minutes per side until deep golden and crisp, and serve with baked beans and brown bread or with eggs for breakfast.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.4 kg (3 lb) corned beef brisket, rinsed
1 bay leaf and 1 tsp black peppercorns
3 small turnips or 1 rutabaga, cut in wedges
1 small green cabbage, cut in 6 wedges
steps: Put the corned beef in a large pot, cover with cold water, add the bay leaf and peppercorns, bring to a boil, skim, then cover and simmer gently for 3 hours until fork-tender.
Boil the beets separately in salted water for 35 to 40 minutes until tender, then slip off the skins; cooking them apart keeps everything else from turning red.
Lift out the beef and keep it warm, then add potatoes, carrots, turnips and onions to the broth and simmer 20 minutes.
Add the cabbage wedges and cook 10 to 12 minutes more until all the vegetables are tender.
Slice the beef across the grain and serve on a platter surrounded by the vegetables and beets, with mustard, horseradish and a little of the broth; save leftovers for red flannel hash.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g (2 cups) cooked corned beef, chopped
3 tbsp (45 g) butter or bacon fat
60 ml (1/4 cup) heavy cream or broth
1/2 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper
steps: Melt the fat in a large cast-iron skillet over medium heat and cook the onion 5 minutes until soft.
Add the corned beef, potatoes and beets, season and stir in the cream, then press the mixture flat with a spatula.
Cook undisturbed for 10 to 12 minutes until a dark, crisp crust forms on the bottom, then flip in sections and crisp the other side for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile fry or poach the eggs, then serve the deep-red hash topped with an egg and parsley.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp black pepper
115 g (4 oz) sharp white cheddar, grated or thinly sliced
4 soft kaiser rolls or hamburger buns
steps: Mix the beef with salt and pepper and shape into 4 thick patties about 2 cm (3/4 in) thick.

Set a steamer basket or small metal trays over simmering water in a covered pot, place the patties on them, cover and steam for 10 to 12 minutes until cooked through (71°C / 160°F); the meat stays moist and pale.
Melt the cheddar in a separate small tin in the steamer for 3 to 4 minutes until molten, as done in Meriden, Connecticut.
Briefly steam or warm the buns, set a patty on each, pour the melted cheese over the top and finish with onion, pickles and mustard or ketchup.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 225 g (8 oz) ground pork or thinly sliced pork
2 tbsp dark soy sauce or gravy master browning sauce
2 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 3 tbsp water
150 g (3 cups) crispy fried chow mein noodles (Hoo-Mee brand in Fall River)
steps: Brown the pork in the oil in a wok or skillet over medium-high heat for 5 to 6 minutes until cooked through.
Add the onion and celery and stir-fry 4 minutes, then pour in the stock and soy sauce and simmer 5 minutes.
Add the bean sprouts and stir in the cornstarch slurry, cooking 2 minutes until the sauce turns thick and glossy brown.
Pile a handful of crispy noodles on the bottom of each bun, ladle the chow mein gravy generously over them, close the bun and eat with a fork as the sandwich softens.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 ml (3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp) lukewarm water
1/2 tsp instant yeast and 1 1/2 tsp salt
24 fresh littleneck clams, shucked and chopped (or 1 can, 6.5 oz/184 g, chopped clams, drained)
Coarse cornmeal for the peel and lemon wedges to serve
steps: Mix the flour, water, yeast and salt into a shaggy dough, knead 5 minutes, then cover and refrigerate for 24 hours to develop the chewy, blistered "apizza" crust; bring to room temperature for 2 hours before baking.
Put a pizza stone or steel in the oven and heat it at the highest setting, ideally 290°C (550°F), for 1 hour.

Stretch the dough into a thin, irregular oval and set it on a cornmeal-dusted peel; brush with olive oil and scatter over the garlic, oregano, Pecorino and the chopped clams (no mozzarella, no tomato).
Slide onto the stone and bake 8 to 10 minutes until the crust is charred in spots and the clams are cooked through, then drizzle with more olive oil and serve with lemon wedges as at Frank Pepe's.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tsp dried oregano and 1/2 tsp red pepper flakes
1 tbsp sugar for the sauce and 1/2 tsp salt
steps: Mix the flour, water, yeast, salt, sugar and 2 tbsp olive oil into a soft dough, knead 8 minutes and let rise covered for 1 1/2 hours until doubled.
Simmer the tomatoes with garlic, oregano, pepper flakes, sugar and salt over low heat for 25 minutes until thick enough to coat a spoon, then cool.
Press the dough into an oiled 33 x 46 cm (13 x 18 in) sheet pan with the remaining oil, rest 20 minutes, then spread the thick sauce all over (no cheese, as in Rhode Island bakeries).
Bake at 220°C (425°F) for 20 to 25 minutes until the bottom is golden and the sauce has darkened slightly.
Cool completely and cut into long rectangular strips; they are eaten at room temperature, often bought by the tray for parties.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp black pepper
120 ml (1/2 cup) clam juice (reserved from the clams)
225 g (1 cup) chopped quahog clams (fresh steamed or canned, drained)
1.5 litres (6 cups) vegetable oil for frying
steps: Whisk the flour, baking powder, salt and pepper in a bowl, then beat in the egg, milk and clam juice to make a thick, sticky batter.
Fold in the chopped clams and let the batter rest 10 minutes.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 185°C (365°F) and drop in tablespoons of batter a few at a time.
Fry 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until the fritters are puffed, deep golden and cooked through in the centre, then drain on paper towels.
Salt while hot and serve by the bagful with clear chowder for dunking, Rhode Island shore-style.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 225 g (8 oz) chouriço or linguiça sausage, finely chopped
150 g (3 cups) day-old bread or Ritz-style crackers, crumbled
2 tbsp chopped parsley and 1/2 tsp paprika
Lemon wedges and hot sauce, to serve
steps: Steam the quahogs in 240 ml (1 cup) water in a covered pot over high heat for 10 minutes until open; chop the meat, strain and reserve the broth, and keep 12 half-shells.
Melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat and cook the sausage, onion, celery and garlic for 8 minutes until soft and the sausage releases its red oil.
Stir in the chopped clams, breadcrumbs, parsley, paprika and pepper flakes, moistening with clam broth until the stuffing holds together.
Pack the stuffing into the half-shells, set on a baking sheet and bake at 190°C (375°F) for 20 minutes until the tops are crisp and golden.
Serve hot with lemon wedges and a dash of hot sauce, Portuguese-Rhode Island style.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 12 natural-casing beef-pork hot dogs (New York System wieners), cut in half if long
1 large onion, very finely chopped, plus extra raw onion to top
1 tbsp chili powder, 1 tsp paprika and 1 tsp ground cumin
1/2 tsp ground allspice, 1/4 tsp ground cinnamon and 1/4 tsp ground nutmeg
240 ml (1 cup) water or beef stock
Yellow mustard and celery salt, to serve
steps: Brown the ground beef in the oil over medium heat, breaking it into very fine crumbs with a potato masher, for 8 minutes until no longer pink.
Add the chopped onion and all the spices and cook 3 minutes until fragrant, then add the water and salt and simmer 25 minutes until the meat sauce is thick and fine-textured.
Grill or griddle the wieners over medium heat for 5 minutes, turning, until browned and heated through.
Put each wiener in a steamed bun, then top in the "New York System" order: yellow mustard, the meat sauce, chopped raw onion and a shake of celery salt; serve with coffee milk.

ingredients: 2 tbsp vegetable oil, plus 1.5 litres (6 cups) for frying
1 tsp ground cinnamon mixed with 50 g (1/4 cup) sugar (optional)
Warm tomato sauce or melted butter, for the savory version
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, salt, water and 2 tbsp oil into a soft dough, knead 5 minutes and let rise covered for 1 hour until doubled.
Divide into 8 balls and stretch each by hand into a thin, irregular disc about 18 cm (7 in) across.
Heat the frying oil to 190°C (375°F) in a wide pot and fry one disc at a time for 1 minute per side until puffed and golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot like a New England fair: dusted with powdered sugar or cinnamon sugar, or with butter and tomato sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 450 g (1 lb / 2 1/3 cups) dried navy or pea beans
170 g (6 oz) salt pork, cut in two pieces and scored
1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper
steps: Soak the beans overnight in plenty of cold water, then drain, cover with fresh water and simmer 45 minutes until the skins split when you blow on a spoonful.
Drain, reserving the liquid, and put the onion and one piece of salt pork in the bottom of a bean pot or Dutch oven, then add the beans and bury the other piece of pork scored-side up on top.
Stir the molasses, sugar, mustard, salt and pepper into 480 ml (2 cups) of the hot bean liquid and pour over the beans, adding water just to cover.
Cover and bake at 135°C (275°F) for 5 to 6 hours, checking every hour and topping up with hot water so the beans stay just covered; uncover for the last hour to brown the top.
Serve the dark, sticky beans with Boston brown bread and franks, as on a traditional Saturday night.

ingredients: 300 g (2 cups) fresh or frozen lima beans or shell beans
300 g (2 cups) fresh sweet corn kernels (about 4 ears)
120 ml (1/2 cup) heavy cream or whole milk
1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp black pepper
1 tbsp chopped fresh parsley or chives
steps: Simmer the lima beans in salted water for 8 to 10 minutes until tender, then drain; this dish comes from the Narragansett word msickquatash for boiled corn and beans.
Melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion 4 minutes until soft.
Add the corn and cook 3 minutes, then add the beans and cream and simmer 3 to 4 minutes until slightly thickened.
Season with salt and pepper, finish with herbs and serve as a side to roast turkey or fish.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tsp baking soda and 1/2 tsp salt
Butter for greasing, and softened butter or cream cheese to serve
steps: Grease two clean 425 g (15 oz) cans or a 1.5 litre (6 cup) pudding mold with butter.
Whisk the rye flour, whole-wheat flour, cornmeal, baking soda and salt, then stir in the buttermilk and molasses until just combined and fold in the raisins.
Fill the cans two-thirds full, cover tightly with buttered foil tied with string, and set on a rack in a deep pot with boiling water reaching halfway up the cans.
Cover the pot and steam over low heat for 2 hours, topping up with boiling water as needed, until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool 10 minutes, slide the loaves out, slice into rounds and serve warm with butter, traditionally alongside baked beans.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Whisk the cornmeal into the boiling water and cook 2 minutes, stirring, into a thin porridge, then stir in the molasses, butter and salt and cool to lukewarm.
Mix in the yeast and enough flour to make a soft dough, then knead 8 to 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Let rise covered in a warm place for 1 1/2 hours until doubled, then shape into two loaves and place in greased 23 x 13 cm (9 x 5 in) loaf pans.
Rise 45 minutes until the dough domes above the pans, then bake at 190°C (375°F) for 35 to 40 minutes until dark brown and hollow-sounding when tapped.
Cool on a rack before slicing; this Rockport, Massachusetts fishermen's bread makes excellent toast.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 85 g (6 tbsp) butter, melted, plus 60 g (4 tbsp) for brushing
steps: Mix the warm milk, yeast, sugar, egg and 85 g melted butter, then add the salt and flour and knead 8 minutes into a soft, smooth dough.
Let rise covered for 1 hour until doubled, then roll out 1 cm (1/2 in) thick and cut into 7.5 cm (3 in) rounds.
Brush each round with melted butter, fold it slightly off-centre into a half-moon, press the fold, and set the rolls snugly in a buttered baking pan.
Rise 40 minutes until puffy, brush with butter and bake at 190°C (375°F) for 15 to 18 minutes until golden.
Brush again with butter, sprinkle with flaky salt and serve warm, as created at Boston's Parker House hotel.

ingredients: 150 g (1 cup) stone-ground white flint cornmeal (Rhode Island "jonnycake meal")
3 tbsp butter or bacon fat for the griddle (butter for vegetarian)
Butter and maple syrup, to serve
steps: Mix the cornmeal, salt and sugar in a bowl and pour over the boiling water, stirring constantly, so the meal scalds and swells into a thick mush; rest 5 minutes.
Stir in the milk to loosen it to a thick, spoonable batter (substitute fine yellow cornmeal if white flint meal is unavailable).
Heat a griddle with butter over medium heat and drop in 2-tablespoon mounds, flattening slightly to about 1 cm (1/2 in) thick.
Cook slowly for 5 to 6 minutes per side until a deep golden crust forms and the centres are set, then serve hot with butter and maple syrup.

ingredients: 3 tbsp (25 g) Marshmallow Fluff (marshmallow creme, contains egg white)
steps: Spread the peanut butter evenly over one slice of bread, all the way to the edges.
Spread the Marshmallow Fluff over the other slice; it is sticky, so dip the knife in warm water for easier spreading.
Add banana slices if you like, press the slices together, cut in half and eat right away, as Massachusetts schoolkids have since the 1910s.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 190 g (1 1/2 cups) cake flour and 1 1/2 tsp baking powder
150 g (3/4 cup) sugar plus 100 g (1/2 cup) for the custard
3 eggs plus 4 egg yolks for the custard
120 ml (1/2 cup) whole milk plus 480 ml (2 cups) for the custard
3 tbsp cornstarch and a pinch of salt
steps: For the custard, heat 480 ml milk until steaming, whisk the yolks with 100 g sugar, cornstarch and salt, temper with the hot milk, then cook over medium heat 2 to 3 minutes, whisking, until thick and bubbling; stir in 1 tsp vanilla, cover with plastic and chill 2 hours.
For the cake, beat the 3 eggs with 150 g sugar for 5 minutes until pale and thick, fold in the flour and baking powder, then the melted butter, 120 ml milk and remaining vanilla.
Pour into a buttered 23 cm (9 in) round pan and bake at 175°C (350°F) for 25 to 30 minutes until springy and a skewer comes out clean; cool completely and split into two layers.
Spread the chilled custard over the bottom layer and set the top layer on it.
Heat the cream until steaming, pour over the chocolate, stir smooth, and pour over the top so it drips down the sides; chill 30 minutes before slicing.

ingredients: 1 tsp ground ginger and 1 tsp ground cinnamon
1/4 tsp ground nutmeg and 1/2 tsp salt
Vanilla ice cream or whipped cream, to serve
steps: Heat 720 ml (3 cups) of the milk in a heavy pan until steaming, then whisk in the cornmeal and cook over low heat, stirring, for 15 minutes until thick like porridge.
Remove from heat and stir in the molasses, sugar, butter, spices and salt, then whisk a little of the hot mixture into the egg and stir it all back in.
Pour into a buttered 1.5 litre (6 cup) baking dish and pour the remaining 240 ml (1 cup) cold milk over the top without stirring.
Bake at 150°C (300°F) for 2 to 2 1/2 hours until set but still slightly wobbly in the centre and a skin has formed.
Rest 30 minutes and serve warm with melting vanilla ice cream, as at Durgin-Park in Boston.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Pour the hot milk over the Grape-Nuts and let them soak 15 minutes to soften.
Whisk the eggs, sugar, vanilla and salt, then slowly whisk in the milk and cereal.
Pour into a buttered 1.5 litre (6 cup) baking dish, dust with nutmeg and set the dish in a larger pan filled with hot water halfway up the sides.
Bake at 165°C (325°F) for 50 to 60 minutes, stirring once after 20 minutes to spread the cereal, until a knife in the centre comes out clean.
Serve warm or chilled with whipped cream, a Rhode Island and Massachusetts diner classic.

ingredients: 315 g (2 1/2 cups) all-purpose flour and 1 tsp salt
225 g (1 cup / 2 sticks) cold unsalted butter, cubed
750 g (5 cups) wild Maine blueberries, fresh or frozen (substitute small cultivated blueberries)
30 g (1/4 cup) cornstarch or quick tapioca
1 tbsp lemon juice and 1/2 tsp lemon zest
1 tbsp butter, diced, and 1 tbsp milk plus 1 tbsp sugar for the top
steps: Rub the cold butter into the flour and salt until pea-sized, add ice water to bring it together, divide in two discs and chill 30 minutes.
Toss the blueberries with sugar, cornstarch, lemon juice, zest and cinnamon.
Roll one disc to line a 23 cm (9 in) pie plate, add the filling, dot with butter, and cover with the second rolled crust or a lattice; crimp the edges and cut steam vents.
Brush with milk, sprinkle with sugar and bake at 220°C (425°F) for 20 minutes, then at 175°C (350°F) for 40 minutes more until the crust is golden and the juices bubble thickly through the vents.
Cool at least 3 hours so the filling sets before slicing; serve with vanilla ice cream.

ingredients: 1 tbsp lemon juice and 1/4 tsp cinnamon
2 tsp baking powder and 1/2 tsp salt
1 tbsp sugar plus 2 tbsp (30 g) cold butter for the dumplings
Heavy cream or vanilla ice cream, to serve
steps: Simmer the blueberries, sugar, water, lemon juice and cinnamon in a wide lidded skillet over medium heat for 5 minutes until saucy.
Mix the flour, baking powder, salt and sugar, rub in the butter and stir in the milk to make a soft dumpling dough.

Drop spoonfuls of dough over the bubbling berries, cover tightly and simmer over low heat for 15 to 18 minutes without lifting the lid, until the dumplings are puffed and cooked through (the berries "grunt" as they steam).
Spoon into bowls warm and pour over cold cream.

ingredients: 315 g (2 1/2 cups) all-purpose flour and 1 tsp salt
225 g (1 cup / 2 sticks) cold unsalted butter, cubed
1.3 kg (3 lb / about 7) tart baking apples such as McIntosh, Cortland or Northern Spy, peeled and sliced
100 g (1/2 cup) sugar and 50 g (1/4 cup) brown sugar
2 tbsp flour and 1 tbsp lemon juice
1 tsp ground cinnamon and 1/4 tsp ground nutmeg
1 tbsp milk and 1 tbsp sugar for the top
225 g (8 oz) aged sharp Vermont cheddar (vegetarian-rennet), sliced
steps: Rub the butter into the flour and salt until pea-sized, add ice water to form a dough, divide in two discs and chill 30 minutes.
Toss the apples with the sugars, flour, lemon juice and spices.
Line a 23 cm (9 in) pie plate with one rolled crust, mound in the apples, top with the second crust, crimp, cut vents, brush with milk and sprinkle with sugar.
Bake at 220°C (425°F) for 20 minutes, then 175°C (350°F) for 40 to 45 minutes until golden and the apples are tender when pierced through a vent.
Serve warm slices with a thick slice of sharp cheddar on top or alongside, the Vermont way ("apple pie without cheese is like a kiss without a squeeze").

ingredients: 480 ml (2 cups) fresh apple cider, reduced to 120 ml (1/2 cup)
2 tsp baking powder and 1/2 tsp baking soda
1 tsp ground cinnamon, 1/4 tsp ground nutmeg and 1/2 tsp salt
100 g (1/2 cup) sugar and 50 g (1/4 cup) brown sugar
1.5 litres (6 cups) vegetable oil for frying
150 g (3/4 cup) sugar mixed with 1 tbsp cinnamon for coating
steps: Boil the cider in a saucepan over medium-high heat for 20 to 25 minutes until reduced to 120 ml (1/2 cup), then cool.
Beat the butter and sugars, beat in the eggs, then the reduced cider and buttermilk, and fold in the flour, leaveners, spices and salt to make a soft, sticky dough.
Pat out on a floured sheet to 1.5 cm (1/2 in) thick, chill 30 minutes, and cut with a doughnut cutter.
Fry in oil at 175°C (350°F) for about 1 1/2 minutes per side until deep brown and cooked through, then drain briefly.
Toss warm donuts in cinnamon sugar and serve with hot or cold cider, as at autumn orchards across New England.

ingredients: 1 tsp baking soda and 1/2 tsp salt
1 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon, 1 tsp ground ginger, 1/2 tsp cloves and 1/4 tsp nutmeg
60 g (1/2 cup) powdered sugar plus 1 tbsp milk for glaze
steps: Beat the butter and brown sugar until fluffy, then beat in the egg and molasses.
Mix in the flour, baking soda, salt and spices, then fold in the raisins; chill the soft dough 15 minutes.
Shape into two logs about 5 cm (2 in) wide on a lined baking sheet, spaced well apart, and flatten slightly.
Bake at 175°C (350°F) for 15 to 18 minutes until the edges are set but the centres still soft.
Cool 10 minutes, drizzle with the powdered sugar glaze and cut diagonally into bars, a sea-chest cookie that keeps well.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 1/2 tsp ground ginger, 1/2 tsp cloves, 1/2 tsp nutmeg and 1/4 tsp allspice
1 tsp baking soda and 1 1/2 tsp salt
75 ml (1/3 cup) water mixed with 2 tbsp dark rum (or extra water)
steps: Beat the butter and sugar until fluffy, then add the molasses and the rum water.
Whisk the flour, spices, baking soda and salt (the salt nods to the seawater used in Marblehead) and stir into the wet mix to make a soft, egg-free dough; chill 1 hour.
Roll out 6 mm (1/4 in) thick on a well-floured board and cut large 10 cm (4 in) rounds.
Sprinkle with sugar and bake at 190°C (375°F) for 10 to 12 minutes until set but still soft; cool on the sheet 5 minutes before moving.
Store in a tin, where these chewy, lily-pad-sized molasses cookies keep for weeks.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 180 g (3/4 cup) plain mashed potato, unseasoned
1 tsp vanilla extract and 1/4 tsp salt
340 g (12 oz / 2 cups) semi-sweet chocolate chips
2 tbsp coconut oil or vegetable shortening
steps: Warm the mashed potato and butter together over low heat until the butter melts, then stir in the powdered sugar, coconut, vanilla and salt to make a stiff dough.
Press into a buttered 23 x 33 cm (9 x 13 in) pan and chill 1 hour until firm, then cut into 2.5 cm (1 in) squares.
Melt the chocolate with the coconut oil in a bowl over barely simmering water, stirring, until smooth.
Dip each square in the chocolate with a fork, letting the excess drip off, and set on parchment until firm; these Maine potato candies keep chilled for a week.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 480 ml (2 cups) pure Vermont maple syrup, preferably dark or amber grade
A large pan of clean packed snow or finely shaved ice
steps: Heat the maple syrup and butter in a deep saucepan over medium heat and boil without stirring for 10 to 15 minutes until a candy thermometer reads 115°C (240°F), the soft-ball stage.
Pack the snow or shaved ice firmly into a baking pan.
Drizzle the hot syrup in thin ribbons over the snow, where it instantly sets into a chewy taffy.
Twirl the strands up with forks and eat right away, alternating with plain doughnuts and sour pickles to cut the sweetness, as at Vermont sugarhouse parties.

ingredients: 180 ml (3/4 cup) pure Vermont maple syrup, dark grade
1/4 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp maple or vanilla extract
steps: Whisk the cornstarch into a little of the milk, then heat with the rest of the milk, cream, maple syrup, sugar and salt over medium heat, stirring, for 6 to 8 minutes until slightly thickened.
Stir in the extract, strain into a bowl and chill thoroughly for at least 4 hours.
Churn in an ice-cream maker for 20 minutes until it reaches a thick soft-serve texture.
Pipe or swirl straight into sugar cones and serve immediately; a creemee is Vermont's lower-fat, extra-soft maple soft-serve.

ingredients: 2 tbsp coffee syrup (Autocrat brand in Rhode Island)
For homemade syrup: 240 ml (1 cup) strong brewed coffee and 200 g (1 cup) sugar
steps: If making syrup, simmer the strong coffee and sugar in a small pan over medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes until reduced by about a third and syrupy, then cool completely.
Stir 2 tablespoons of coffee syrup into the cold milk until evenly tan, adding more to taste.
Serve over ice or straight from the fridge; this is Rhode Island's official state drink.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 can (300 g / 10.5 oz) condensed cream of mushroom soup
300 g (2 cups) frozen green beans or mixed vegetables, thawed
1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper
900 g (2 lb) bag frozen tater tots
steps: Heat the oven to 190 C (375 F) and grease a 23 x 33 cm (9 x 13 in) baking dish.
Brown the ground beef and onion in a large skillet over medium-high heat for 8-10 minutes, breaking up the meat, until no pink remains; drain the fat and season with salt, pepper and garlic powder.
Stir in the soup, milk and green beans, then spread the mixture evenly in the baking dish and scatter the cheese over it.
Arrange the frozen tater tots in tight rows over the top, covering it completely.
Bake uncovered for 40-45 minutes until the tots are deep golden and crisp and the filling bubbles at the edges; rest 5 minutes and serve, Minnesota church-supper style, with ketchup on the side.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g (1.1 lb) pork tenderloin, cut into 4 equal pieces
2 large eggs beaten with 60 ml (1/4 cup) milk
120 g (2 cups) crushed saltine crackers or dry breadcrumbs
1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp pepper and 1/2 tsp garlic powder
vegetable oil for shallow frying, about 1 cm (1/2 in) deep
dill pickle chips, sliced onion, yellow mustard and lettuce, to serve
steps: Place each pork piece between plastic wrap and pound with a meat mallet to about 6 mm (1/4 in) thick and roughly 20 cm (8 in) across; the cutlet should dwarf the bun, as in Indiana and Iowa.
Season the flour with salt, pepper and garlic powder; dredge each cutlet in flour, dip in the egg wash, then press firmly into the cracker crumbs.
Heat the oil in a large skillet to 175 C (350 F) and fry the cutlets one or two at a time for 2-3 minutes per side until deep golden and the pork reaches 63 C (145 F).
Drain on a rack, then set each cutlet on a bun with mustard, pickles, onion and lettuce, leaving the crisp edges hanging out.

ingredients: dill pickle slices and yellow mustard, to serve
steps: Brown the beef in a large skillet over medium-high heat for 8 minutes, constantly breaking it into very fine crumbles with a potato masher; spoon off most of the fat.
Add the onion, broth, mustard, Worcestershire, sugar, salt and pepper.
Simmer uncovered over medium-low heat for 15 minutes, stirring, until the liquid is mostly absorbed but the meat is still moist.
Steam the buns briefly, then heap the loose meat on with a slotted spoon and top with pickles and mustard, Iowa Maid-Rite style; eat with a spoon handy for the fallen crumbs.

ingredients: 4 slices American cheese, each folded into a small square stack
1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper
grilled onions and dill pickles, to serve
steps: Mix the beef lightly with Worcestershire and garlic powder and divide into 8 thin patties about 11 cm (4.5 in) across.
Place a stack of cheese in the center of 4 patties, cover with the remaining patties and pinch the edges very well to seal so no cheese can escape.
Season both sides with salt and pepper and cook in a cast-iron skillet over medium heat for 5-6 minutes per side until the burger reaches 71 C (160 F) and the cheese inside is molten.
Rest 2 minutes, then serve on toasted buns with grilled onions and pickles, as in Minneapolis bars; warn diners the first bite holds scalding cheese.

ingredients: 600 g (1.3 lb) ground beef (80/20), divided into 4 balls
85 g (6 tbsp) salted Wisconsin butter, divided
4 slices American or mild cheddar cheese
steps: Melt 1 tbsp butter in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion for 8 minutes until soft and lightly golden; set aside.
Heat a heavy griddle or cast-iron pan over high heat, add the beef balls and smash each flat with a sturdy spatula; season with salt and pepper.
Cook 2-3 minutes until a deep brown crust forms, flip, add cheese and cook 2 minutes more until well done throughout.
Toast the buns, then spread the top bun generously with about 1 tbsp butter each so it melts into the bread.
Build each burger with onions and pickles and serve straight away, Wisconsin style, with a frozen custard on the side.

ingredients: 2 bottles (700 ml / 24 oz) lager or pilsner beer
6 brat buns or crusty hard rolls (semmel)
spicy brown or stone-ground mustard, to serve
steps: Melt the butter in a wide pot, add the onions and cook over medium heat for 5 minutes until starting to soften.
Add the beer and brats, bring to a bare simmer (do not boil hard or the casings split) and poach for 15 minutes.
Grill the brats over medium coals or a medium gas grill for 8-10 minutes, turning, until browned and the inside reaches 71 C (160 F).
Return the grilled brats to the beer-onion bath to keep warm until serving.
Serve in buns topped with the beer onions, sauerkraut and plenty of mustard, the classic Sheboygan tailgate way.

ingredients: 700 g (1.5 lb) cod or haddock fillets, cut into pieces (lake perch or bluegill are local choices)
150 g (1 1/4 cups) all-purpose flour, plus extra for dusting
300 ml (1 1/4 cups) cold lager beer or club soda
4 cups coleslaw and 4 slices rye bread, to serve
lemon wedges and tartar sauce, to serve
steps: Pat the fish very dry, season lightly with salt and dust in flour.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, salt and paprika, then whisk in the cold beer until just smooth and as thick as pancake batter.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 185 C (365 F); dip each piece of fish in the batter, let the excess drip off and fry in batches for 4-5 minutes until deep golden and the fish flakes easily.
Drain on a rack and serve hot with coleslaw, buttered rye bread, tartar sauce, lemon and potato pancakes or fries, as at a Wisconsin supper club or church Lenten fry.

ingredients: 700 g (1.5 lb) skinless walleye fillets (substitute yellow perch or tilapia)
2 large eggs beaten with 2 tbsp milk
80 g (1/2 cup) fine cornmeal or crushed saltines
1 tsp seasoned salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper
60 ml (1/4 cup) vegetable oil and 2 tbsp butter
lemon wedges and tartar sauce, to serve
steps: Pat the fillets dry and season with seasoned salt and pepper.
Mix the flour and cornmeal; dip each fillet in egg, then press into the coating.
Heat the oil and butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat until the butter foams, then fry the fillets for 3 minutes per side until golden and the flesh is opaque and flakes easily.
Drain briefly on paper towels and serve with lemon, tartar sauce and wild rice or potatoes, the way Minnesota lake cabins do a shore lunch.

ingredients: 1.4 kg (3 lb) ready-to-cook lutefisk, bought soaked and rinsed from a Scandinavian grocer or butcher
white sauce: 2 tbsp butter, 2 tbsp flour, 360 ml (1 1/2 cups) milk, pinch of nutmeg (optional)
allspice and black pepper, to serve
steps: Buy lutefisk already processed and soaked ready to cook; never treat fish with lye at home. Rinse it well in cold water and cut into serving pieces.

Heat the oven to 200 C (400 F), lay the fish skin side down in a glass baking dish, sprinkle with salt, cover tightly with foil and bake for 20-25 minutes until the flesh is opaque and flakes but is still slightly jelly-like; pour off the liquid.
Meanwhile, for the white sauce melt the butter, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the milk and simmer 3-4 minutes until thick; season with salt and nutmeg.
Serve the fish on warm plates with boiled potatoes, melted butter or white sauce, lefse and a dusting of allspice and pepper, as at a Norwegian-Lutheran church lutefisk dinner.

ingredients: 120 ml (1/2 cup) tomato soup or ketchup
steps: Heat the oven to 175 C (350 F). Mix the ham, pork, graham crumbs, eggs and milk with your hands until evenly combined.
Shape into 12 balls about the size of a small fist and set them in a single layer in a greased baking dish.
Whisk the brown sugar, tomato soup, vinegar and dry mustard until the sugar dissolves and pour over the balls.
Bake uncovered for 60 minutes, basting every 20 minutes, until glazed and the centers reach 71 C (160 F); serve with scalloped potatoes, the classic Iowa potluck plate.

ingredients: 1.4 kg (3 lb) bone-in chicken thighs and breasts
1 onion, 2 celery stalks and 2 carrots, roughly chopped
2 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper
250 g (2 cups) all-purpose flour for the noodles
steps: Simmer the chicken, water, onion, celery, carrots and salt over low heat for 60 minutes until the meat is tender; lift out the chicken, strain the broth and shred the meat, discarding skin and bones.
For the noodles, mix the flour with a pinch of salt, add the eggs and milk and knead into a stiff dough; rest 15 minutes, roll very thin, let dry 15 minutes, then cut into wide strips.
Bring the broth to a boil with the butter, drop in the noodles and cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring, until tender and the broth thickens from the flour.
Stir in the chicken and pepper and heat through; serve thick and stew-like over mashed potatoes, as at Indiana and Ohio church dinners.

4 cooked beef patties (450 g / 1 lb total) or thick slices of ham

225 g (2 cups) shredded sharp cheddar cheese
1 tsp Worcestershire sauce and 1/2 tsp dry mustard
steps: Bake the fries according to the package until crisp, and cook the patties in a skillet over medium-high heat for 4 minutes per side until well done.

ingredients: 3 tbsp chili powder and 1 tbsp cocoa powder
1 tsp each ground cinnamon, cumin and allspice, 1/4 tsp ground cloves
2 tbsp cider vinegar and 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce
finely shredded mild cheddar, diced onion and kidney beans, to serve
steps: Put the raw beef in a pot with the cold water and break it apart with a whisk until finely separated; this gives the signature fine texture (do not brown it).
Bring to a boil, then add the onions, tomato sauce, spices, cocoa, vinegar, Worcestershire, bay leaves and salt.
Simmer uncovered on low for 3 hours, stirring occasionally, until thickened; chill overnight if you can and lift off the solidified fat, then reheat.
Serve "ways" over spaghetti: 3-way with a mound of shredded cheddar, 4-way adds onions or beans, 5-way adds both, with oyster crackers on the side.

ingredients: 2 tsp salt and 1 tsp black pepper
steps: Bring the water, salt, pepper, allspice and bay leaves to a boil, stir in the steel-cut oats, cover and simmer on low for 2 hours, stirring often, until very thick.
Add the pork, beef and onion, breaking up the meat, and cook for 1 hour more, stirring often, until the mixture is stiff and the meat fully cooked; remove the bay leaves.
Pack into two loaf pans lined with plastic wrap and refrigerate overnight until firm.
Slice 1 cm (1/2 in) thick and fry in a little butter over medium heat for 5-6 minutes per side until deeply crisp; serve for breakfast with eggs, as in Cincinnati.

ingredients: 225 g (1/2 lb) ground beef (or ground beef heart, traditional)
1 small onion, minced, plus 1 onion finely diced for topping
1 tbsp chili powder, 1 tsp paprika, 1 tsp cumin
1 tbsp tomato paste and 1 tbsp flour
steps: Brown the ground beef with the minced onion in a saucepan over medium heat, mashing very fine, for 6 minutes until no pink remains.
Stir in the flour, spices and tomato paste for 1 minute, then add the broth and salt and simmer 25-30 minutes until a thin, meaty, loose sauce (Coney sauce, no beans).
Grill or griddle the hot dogs over medium heat for 5-6 minutes until snappy and heated through.
Put each dog in a steamed bun, add a stripe of yellow mustard, ladle on the Coney sauce and finish with diced raw onion, as at Lafayette and American Coney Island.

ingredients: 1 tsp instant yeast, 1 tsp sugar, 1 1/2 tsp salt
2 tbsp olive oil plus 1 tbsp butter for the pan
340 g (12 oz) Wisconsin brick cheese, cubed (substitute half mozzarella, half Monterey Jack)
1 garlic clove, grated, 1/2 tsp dried oregano and 1/2 tsp sugar
steps: Mix flour, water, yeast, sugar and salt into a sticky dough; rest 2 hours covered until doubled.
Grease a 25 x 35 cm (10 x 14 in) steel pan (blue-steel Detroit pan) with oil and butter, press the dough to the corners, and rest 20 minutes so it relaxes and puffs.
Simmer the tomatoes, garlic, oregano and sugar for 10 minutes into a thick sauce.
Heat the oven to 260 C (500 F). Scatter the brick cheese all the way to the pan edges so it melts down the sides and forms the caramelized "frico" crust.

Bake 12-15 minutes until the edges are dark brown and crisp; ladle two or three "racing stripes" of hot sauce down the top, sprinkle with parmesan, loosen the edges with a spatula and cut into squares.

ingredients: 400 g (3 1/4 cups) all-purpose flour and 1 tsp salt
170 g (3/4 cup) cold lard or butter, cubed
450 g (1 lb) beef skirt or chuck steak, cut in small cubes
2 medium potatoes, peeled and diced small
1 cup diced rutabaga ("baga") and 1 onion, diced
1 1/2 tsp salt and 1 tsp black pepper
1 egg yolk beaten with 1 tbsp milk (optional glaze)
steps: Rub the lard into the flour and salt until crumbly, add ice water to form a dough, divide into 6 and chill 30 minutes.
Toss the raw beef, potatoes, rutabaga and onion with salt and pepper.
Roll each dough piece into a 20 cm (8 in) circle, pile filling on one half, dot with butter, fold over and crimp the edge tightly; cut a small steam slit.
Brush with glaze and bake at 200 C (400 F) for 15 minutes, then at 175 C (350 F) for 45 minutes until golden and the beef is tender (check one with a skewer).
Rest 10 minutes and serve hot with ketchup or gravy, as Michigan Yoopers do, Cornish-miner style.

ingredients: 400 g (3 1/4 cups) all-purpose flour and 3 tbsp fine cornmeal
2 tsp instant yeast, 1 tsp sugar, 1 1/2 tsp salt
75 g (5 tbsp) melted butter plus 2 tbsp for the pan
280 g (10 oz) frozen spinach, thawed and squeezed dry
1 can (800 g / 28 oz) crushed tomatoes, drained slightly
2 garlic cloves, 1 tsp dried oregano, 1 tsp sugar
steps: Mix flour, cornmeal, yeast, sugar, salt, water and melted butter into a soft dough; knead 3 minutes and let rise 90 minutes.
Butter a 30 cm (12 in) deep-dish pan or cast-iron skillet and press the dough over the bottom and 5 cm (2 in) up the sides.
Layer in order: mozzarella slices on the dough, then the spinach, then the uncooked tomatoes mixed with garlic, oregano and sugar.
Sprinkle with parmesan and bake at 220 C (425 F) on the lowest rack for 30-35 minutes until the crust is golden and the sauce bubbles.
Rest 10 minutes so it sets before cutting into wedges and eating with a knife and fork, Chicago style.

180 ml (3/4 cup) tomato sauce with 1/2 tsp each oregano, fennel and garlic powder
1 green bell pepper and 1 onion, thinly sliced
1/2 tsp crushed red pepper and grated parmesan, to serve
steps: Mix the flour, water, yeast, salt, sugar and oil into a firm, dry dough and refrigerate overnight (a "cold ferment") for a cracker-like crust.
Roll very thin, about 3 mm (1/8 in), to a 35 cm (14 in) round and dock it with a fork; let it air-dry 30 minutes.
Spread the seasoned sauce right to the edge, then add mozzarella, peppers and onion.
Bake on a hot pizza stone or steel at 260 C (500 F) for 12-15 minutes until the crust is crisp and the cheese spotted brown.
Cut into small squares ("party cut") as Chicago bars do and serve with red pepper flakes and parmesan.

6 poppy seed hot dog buns, steamed
120 ml (1/2 cup) bright green sweet pickle relish

ingredients: 1.6 kg (3.5 lb) beef top round or sirloin tip roast
1 tbsp each dried oregano, basil and black pepper
1 tsp each garlic powder, onion powder, crushed red pepper
8 crusty Italian or French sub rolls
2 cups giardiniera (spicy pickled vegetables in oil)
2 green bell peppers, sliced and sauteed in olive oil (sweet peppers)

Cool the beef, then chill until firm so it can be sliced paper thin; keep the seasoned roasting juices ("gravy").
Slice the beef as thinly as possible, then warm the slices in the simmering gravy for 2-3 minutes.
Pile the beef into the rolls with tongs, top with hot giardiniera and/or sweet peppers, and spoon over extra gravy - or dip the whole sandwich ("dipped" or "wet") the Chicago way.

ingredients: 4 hot dog buns or soft rolls
steps: Cook the onions in oil with salt and sugar over medium-low heat for 30 minutes, stirring, until soft, sweet and caramelized.
Grill or griddle the sausages over medium heat for 10 minutes, turning, until charred, split and heated through to 71 C (160 F).
Put each sausage in a bun, smear with yellow mustard, heap with the grilled onions and add two whole sport peppers.
Serve with fries wrapped up in the same paper, like the Maxwell Street market stands in Chicago.

ingredients: 2 large green plantains, peeled and halved crosswise
300 g (10 oz) thin-sliced beef steak (sirloin or skirt)
2 garlic cloves, minced, plus 1 tbsp olive oil
lettuce, tomato slices and 2 tbsp mayonnaise
steps: Fry the plantain halves in 2 cm (3/4 in) of oil at 165 C (325 F) for 4 minutes until tender but pale; drain.
Place each plantain between two cutting boards (or under a heavy pan) and press flat to about 1 cm (1/2 in); fry again at 185 C (365 F) for 3 minutes until crisp and golden, then salt.
Season the steak with adobo and sear in a hot skillet for 1-2 minutes per side until cooked through; top with cheese to melt.
Mix the garlic with olive oil and mayonnaise; brush onto the plantain "bread", then build with steak, lettuce and tomato as in Chicago's Puerto Rican Humboldt Park.

1 tsp dried oregano and 1 tsp salt, plus pepper
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat and brown the seasoned chicken skin-side down for 6-8 minutes; remove, then brown the potato wedges for 6 minutes.
Add the garlic and oregano for 1 minute, then pour in the wine and broth, scraping the pan.
Return the chicken skin-side up, and roast at 220 C (425 F) for 30-35 minutes until the potatoes are tender and the chicken reaches 74 C (165 F).
Scatter the peas over for the last 5 minutes, sprinkle with parsley and serve with the garlic-wine pan juices, as in Chicago's Italian steakhouses.

lemon wedges and crusty bread, to serve

Dot and press the crumb butter over the shrimp in an even layer.
Bake for 15-18 minutes until the shrimp are pink and opaque and the topping is golden; serve with lemon and bread to mop up the garlic butter, a Chicago classic since the early 1900s.

ingredients: 2.3 kg (5 lb) beef brisket point (the fatty end)
3 tbsp coarse black pepper and 2 tbsp kosher salt
2 tbsp brown sugar, 1 tbsp paprika, 2 tsp garlic powder
240 ml (1 cup) Kansas City barbecue sauce
hickory or oak wood for smoking

Smoke over hickory at 120 C (250 F) for 7-8 hours until the internal temperature reaches 90 C (195 F) and a probe slides in easily.
Cut the point into 3-4 cm (1 1/2 in) cubes and toss in a foil pan with the barbecue sauce, honey and butter.
Return to the smoker uncovered for 1 1/2-2 hours until the sauce caramelizes and the cubes are sticky and dark at the edges.
Serve on white bread with pickles and onions, with baked beans and fries, Kansas City style.

Heat the oil to 175 C (350 F) and fry the ravioli in batches for 2-3 minutes, turning once, until golden brown and the filling is hot.

180 ml (3/4 cup) tomato sauce with 1 tsp dried oregano and 1/2 tsp sugar
225 g (8 oz) Provel cheese, shredded (substitute processed white cheddar + provolone + Swiss)
1 green bell pepper and 1 small onion, diced

ingredients: 150 g (5 oz) cooked chicken or shrimp, chopped (egg foo young filling)
1 tbsp soy sauce and 1/4 tsp salt
4 tbsp mayonnaise, 8 dill pickle slices, 4 lettuce leaves, 4 tomato slices
steps: Beat the eggs with soy sauce and salt, then stir in the bean sprouts, onion and chicken.

Spread the bread with mayonnaise and sandwich each egg foo young patty with pickles, lettuce and tomato, as served in St. Louis Chinese-American takeouts.

ingredients: 4 pork shoulder (Boston butt) steaks, 2 cm (3/4 in) thick
1 tbsp salt, 1 tsp pepper, 1 tsp garlic powder, 1 tbsp paprika
360 ml (1 1/2 cups) sweet tomato barbecue sauce (Maull's style)
240 ml (1 cup) lager beer or water
steps: Season the steaks with salt, pepper, garlic powder and paprika.
Grill over medium-high heat for 4-5 minutes per side until well marked.
Layer the steaks in a foil pan with the onion, pour over the barbecue sauce mixed with beer, cover with foil and set on the cooler side of the grill (or in a 160 C / 325 F oven).
Braise for 1 1/2 hours until fork tender and over 71 C (160 F), then serve with the sauce, potato salad and white bread, a St. Louis summer cookout staple.

50 g (1/2 cup) shredded cheddar and 2 tbsp diced onion
steps: Cook the hash browns in 1 tbsp butter in a skillet over medium heat for 10-12 minutes, flipping once, until golden and crisp; season.
Cook the seasoned patties in another pan for 4 minutes per side until well done.
Fry the eggs in the remaining butter to your liking.
Build each plate in layers, St. Louis diner style: hash browns, burger patty, two eggs, then smother with hot chili, cheese and onion; serve with toast.

ingredients: 1.8 kg (4 lb) whole chicken, cut into pieces
900 g (2 lb) beef chuck or oxtail
2 onions, chopped, and 4 celery stalks, sliced
300 g (2 cups) frozen peas and 300 g (2 cups) frozen corn
1 tbsp salt, 1 tsp pepper, 2 bay leaves
steps: Simmer the chicken and beef in the water with salt and bay leaves for 2 hours until very tender; lift out, discard bones and skin and shred the meat.
Return the meat to the broth with onions, celery, carrots, potatoes, cabbage and tomatoes and simmer 1 1/2 hours, stirring often.

Serve hot with oyster crackers, as at Green Bay church picnics where it is cooked in giant kettles (scale up as needed).

ingredients: 160 g (1 cup) Minnesota wild rice (manoomin), rinsed
60 g (4 tbsp) butter and 30 g (1/4 cup) flour
1 onion, 2 carrots and 2 celery stalks, diced
300 g (2 cups) cooked chicken, shredded (or diced ham)
1 tsp dried thyme, 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp pepper
steps: Simmer the wild rice in 720 ml (3 cups) of the broth for 45 minutes until the grains split open and are tender.
In a soup pot, melt the butter and cook the onion, carrots, celery and mushrooms over medium heat for 8 minutes until soft.
Stir in the flour for 1 minute, then gradually whisk in the remaining broth and simmer 5 minutes until thickened.
Add the rice with its liquid, chicken, thyme, salt and pepper; stir in the cream and heat gently 5 minutes without boiling. Serve with crusty bread.

ingredients: 1 onion, 1 carrot and 1 celery stalk, finely diced
360 ml (12 oz) lager or Wisconsin amber beer
450 g (1 lb) sharp Wisconsin cheddar, shredded
1 tsp Dijon mustard and 1/2 tsp smoked paprika
steps: Melt the butter in a pot and cook the onion, carrot and celery over medium heat for 8 minutes until soft.
Stir in the flour for 2 minutes, then slowly whisk in the broth and beer and simmer 10 minutes until thickened.
Add the milk and heat until steaming, then reduce to low and add the cheese one handful at a time, stirring until melted and smooth (do not boil).
Season with mustard, paprika and Worcestershire, and serve with popcorn or soft pretzels on top, the Wisconsin way.

ingredients: 450 g (1 lb) fresh Wisconsin white cheddar cheese curds (squeaky, day-old at most)
1 tsp baking powder, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp garlic powder
240 ml (1 cup) cold lager beer or milk
steps: Chill the curds in the freezer for 15 minutes so they hold their shape.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, salt and garlic powder, then whisk in the cold beer to a smooth, thin batter.
Heat the oil to 190 C (375 F); dip the curds in batter, let the excess drip off and fry in small batches for 1-2 minutes until golden and puffed, before the cheese leaks.
Drain on a rack, salt lightly and serve immediately with ranch dressing, as at the Wisconsin State Fair.
