ingredients: 450 g (1 lb) sauerkraut, drained, squeezed dry and finely chopped
2 tbsp chopped parsley and 1 tsp dry mustard
60 g (1/2 cup) flour, 2 eggs beaten, 120 g (1 cup) breadcrumbs for coating
steps: Brown the sausage and onion in a skillet over medium heat for 8 minutes until fully cooked; drain the fat.
Mix with the sauerkraut, cream cheese, parsley and dry mustard, then chill at least 1-2 hours until firm.
Roll into 2.5 cm (1 in) balls, roll in flour, dip in egg and coat with breadcrumbs.
Fry at 175 C (350 F) for 2-3 minutes until deep golden; drain and serve with spicy mustard, an Akron, Ohio party snack.

ingredients: 270 g (9 cups) Rice Chex cereal (or other crisp rice square cereal)
steps: Put the cereal in a very large bowl.
Microwave the chocolate chips, peanut butter and butter for 1 minute, then in 30-second bursts, stirring, until smooth; stir in the vanilla.
Pour over the cereal and fold gently until every piece is coated.
Tip into a large zip-top bag with the powdered sugar, seal and shake until coated; spread on a tray to cool, Minnesota-potluck style.

ingredients: 100 g (1/2 cup) popcorn kernels, popped (about 4 l / 16 cups)
200 g (1 cup) sugar, 60 ml (1/4 cup) light corn syrup and 60 g (4 tbsp) butter
1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp baking soda
30 g (2 tbsp) butter and 2 tbsp milk for the cheese coating
steps: Divide the popcorn between two large bowls. Heat the oven to 120 C (250 F).

Boil the sugar, corn syrup, 4 tbsp butter and salt for 4 minutes, stir in the baking soda and pour over one bowl; toss, spread on a tray and bake 45-60 minutes, stirring every 15, until crisp caramel corn.
Melt 2 tbsp butter with the milk, toss with the second bowl of popcorn, then sprinkle with cheese powder and toss until evenly orange.

ingredients: 12 blue corn tortillas (15 cm / 6 in); sub yellow corn tortillas
720 ml (3 cups) New Mexico red chile sauce (see recipe)
340 g (12 oz, 3 cups) shredded cheddar or Monterey Jack cheese
120 ml (1/2 cup) vegetable oil for softening tortillas
steps: Warm the red chile sauce in a saucepan over low heat and heat the oil in a small skillet over medium-high heat.
Dip each tortilla in the hot oil for about 5 seconds per side until pliable but not crisp, then drain on paper towels.
On each ovenproof plate lay one tortilla, spoon over chile sauce, then sprinkle cheese and onion; repeat to make a stack three tortillas high and finish with sauce and cheese.
Bake the plates at 200°C (400°F) for 8–10 minutes until the cheese bubbles, then top with lettuce and tomato and serve with pinto beans and Spanish rice.

ingredients: 8 large fresh New Mexico green chiles (Hatch or Anaheim), roasted and peeled with stems left on
225 g (8 oz) Monterey Jack or asadero cheese, cut into 8 sticks
65 g (1/2 cup) all-purpose flour, plus extra for dredging
720 ml (3 cups) vegetable oil for frying
480 ml (2 cups) green or red chile sauce, warmed, to serve
steps: Slit each roasted chile lengthwise, scrape out the seeds and slip a stick of cheese inside, then pat dry and dredge lightly in flour.
Beat the egg whites to stiff peaks, whisk the yolks with milk, flour, salt and baking powder into a batter, and fold in the whites until just combined.
Heat the oil in a deep skillet to 180°C (350°F), dip each chile in the batter and fry 2–3 minutes per side until puffed and golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve immediately smothered in warm red or green chile, with beans and rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 900 g (2 lb) pork shoulder, cut into large chunks
480 ml (2 cups) New Mexico red chile sauce (see recipe)
900 g (2 lb, about 4 cups) masa harina (prepared tamale masa) mixed with 720 ml (3 cups) warm pork broth
225 g (1 cup) lard or vegetable shortening
30 dried corn husks, soaked in hot water 30 minutes
steps: Simmer the pork in salted water for about 2 hours until fork-tender, shred it and mix with the red chile sauce and oregano; save the broth for the masa.
Beat the lard until fluffy, then beat in the masa harina, broth, baking powder and salt for 5 minutes until a small piece floats in cold water.
Spread 3 tbsp masa thinly over the wide half of each drained husk, add 1 heaped tbsp of red chile pork, fold the sides in and fold up the narrow end.
Stand the tamales upright in a steamer over simmering water, cover and steam 75–90 minutes until the masa pulls cleanly away from the husk; rest 10 minutes before serving with extra red chile.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 450 g (1 lb) cooked shredded beef (machaca) or chicken
115 g (4 oz, 1 cup) shredded Monterey Jack or cheddar
1 can (115 g / 4 oz) diced green chiles
720 ml (3 cups) vegetable oil for frying
120 ml (1/2 cup) sour cream and 1 cup guacamole, to serve
steps: Warm the beef with the onion and green chiles in a skillet over medium heat for 5 minutes until hot through.
Warm the tortillas so they are pliable, spread each with beans, add a quarter of the meat and cheese, then fold in the sides and roll up tightly, securing with toothpicks.
Heat the oil in a deep pan to 180°C (350°F) and fry the chimichangas seam-side down first, 2–3 minutes per side, until deep golden and crisp.
Drain, remove toothpicks, and serve the Tucson favourite topped with sour cream, guacamole, shredded lettuce and red or green enchilada sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 900 g (2 lb) beef top round or flank, sliced very thinly with the grain
steps: Rub the beef with garlic, lime juice, salt and pepper, lay the slices on a wire rack over a tray and refrigerate uncovered overnight.
Dry the beef in the oven at its lowest setting, about 75°C (170°F), with the door slightly ajar for 4–5 hours until stiff and leathery (traditionally it is sun-dried in Tucson's desert air).
Pound or shred the dried beef into fine threads, then fry it in oil with the onion over medium-high heat for 5 minutes until crisp at the edges.
Add the tomatoes and green chiles and cook 5 minutes more until saucy, then serve as a filling for burritos, enchiladas or chimichangas with flour tortillas.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 900 g (2 lb) pork shoulder, cut into 2.5 cm (1 in) cubes
12 roasted New Mexico green chiles, peeled and chopped (about 1.5 cups); sub frozen roasted Hatch chile
4 medium potatoes (about 680 g / 1.5 lb), peeled and cubed
steps: Toss the pork with flour and salt, then brown in oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat for 8 minutes, in batches.
Add the onion and garlic and cook 4 minutes until soft, then add cumin, stock and half the green chile and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat, cover and simmer for 45 minutes, then add the potatoes and remaining chile and simmer 30 minutes more until the pork is tender and the potatoes are soft.
Taste for salt and serve in bowls with warm flour tortillas.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 450 g (1 lb) dried posole (nixtamalized corn), soaked overnight; sub 2 cans (850 g / 30 oz) hominy
3 dried New Mexico red chile pods, stemmed and seeded, or 2 tbsp red chile powder
steps: Drain the soaked posole, cover with the water in a large pot and simmer for 2 hours until the kernels burst open.
Add the pork, onion, garlic, chile pods and oregano and simmer gently 1.5–2 hours more until the pork is tender and the corn is chewy-soft.
Season with salt (add it only at the end so the corn softens), skim excess fat, and remove the chile pods if you prefer.
Serve in bowls with red chile sauce on the side, chopped onion, lime and oregano, as at Christmas Eve in northern New Mexico.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.4 kg (3 lb) bone-in mutton or lamb shoulder, cut into chunks
2 ears fresh corn, cut into rounds; or 1 cup frozen corn
steps: Put the mutton in a large pot with the water and salt, bring to a boil over high heat and skim the foam from the surface.
Reduce to a gentle simmer, cover and cook for 1.5 hours until the meat is starting to come off the bone.
Add the potatoes, carrots, onion, celery and corn and simmer 30–40 minutes until the vegetables are tender and the meat is very soft.
Season with pepper and serve hot in bowls with Navajo fry bread or kneel-down bread on the side.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 225 g (8 oz) breakfast chorizo or bacon, chopped
240 ml (1 cup) red or green chile sauce (or both, "Christmas")
steps: Fry the potatoes in oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat for 12–15 minutes, turning, until crisp and cooked through; season with salt.
In another pan cook the chorizo or bacon over medium heat for 6–8 minutes until fully cooked and browned, then add the eggs and stir gently until softly set.
Warm the tortillas, then fill each with potatoes, eggs and meat, cheese and a spoonful of chile, and roll up.
Serve wrapped in foil to eat on the go, or plated and smothered in more chile with melted cheese on top.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 480 ml (2 cups) red or green chile sauce, warmed
480 ml (2 cups) refried pinto beans, warmed
steps: Fry the tortillas one at a time in hot oil over medium-high heat for 20 seconds per side until softened, and drain.
In the same pan fry the eggs over medium heat for 3–4 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks are as done as you like; season with salt.
Put two overlapping tortillas on each warm plate, spread with beans, top with two eggs and ladle chile sauce over.
Scatter with cheese, place under a hot grill for 1 minute to melt, and serve with hash-brown potatoes.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 bolillo-style hot dog rolls, split on top
240 ml (1 cup) cooked pinto beans, warmed
steps: Wrap each hot dog tightly in a slice of bacon in a spiral, securing the ends with toothpicks.
Cook on a griddle over medium heat for 10–12 minutes, turning, until the bacon is crisp all over and the dogs are hot through.
Warm the soft rolls on the griddle without browning, then nestle a dog in each and spoon in beans, onion and tomato.
Zigzag with mayo, mustard and salsa verde and serve with a roasted güero chile on the side, Tucson-style.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 very large flour tortilla (35 cm / 14 in)
170 g (6 oz, 1.5 cups) shredded cheddar or longhorn cheese
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F), brush the tortilla on both sides with butter and lay it flat on a pizza pan.
Bake 3–4 minutes until it begins to crisp and bubble, then pop any large air pockets.
Cover evenly with cheese and green chiles and bake 4–5 minutes more until the cheese is melted and the edges are golden and crisp.
Sprinkle with green onion, cut into wedges and serve straight away with salsa.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 3 medium zucchini or Mexican grey squash (calabacitas), diced (about 4 cups)
2 ears sweet corn, kernels cut off (about 1.5 cups)
55 g (2 oz, 1/2 cup) shredded Monterey Jack
steps: Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat and cook the onion and garlic for 3 minutes until soft.
Add the squash and corn, season with salt and sauté 6–8 minutes until the squash is just tender but not mushy.
Stir in the green chile, then scatter the cheese over, cover and leave 1 minute to melt.
Serve as a side with enchiladas or grilled meats, or as a filling for tortillas.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 225 g (8 oz, 1.5 cups) chicos (horno-roasted dried sweet corn); sub dried hominy
2 l (8 cups) water or vegetable stock
steps: Rinse the chicos and soak them overnight in plenty of cold water, then drain.
Simmer in the water or stock in a covered pot for 2.5–3 hours until the kernels are tender but still chewy, topping up with water as needed.
Meanwhile, cook the onion and garlic in oil over medium heat for 5 minutes, stir in the chile powder and oregano for 30 seconds, and add to the pot for the last 30 minutes.
Season with salt and serve the smoky corn as a side with beans and tortillas, as it is eaten in northern New Mexican villages.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 12 dried New Mexico red chile pods (about 70 g / 2.5 oz), stemmed and seeded
950 ml (4 cups) hot water or vegetable stock
steps: Rinse the chile pods, toast them in a dry skillet over medium heat for 30 seconds per side until fragrant (don't let them blacken), then soak in the hot water for 20 minutes.
Blend the pods with 3 cups of soaking water and the garlic until completely smooth, then strain through a sieve to remove skins.
Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat, whisk in the flour for 1 minute to make a light roux, then whisk in the chile purée, oregano, cumin and salt.
Simmer 15–20 minutes, stirring, until the sauce coats a spoon, adding water if too thick; use on enchiladas, burritos and eggs, or freeze in portions.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 375 g (3 cups) all-purpose flour (Blue Bird flour is the traditional choice)
720 ml (3 cups) vegetable oil or shortening for frying
steps: Mix the flour, baking powder and salt in a bowl, then add the warm water and melted shortening and knead briefly into a soft, slightly sticky dough.
Cover with a cloth and rest 30 minutes, then divide into 6 balls and stretch each by hand into a round about 18 cm (7 in) across and 1 cm thick, poking a small hole in the centre.
Heat the oil in a deep skillet to 190°C (375°F) and fry each round 1–2 minutes per side until puffed and golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with honey and powdered sugar, alongside mutton stew, or as the base for Navajo tacos.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 1/4 tsp (1 packet / 7 g) active dry yeast
steps: Dissolve the yeast and sugar in the warm water and leave 10 minutes until foamy, then mix in the flour, salt and shortening and knead for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover and let rise in a warm spot for about 1.5 hours until doubled.
Punch down and shape into round loaves, or the traditional Pueblo "bear claw" shape by flattening a round, folding it in half and cutting slits along the curved edge; rise again 30–40 minutes.
Bake in a hot horno (adobe oven) or a conventional oven at 200°C (400°F) for 35–40 minutes until deep golden and hollow-sounding when tapped underneath; cool before slicing.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 720 ml (3 cups) vegetable oil for frying
steps: Mix the flour, baking powder and salt, rub in the shortening with your fingertips, then stir in the warm milk and knead 2 minutes into a smooth dough.
Cover and rest 30 minutes, then roll out 3 mm (1/8 in) thick and cut into 8 cm (3 in) squares or triangles.
Heat the oil to 200°C (400°F) and fry a few at a time, spooning hot oil over the tops so they puff into hollow pillows, about 1 minute per side until golden.
Drain and serve hot with honey to drizzle inside, or split and stuff with beans and carne adovada and smother with chile.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 225 g (1 cup) lard (traditional); sub cold butter or vegetable shortening
150 g (3/4 cup) sugar, plus 100 g (1/2 cup) for coating
60 ml (1/4 cup) brandy or orange juice
steps: Beat the lard and 3/4 cup sugar until light and fluffy, then beat in the egg and anise seed.
Mix the flour, baking powder and salt and add to the creamed mixture alternately with the brandy or juice to make a stiff dough.
Roll the dough out 6 mm (1/4 in) thick on a floured surface and cut into stars or the traditional fleur-de-lis shapes.

Mix the remaining sugar with the cinnamon, dip the tops of the cookies in it and bake at 180°C (350°F) for 10–12 minutes until just golden on the bottom; cool on a rack. These are New Mexico's official state cookie, baked for Christmas.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Whisk 1 cup of the milk with the flour, egg yolks and salt until smooth, and heat the remaining milk with the sugar in a saucepan over medium heat until steaming.
Whisk the yolk mixture into the hot milk and cook, stirring constantly, for 8–10 minutes until it thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon (about 80°C / 175°F); stir in the vanilla.
Beat the egg whites to stiff peaks and gently fold them into the hot custard so they cook in its heat.
Spoon into dishes, dust with cinnamon or nutmeg and chill at least 1 hour before serving.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 60 g (1/2 cup) roasted blue corn meal (harinilla); sub fine blue corn meal
950 ml (4 cups) milk or water (or half and half)
steps: Whisk the blue corn meal into 1 cup of cold milk or water until smooth with no lumps.
Bring the remaining liquid to a simmer in a saucepan over medium heat, then whisk in the corn slurry.
Cook, whisking constantly, for 8–10 minutes until smooth and thick enough to coat a spoon.
Stir in the honey, cinnamon and salt and serve hot in mugs, as Pueblo and Hispanic families drink it for breakfast on cold mornings.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 6 ripe prickly pear fruits (tunas), peeled with gloves; sub 120 ml (1/2 cup) prickly pear syrup
180 ml (3/4 cup) fresh lemon juice (about 4 lemons)
ice and lemon slices, to serve
steps: Wearing gloves, cut off the ends of the prickly pears, slit the skin lengthwise and peel it away, then blend the magenta flesh and strain through a fine sieve to remove the seeds.
Heat the sugar with 1 cup of the water in a small pan for 3–4 minutes, stirring, until dissolved to make a simple syrup; cool.
Stir together the prickly pear juice, lemon juice, syrup and remaining water in a pitcher and taste for sweetness.
Serve over plenty of ice with lemon slices, the vivid pink cooler of Arizona's Sonoran Desert.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 680 g (1.5 lb) firm white fish (rockfish, cod or mahi-mahi), cut into strips
125 g (1 cup) all-purpose flour, plus extra for dredging
240 ml (1 cup) cold Mexican lager or sparkling water
120 ml (1/2 cup) crema or mayonnaise thinned with 2 tbsp lime juice
720 ml (3 cups) vegetable oil for frying
steps: Whisk the flour, salt and cold beer or sparkling water into a smooth batter about as thick as pancake batter.
Heat the oil to 190°C (375°F), dredge the fish strips in flour, dip in batter and fry 3–4 minutes until crisp, golden and the fish flakes easily.
Warm the tortillas on a dry griddle and double them up.
Fill each with fried fish, cabbage, a drizzle of white sauce and pico de gallo, and serve with lime wedges, San Diego and Baja style.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 680 g (1.5 lb) carne asada, cooked and chopped (see California Burrito marinade), or al pastor
480 ml (2 cups) whole pinto or black beans, warmed
115 g (4 oz, 1 cup) shredded Monterey Jack
240 ml (1 cup) pico de gallo or salsa roja
steps: Steam the tortillas briefly (or warm on a griddle covered with a lid) until soft and stretchy, scattering cheese on to melt.
Lay rice, beans and hot meat in a line down the centre, then top with guacamole, sour cream and salsa.
Fold the bottom over the filling, tuck in the sides and roll up very tightly, then wrap in foil.
Cut in half through the foil and serve as in San Francisco's Mission District taquerias, with chips and salsa.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 680 g (1.5 lb) skirt or flank steak
60 ml (1/4 cup) orange juice and 3 tbsp lime juice
3 garlic cloves, minced and 1 tsp ground cumin
115 g (4 oz, 1 cup) shredded cheddar or Jack
steps: Marinate the steak in the citrus juices, garlic, cumin and salt in the refrigerator for 2 hours.
Bake the fries according to the package until very crisp, and grill the steak over high heat for 4–5 minutes per side to medium, rest 5 minutes and chop small.
Warm the tortillas, then fill each with carne asada, a generous handful of fries, cheese, guacamole, sour cream and pico de gallo.
Roll up tightly, wrap in foil and serve hot, the San Diego taco-shop favourite.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 450 g (1 lb) carne asada, marinated and grilled (see California Burrito), chopped
170 g (6 oz, 1.5 cups) shredded cheddar and Jack cheese
steps: Bake or fry the fries until very crisp and spread them on an ovenproof platter.
Scatter the hot chopped carne asada and cheese over the fries and bake at 200°C (400°F) for 5 minutes until the cheese melts.
Spoon over dollops of guacamole and sour cream, then the pico de gallo and cilantro.
Serve at once with forks, San Diego late-night style.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 680 g (1.5 lb) beef short rib or ribeye, sliced very thin (bulgogi cut)
2 tbsp brown sugar and 1 tbsp sesame oil
4 garlic cloves, minced and 1 tbsp grated ginger
2 cups shredded napa cabbage and romaine tossed with 1 tbsp rice vinegar
cilantro, sliced green onions, sesame seeds and lime wedges
steps: Mix the soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil, pear, garlic, ginger and 1 tbsp gochujang and marinate the beef in it for 2 hours in the refrigerator.
Cook the beef in batches in a very hot skillet or grill pan for 2–3 minutes until caramelised at the edges and cooked through.
Warm the tortillas on a griddle and thin the remaining gochujang with a little lime juice and oil to make a drizzle.
Fill the tortillas with beef, slaw and kimchi, drizzle with sauce, and finish with cilantro, green onion and sesame, Los Angeles food-truck style.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 green bell peppers or jalapeños, sliced
ketchup, mustard and mayonnaise, to serve
steps: Wrap each hot dog tightly in bacon in a spiral and secure with toothpicks.
Heat the oil on a griddle over medium heat and cook the onion and peppers 10–12 minutes until soft and charred in spots, pushing them to one side.
Cook the wrapped dogs on the griddle 10–12 minutes, turning, until the bacon is crisp and fully cooked.
Toast the buns on the griddle, add the dogs, pile on the onions and peppers and finish with ketchup, mustard and mayo, as sold from LA street carts ("danger dogs").
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.4 kg (3 lb) beef top round or rib roast
2 tsp salt and 1 tsp black pepper
steps: Season the beef, sear it in oil in a roasting pan on the stove over high heat until browned all over, then add onion, stock and wine.
Roast at 160°C (325°F) for about 1.5–2 hours until 57°C (135°F) inside for medium-rare, then rest 15 minutes.
Strain and simmer the pan juices for 10 minutes to make the jus, and slice the beef paper-thin.
Dip the cut sides of each roll in the jus, pile with beef, and serve with a cup of jus for dipping and hot mustard, as at Philippe's and Cole's in downtown Los Angeles.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 tbsp red wine vinegar mixed with 2 tbsp oil, for basting
2 cups red oak (or oak) wood chunks for the fire
steps: Rub the tri-tip all over with salt, pepper, garlic powder and parsley and let it stand 1 hour at room temperature.
Build a fire with red oak (coast live oak) wood or add oak chunks to charcoal, and let it burn down to glowing coals.
Grill the tri-tip over medium-high heat for 30–40 minutes, turning and basting with vinegar-oil every 5 minutes, until 54–57°C (130–135°F) inside.
Rest 10 minutes, slice thinly across the grain, and serve with pinquito beans, fresh salsa, garlic bread and green salad, the Santa Maria barbecue plate.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 cooked Dungeness crab, cleaned and cracked into pieces
450 g (1 lb) clams or mussels, scrubbed
450 g (1 lb) firm white fish (halibut or rockfish), cut into chunks
240 ml (1 cup) dry white wine and 480 ml (2 cups) fish stock
1 tsp red pepper flakes, 1 bay leaf, fresh basil and parsley
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook onion, fennel and garlic for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the wine and boil 2 minutes, then add tomatoes, stock, pepper flakes and bay leaf and simmer 25 minutes.
Add the clams and crab, cover and cook 5 minutes, then add fish and shrimp and cook 4–5 minutes more until the shells open, the shrimp are pink and the fish flakes; discard any unopened shells.
Stir in basil and parsley and serve in big bowls with San Francisco sourdough bread, the Italian fishermen's stew of North Beach.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Clam Chowder in a Sourdough Bread Bowl

ingredients: 900 g (2 lb) fresh clams, steamed and chopped, plus their liquor; or 3 cans (185 g / 6.5 oz) chopped clams with juice
3 tbsp butter and 30 g (1/4 cup) flour
480 ml (2 cups) whole milk and 240 ml (1 cup) cream
steps: Cook the bacon in a pot over medium heat until crisp, add butter, onion and celery and cook 5 minutes, then stir in the flour for 2 minutes.
Gradually whisk in the clam juice and liquor, add potatoes and thyme and simmer 15 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Add milk, cream and clams and heat gently for 5 minutes without boiling; season with salt and pepper.
Cut a lid from each boule, hollow out the crumb leaving a 2 cm wall, toast the bowls 5 minutes at 180°C (350°F), and ladle in the chowder, Fisherman's Wharf style.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 large eggs, beaten with 2 tbsp milk
30 g (1/4 cup) flour and 30 g (1/2 cup) fine cracker crumbs
steps: Fry the bacon in a skillet over medium heat until crisp, remove and keep warm, leaving the fat.
Dredge the oysters in flour, dip in a little of the egg and roll in cracker crumbs, then fry in the bacon fat with the butter for 1–2 minutes per side until golden and cooked through.
Pour the remaining eggs around the oysters, lower the heat and cook 3–4 minutes, lifting the edges, until set like a frittata.
Top with the bacon and parsley and serve the Gold Rush dish of Placerville ("Hangtown") with sourdough toast.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 thick slices sourdough or whole-grain bread
4 radishes, thinly sliced, and microgreens to garnish
steps: Toast the bread until deeply golden and crisp.
Mash the avocado with the lemon juice and a pinch of salt, leaving it slightly chunky.
Spread thickly on the toast, drizzle with olive oil and top with flaky salt, pepper flakes, radishes and microgreens.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 60 g (4 tbsp) butter and 30 g (1/4 cup) flour
steps: Cook the spaghetti in salted boiling water until just short of al dente, then drain.
Melt the butter in a large pan over medium heat, sauté the mushrooms for 6 minutes, stir in the flour, then whisk in the stock, cream and sherry and simmer 5 minutes until thick.
Stir in the chicken, pasta and half the Parmesan, season, and spread in a buttered baking dish.
Top with breadcrumbs and remaining Parmesan and bake at 190°C (375°F) for 25 minutes until bubbling and golden; the dish was named in San Francisco for opera singer Luisa Tetrazzini.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 450 g (1 lb) thin egg noodles or spaghetti
steps: Cook the noodles in boiling water until al dente, drain and keep warm.
Melt the butter in a large pan over medium-low heat and cook the garlic 3–4 minutes until fragrant and pale golden, not brown.
Stir in the oyster sauce, fish sauce and sugar, add the noodles and toss over the heat for 2 minutes to coat.
Toss with Parmesan, top with green onion and serve with roasted Dungeness crab, the Vietnamese-American dish made famous by Thanh Long.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 60 ml (1/4 cup) rice vinegar, 2 tbsp sugar, 1 tsp salt
225 g (8 oz) cooked crab meat or surimi (imitation crab) sticks
2 tbsp toasted sesame seeds or masago
soy sauce, wasabi and pickled ginger, to serve
steps: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear, cook with 480 ml (2 cups) water, then fold in the warmed vinegar, sugar and salt and cool to room temperature.
Lay a nori sheet on a plastic-wrapped bamboo mat, spread a thin layer of rice over it with wet hands, sprinkle with sesame seeds and flip so the nori faces up.
Line crab, avocado and cucumber along one edge and roll firmly away from you, pressing to make a tight inside-out roll.
Slice into 8 pieces with a wet knife and serve with soy sauce, wasabi and ginger; this roll was created in Los Angeles in the 1960s–70s.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 8 sand dab fillets or small whole cleaned sand dabs (about 680 g / 1.5 lb); sub petrale sole or flounder
steps: Pat the fish dry and dredge in seasoned flour, shaking off the excess.
Heat the oil and 2 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat and fry the fish 2–3 minutes per side until golden and opaque and flaking easily.
Remove the fish, add the remaining butter to the pan and swirl until nutty brown, then add lemon juice and parsley.
Pour the brown butter over the sand dabs and serve with lemon wedges and boiled potatoes, a San Francisco grill classic.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 farmed red abalone (about 225 g / 8 oz total meat), shucked and cleaned
60 g (1 cup) panko or fine cracker crumbs
steps: Trim the dark skirt and slice each abalone horizontally into 1 cm (3/8 in) steaks, then pound gently with a mallet until tender and about 6 mm (1/4 in) thick.
Season, dredge in flour, dip in egg and coat with crumbs.
Melt the butter in a skillet over high heat and fry the steaks 30–45 seconds per side until just golden; overcooking makes abalone tough.
Serve immediately with lemon wedges; wild California abalone harvest is closed, so buy legally farmed abalone (sub large sea scallops sliced in half).
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 6 slices bacon, cooked crisp and crumbled
85 g (3/4 cup) crumbled Roquefort or blue cheese
120 ml (1/2 cup) red wine vinaigrette with Dijon
steps: Arrange the chopped greens in a wide shallow bowl.
Lay the chicken, bacon, egg, avocado, tomato and blue cheese in neat rows across the greens.
Scatter chives over, present at the table, then toss with the vinaigrette just before serving, as created at Hollywood's Brown Derby.

ingredients: 450 g (1 lb) cooked Dungeness crab meat

steps: Simmer the celery hearts in the stock in a covered skillet for 15–20 minutes until tender when pierced.
Whisk the vinegar, olive oil and mustard with salt and pepper, pour over the celery in its dish and cool, then chill at least 1 hour to marinate.
Arrange the celery on lettuce, crisscross with anchovies, scatter egg, parsley and capers or pimiento, and serve cold, the salad of chef Victor Hirtzler of San Francisco's St. Francis Hotel.

1 can (310 g / 11 oz) mandarin orange segments, drained
3 green onions, sliced and 1/4 cup cilantro
1 cup crispy fried wonton strips or rice noodles
60 ml (1/4 cup) rice vinegar, 3 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp sesame oil, 2 tbsp honey, 1 tsp grated ginger
steps: Poach the chicken in simmering salted water for 15–18 minutes until 74°C (165°F) inside, cool and shred.
Whisk the vinegar, soy sauce, sesame oil, honey and ginger into a dressing.
Toss the cabbage, romaine, chicken, green onion and cilantro with the dressing.

2 tbsp tarragon vinegar or lemon juice
steps: Blend all the ingredients in a blender until smooth and pale green.

Serve over romaine, seafood salad or as a dip; it was created at San Francisco's Palace Hotel in the 1920s.

ingredients: 450 g (1 lb) pizza dough (homemade or bought)
170 g (6 oz) fresh goat cheese and mozzarella, crumbled/torn
1 red onion, thinly sliced and caramelised
1 cup roasted red peppers or cherry tomatoes
1/2 cup sun-dried tomatoes or artichoke hearts
fresh basil and arugula to finish
steps: Let the dough come to room temperature for 1 hour, and heat the oven with a pizza stone to its highest setting, about 260°C (500°F), for 30 minutes.
Stretch the dough into a thin 30 cm (12 in) round and brush with olive oil.
Scatter the cheeses and vegetables over and bake 8–12 minutes until the crust is crisp and spotted brown and the cheese bubbles.
Top with fresh basil and arugula, drizzle with oil and serve, in the spirit of Wolfgang Puck's Spago and Chez Panisse's café.

ingredients: 100 g (1/2 cup) active sourdough starter, fed and bubbly
steps: Mix the starter, flour and water into a shaggy dough, rest 30 minutes, then add the salt and squeeze it in.
Over the next 3–4 hours give the dough 4 sets of stretch-and-folds 30 minutes apart, then leave until about 50% risen and airy.
Shape into a tight round, place in a floured banneton, cover and refrigerate overnight (8–12 hours) for the classic tang.

Bake in a preheated covered Dutch oven at 250°C (480°F) for 20 minutes, slashing the top first, then uncover and bake at 230°C (450°F) for 20–25 minutes until deep brown and hollow-sounding; cool 1 hour before slicing.

ingredients: 900 g (2 lb) russet potatoes, cut into fries
steps: Soak the cut potatoes in cold water 10 minutes, dry well and toss with oil.
Bake on a sheet at 220°C (425°F) for 35–40 minutes, turning once, until crisp and golden (or deep-fry twice).
Meanwhile, warm the butter and garlic over low heat for 2 minutes until fragrant but not browned.
Toss the hot fries with the garlic butter, parsley, salt and Parmesan and serve at once, as at San Francisco ballparks and the Gilroy Garlic Festival.

ingredients: 12 baby artichokes, or 2 cans (400 g / 14 oz) artichoke hearts, drained
2 large eggs, beaten with 2 tbsp milk
120 ml (1/2 cup) aioli or ranch dressing, to serve
steps: Trim the baby artichokes down to the pale leaves, cut into quarters and rub with lemon; simmer 5 minutes in salted water and drain well.
Dredge each piece in flour, dip in egg and coat in breadcrumbs.
Fry in oil heated to 180°C (350°F) for 2–3 minutes until golden and crisp, then drain and salt.
Serve hot with aioli and lemon wedges, as at the roadside stands of Castroville, "Artichoke Center of the World".

steps: Whisk the egg whites and sugar until frothy, then whisk in the butter, extracts, water and flour into a smooth batter.
Spread 1 tbsp batter into thin 8 cm (3 in) circles on a parchment-lined tray, only 2–3 at a time.
Bake at 180°C (350°F) for 6–8 minutes until the edges are golden.

Working fast while hot, place a fortune in the centre, fold in half, then bend the folded edge over the rim of a cup; cool in a muffin tin to hold the shape. The cookie was popularised in San Francisco and Los Angeles.

900 g (2 lb, about 6 cups) olallieberries; sub blackberries
2 tbsp milk and 1 tbsp coarse sugar for the top

Line the pie dish with half the pastry, add the berries, dot with butter and cover with the top crust or a lattice, crimping the edges and cutting vents.
Brush with milk, sprinkle with sugar and bake at 220°C (425°F) for 20 minutes, then at 180°C (350°F) for 35–40 minutes until the filling bubbles thickly through the vents.
Cool at least 3 hours to set, and serve with vanilla ice cream, as along California's Central Coast around Cambria.

ingredients: pastry for a double-crust 23 cm (9 in) pie, made with butter
900 g (2 lb, about 6 cups) boysenberries, fresh or frozen
steps: Toss the berries with sugar, cornstarch and lemon juice (if frozen, don't thaw first).
Fill the pastry-lined dish, dot with butter, add the top crust, crimp, cut vents and brush with cream.
Bake at 220°C (425°F) for 20 minutes, then at 180°C (350°F) for 40 minutes until golden and bubbling in the centre.
Cool completely before slicing and serve with whipped cream; the boysenberry was made famous by Knott's Berry Farm in Buena Park.

4 large scoops (about 2 cups) vanilla ice cream

crushed ice, mint sprig and spent lime shell
steps: Shake the rums, lime juice, curaçao, orgeat and syrup hard with ice for 10 seconds.
Strain into a double old-fashioned glass filled with crushed ice.
Garnish with the lime shell and a mint sprig; Trader Vic Bergeron created it in Oakland in 1944. Use rums bought from licensed producers and serve only to adults.

ingredients: 1 untreated cedar grilling plank, soaked in water 1 hour
900 g (2 lb) skin-on wild salmon fillet (king/chinook or sockeye)
1 tbsp fresh dill or thyme, chopped
1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper
steps: Soak the cedar plank in water for at least 1 hour so it smoulders rather than burns.
Mix the brown sugar, mustard, soy sauce, dill, salt and pepper and spread over the flesh side of the salmon.
Lay the salmon skin-side down on the plank, top with lemon slices and set over medium heat on a covered grill, about 200°C (400°F).
Grill 15–20 minutes until the plank smokes and the salmon is opaque and flakes easily at 52–60°C (125–140°F); serve on the plank with roasted potatoes and greens.

ingredients: 1.4 kg (3 lb) skin-on wild salmon fillet
2 tbsp maple syrup or honey for glazing
steps: Dissolve the salt and sugar in the water, submerge the salmon and brine in the refrigerator for 4 hours.
Rinse, pat dry and set on a rack in the refrigerator uncovered for 1 hour until the surface feels tacky (the pellicle).
Smoke over alder wood at 80–95°C (175–200°F) for 2.5–3 hours, brushing with maple syrup and pepper in the last hour, until the salmon reaches 63°C (145°F) inside and is deep amber.
Cool and serve warm or cold with crackers, cream cheese and capers; alder is the traditional Northwest smoking wood.

ingredients: 1 whole side (about 1.8 kg / 4 lb) wild sockeye or coho salmon, butterflied, skin on
4 long split cedar stakes and a bed of alder wood for the fire
steps: Build an alder wood fire and let it burn to a strong, steady bed of coals with some flame.
Weave the butterflied salmon onto split cedar stakes with crosswise cedar sticks to hold it open flat, then season the flesh with salt.

Drive the stakes into the ground leaning toward the fire, flesh facing the heat about 60 cm (2 ft) away, and cook 45–60 minutes, turning the skin side to the fire for the last 10 minutes, until the flesh is opaque and flakes easily.
Brush with butter and lemon and serve with roasted potatoes, salad and berries, in the tradition of Coast Salish salmon ceremonies of Puget Sound (at home, bake on a cedar plank at 200°C / 400°F).

ingredients: 680 g (1.5 lb) skinless salmon fillet, chilled
1 tbsp chopped dill and 1 tsp lemon zest
4 brioche buns, lettuce, red onion and tartar sauce
steps: Finely chop a quarter of the salmon to a paste and the rest into small pieces, then mix with mustard, green onion, dill, lemon zest, panko and salt.
Form 4 patties about 2 cm thick and chill 15 minutes to firm.
Fry in oil in a skillet over medium-high heat for 3–4 minutes per side until browned and cooked through at 63°C (145°F).
Serve on toasted buns with lettuce, onion and tartar sauce.

ingredients: 2 live Dungeness crabs (about 900 g / 2 lb each)
steps: Bring 5 cm (2 in) of well-salted water to a rolling boil in a large pot fitted with a steamer rack.
Chill the live crabs in the freezer for 15 minutes to sedate them, then put them in the steamer, cover and steam 15–20 minutes until bright orange and the meat is opaque.
Cool slightly, pull off the back shell, remove the gills and rinse, then crack the legs and break the body in half.
Serve with melted butter, lemon wedges and sourdough bread, the classic Northwest crab feed.

steps: Whisk the egg, mayonnaise, mustard, Worcestershire and lemon juice, then gently fold in the crab, green onion and 3/4 cup panko without breaking up the lumps.
Shape into 8 cakes, coat lightly in the remaining panko and chill 20 minutes.
Fry in butter in a skillet over medium heat for 3–4 minutes per side until golden and hot through.
Serve with lemon wedges and a remoulade or tartar sauce.

ingredients: 24 live Pacific or Kumamoto oysters from a certified shellfish dealer (Willapa Bay, Hood Canal, Puget Sound)
steps: Buy only live, tightly closed oysters from a certified shellfish dealer, keep them cold below 5°C (41°F) and eat on the day; because raw shellfish carry risk, those who are pregnant, elderly or immune-compromised should eat them cooked instead.
Mix the vinegar, shallot and pepper to make a mignonette and chill.
Scrub the shells, hold each oyster cupped side down in a towel, work an oyster knife into the hinge, twist to open and cut the muscle free, keeping the liquor.
Arrange on crushed ice and serve at once with mignonette and lemon.

2 large eggs, beaten with 2 tbsp milk
90 g (1.5 cups) panko or cracker crumbs
steps: Pat the oysters dry and dredge in seasoned flour, dip in egg and coat in crumbs.
Heat the butter and oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the oysters in batches 2 minutes per side until golden and the edges curl and the oysters are cooked through.
Drain and serve with lemon and tartar sauce, or on a toasted roll as an oyster po'boy.

ingredients: 12 Pacific razor clams, cleaned and butterflied (dug in season on Washington's Long Beach Peninsula); sub large frozen razor clams
steps: Blanch the clams 10 seconds in boiling water to loosen the shell and skin, then remove the gut and gills, split and rinse, keeping the white meat and digger.
Dredge each clam in seasoned flour, dip in egg and coat in cracker crumbs.
Fry in hot butter and oil over medium-high heat for 45–60 seconds per side until golden and just cooked; longer makes them chewy.
Serve immediately with lemon and tartar sauce.

240 ml (1 cup) dry white wine (Washington Pinot Gris)
steps: Discard any mussels with cracked shells or that won't close when tapped.
Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat and cook the shallots and garlic for 3 minutes until soft, then add the wine and bring to a boil.
Add the mussels, cover and steam 5–6 minutes, shaking the pot, until the shells open; discard any that stay closed.
Stir in cream and parsley and serve in bowls with the broth and crusty bread.

ingredients: 1 live geoduck (about 900 g / 2 lb) from a certified shellfish dealer, sashimi-grade
steps: Use only a live, sashimi-grade geoduck bought from a certified shellfish dealer and keep it cold; anyone pregnant or immune-compromised should eat it cooked.
Cut the siphon from the shell, blanch it in boiling water for 10 seconds, plunge into iced water and peel off the tough skin.
Split the siphon lengthwise, rinse out any sand, and slice very thinly on the diagonal; keep the body meat for chowder or stir-fry.
Arrange the crisp slices on ice over cucumber and serve with soy, wasabi, ginger and a squeeze of citrus.

ingredients: 900 g (2 lb) whole live or fresh BC/Puget Sound spot prawns, heads removed

Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the garlic and pepper flakes for 30 seconds.
Add the prawns in their shells and cook 2–3 minutes, tossing, until just pink and opaque.
Toss with lemon juice, parsley and flaky salt and serve straight away to peel and eat, during the short May spot-prawn season.

ingredients: 900 g (2 lb) boneless skin-on chicken thighs
2 tbsp grated ginger and 3 garlic cloves, grated
1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
2 cups iceberg salad with creamy dressing, sesame seeds
steps: Simmer the soy sauce, sugar, mirin, ginger and garlic for 5 minutes, cool, and marinate the chicken in half of it for 2 hours in the refrigerator.
Thicken the remaining sauce with the cornstarch slurry over medium heat for 1 minute until glossy.
Grill or broil the chicken over high heat 5–6 minutes per side until charred at the edges and 74°C (165°F) inside, then chop into strips.
Serve over rice with the sweet sauce poured over, sesame seeds and a side of iceberg salad, the Seattle strip-mall plate.

950 ml (4 cups) fish or vegetable stock
480 ml (2 cups) milk and 240 ml (1 cup) cream
1 cup corn kernels, 2 tbsp dill, salt and pepper
steps: Melt the butter over medium heat and cook onion, celery and carrot for 6 minutes until soft, then stir in the flour for 2 minutes.
Gradually whisk in the stock, add potatoes and simmer 15 minutes until tender.
Add milk, cream and corn and heat 5 minutes without boiling, then stir in the smoked salmon and dill and warm through 2 minutes.
Season and serve with oyster crackers or sourdough bread.

ingredients: 1.4 kg (3 lb) skinless salmon (sockeye or king), cut into 2.5 cm (1 in) strips
120 ml (1/2 cup) maple syrup or honey for glazing
steps: Dissolve the sugar and salt in the water and brine the salmon strips in the refrigerator overnight (8–10 hours).
Rinse, pat dry and dry on racks in the refrigerator for 1–2 hours until tacky.
Smoke over alder at 70–80°C (160–175°F) for 3–4 hours, brushing with maple syrup every hour, until firm, glossy and deep mahogany, and at least 63°C (145°F) inside.
Cool and refrigerate up to 2 weeks; the sweet, chewy strips are a traditional Northwest Indigenous and fishing-town snack.

ingredients: 4 all-beef hot dogs or Polish sausages, split
sliced jalapeños, sriracha or brown mustard, to serve
steps: Cook the onion in butter over medium heat for 12–15 minutes until soft and golden.
Grill the split dogs over medium-high heat for 5–6 minutes until charred and hot through, and toast the buns.
Spread each bun generously with cream cheese, add the dog and top with grilled onions, jalapeños and sriracha or mustard, as sold outside Seattle stadiums and bars late at night.

ingredients: 2 large Walla Walla sweet onions; sub Vidalia or other sweet onions
300 ml (1.25 cups) cold buttermilk or beer
1.4 l (6 cups) vegetable oil for frying
steps: Slice the onions into 1 cm (3/8 in) rings and separate them.
Whisk 1 cup flour with the baking powder, salt, paprika and buttermilk or beer into a smooth batter.
Heat the oil to 190°C (375°F), dust the rings in the remaining flour, dip in batter and fry in batches 2–3 minutes until deep golden and crisp.
Drain, salt and serve hot with fry sauce or ranch.

ingredients: 1.4 l (6 cups) vegetable oil for frying
steps: Parboil the whole potatoes in salted water for 8 minutes until just tender at the edges, then cool completely.
Grate the potatoes coarsely, squeeze out moisture, and mix with flour, salt, onion powder and pepper.
Shape into small cylinders about 2.5 cm (1 in) long and chill 15 minutes; the tot was invented by Ore-Ida in Ontario, Oregon.
Fry in batches at 180°C (350°F) for 3–4 minutes until deep golden and crisp, drain and salt; serve with ketchup.

ingredients: powdered sugar and lemon wedges, to serve
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F) with a 25 cm (10 in) cast-iron skillet inside for 10 minutes.
Blend the eggs, flour, milk, sugar, salt and nutmeg until smooth and frothy.
Add the butter to the hot skillet to melt and coat, pour in the batter and bake 18–20 minutes without opening the door until dramatically puffed and golden brown.
Dust with powdered sugar and serve straight away with lemon, as at Seattle's Manca's Café, where it was created.

ingredients: pastry for a double-crust 23 cm (9 in) pie, made with butter
900 g (2 lb, about 6 cups) Oregon marionberries, fresh or frozen; sub blackberries
1 tbsp milk and 1 tbsp coarse sugar for the top
steps: Toss the berries with sugar, cornstarch and lemon juice.
Fill the pastry-lined dish, dot with butter, cover with a lattice or vented top crust and brush with milk and sugar.
Bake at 220°C (425°F) for 20 minutes, then at 180°C (350°F) for 40 minutes until the crust is golden and the filling bubbles thickly.
Cool at least 3 hours before slicing and serve with vanilla ice cream, Oregon's signature pie.

ingredients: 450 g (1 lb) sashimi-grade ahi (yellowfin or bigeye tuna), cut into 2 cm (3/4 in) cubes
2 tbsp ogo (fresh limu seaweed), chopped, or rehydrated wakame as a substitute
1 tsp ʻinamona (roasted kukui nut relish) or toasted sesame seeds
1/2 tsp Hawaiian ʻalaea sea salt or flaky sea salt
steps: Use only sashimi/sushi-grade tuna that has been kept very cold; cube it on a chilled board and keep it in the fridge until mixing.
Gently toss the tuna with the shoyu, sesame oil, onions, ogo, ʻinamona, salt and chili flakes.
Cover and chill for 15–30 minutes so the flavours soak in, but eat the same day.
Serve cold over hot white rice as a poke bowl, or on its own as pūpū (appetizer).

ingredients: 2.7 kg (6 lb) bone-in pork shoulder (pork butt)
1 1/2 tbsp Hawaiian ʻalaea red sea salt, or coarse sea salt
2 tbsp liquid smoke (to mimic the imu underground oven)
4–6 ti or banana leaves (optional), or foil
1/2 head green cabbage, cut into wedges (optional)
steps: Pierce the pork all over with a knife, rub in the liquid smoke and then the sea salt.
Wrap the pork in ti or banana leaves if you have them, place in a slow cooker or roasting pan and add the water.
Cook on low in a slow cooker for 10–12 hours, or covered in a 160°C (325°F) oven for 6–7 hours, until the meat falls apart and reaches at least 90°C (195°F).
Shred the pork in its juices, adding the cabbage for the last 30 minutes if using, and adjust salt.
Serve with rice, poi and lomi lomi salmon as at a lūʻau.

ingredients: 900 g (2 lb) pork butt, cut into 6 chunks
340 g (12 oz) salted butterfish (black cod) or salmon, cut into 6 pieces
24–30 lūʻau (taro) leaves, stems removed; fresh spinach is a substitute
12 ti leaves, ribs trimmed (or foil and parchment)
steps: Season the pork with the salt.
Stack 4–5 lūʻau leaves, place a piece of pork and a piece of fish in the centre and fold the leaves around them into a bundle.
Lay 2 ti leaves in a cross, set the bundle in the middle, fold up and tie the ends of the ti leaves (or wrap tightly in parchment then foil).

Steam the bundles in a covered steamer over simmering water for 4 hours, topping up the water, until the pork is very tender and the taro leaves are fully cooked (undercooked taro leaves sting the throat).
Unwrap the ti leaves (they are not eaten) and serve with rice or poi.

ingredients: 900 g (2 lb) boneless short ribs, thinly sliced across the bone (kalbi-style) or chicken thighs
740 g (4 cups) cooked white rice (2 scoops per plate)
steps: Mix the shoyu, sugar, sesame oil, garlic, ginger and green onions, add the meat and marinate overnight in the fridge.
Heat a grill or cast-iron pan over high heat.
Grill the meat for 2–3 minutes per side until caramelised and cooked through (chicken to 74°C / 165°F).
Serve on a plate with two scoops of white rice and one scoop of mac salad, the classic plate-lunch layout.

ingredients: 1.4 kg (3 lb) bone-in chicken thighs and drumsticks
steps: Whisk all the ingredients except the chicken; reserve 120 ml (1/2 cup) for basting and marinate the chicken in the rest overnight.
Prepare a medium charcoal or gas grill (ideally over kiawe/mesquite wood) at about 180°C (350°F).
Grill the chicken, turning ("huli" means turn) every 5 minutes and basting with the reserved sauce, for 30–40 minutes.
Cook until charred, sticky and 74°C (165°F) at the bone.
Serve with rice, macaroni salad and grilled pineapple.

ingredients: 900 g (2 lb) boneless chicken thighs, cut into bite-size pieces
60 g (1/2 cup) mochiko (sweet glutinous rice flour)
720 ml (3 cups) vegetable oil, for frying
steps: Mix the mochiko, cornstarch, shoyu, sugar, eggs, garlic, green onions and salt into a batter.
Add the chicken, coat well and marinate overnight in the fridge.
Heat the oil to 175°C (350°F) in a deep pan.
Fry the chicken in batches for 5–6 minutes until deep golden, crisp and cooked through.
Drain on a rack and serve with rice, mac salad or in a bento.

ingredients: 4 boneless chicken thighs, pounded to 1 cm (1/2 in) thick
1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper
480 ml (2 cups) vegetable oil, for frying
steps: Season the chicken, then dredge in flour, dip in egg and press firmly into the panko.
Heat the oil to 175°C (350°F) in a deep skillet.
Fry the chicken for 4–5 minutes per side until golden and 74°C (165°F) inside; drain on a rack.
For the katsu sauce, whisk the ketchup, Worcestershire, shoyu and sugar until smooth.
Slice into strips and serve with rice, shredded cabbage or mac salad and the sauce.

ingredients: 900 g (2 lb) large shell-on shrimp, deveined through the shell
steps: Toss the shrimp with half the garlic, the olive oil and salt; marinate for 30 minutes in the fridge.
Pat off excess garlic and dust the shrimp with the flour mixed with paprika.
Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the shrimp for 2–3 minutes per side until pink and opaque.
Push the shrimp aside, add the remaining garlic and fry for 1–2 minutes until golden, then toss everything together.
Serve with two scoops of rice, spooning the garlic butter over, with lemon and parsley, like the North Shore shrimp trucks.

ingredients: 900 g (2 lb) lūʻau (young taro) leaves, stems removed; fresh spinach is a substitute
680 g (1.5 lb) cleaned squid or octopus (heʻe), cut into bite-size pieces
1 can (400 ml / 13.5 fl oz) coconut milk
steps: Boil the taro leaves in the water for 1 hour, changing the water once, until completely soft; taro leaves must be well cooked or they irritate the throat. Drain and chop. (Spinach needs only 3 minutes.)
Simmer the squid in fresh water for 30–40 minutes until tender (octopus may take longer); drain.
Melt the butter in a pot and cook the onion for 4 minutes, then add the coconut milk, salt and sugar and bring to a gentle simmer.
Stir in the leaves and squid and simmer for 10 minutes until creamy.
Serve warm with poi or rice at a lūʻau.

ingredients: 1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper
30 g (2 tbsp) butter and 2 tbsp flour
740 g (4 cups) hot cooked white rice
steps: Season the beef and shape into 4 patties; fry in the oil over medium-high heat for 4–5 minutes per side until cooked through (71°C / 160°F).
In the same pan, cook the onion and mushrooms in the butter for 5 minutes, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the stock and shoyu and simmer for 5 minutes into a brown gravy.

Scoop rice into each bowl, top with a patty, smother with gravy and crown with a fried egg.

ingredients: 1 can (340 g / 12 oz) Spam, sliced into 8 slices
740 g (4 cups) cooked short-grain rice, warm and lightly salted
steps: Fry the Spam slices in the oil over medium heat for 2–3 minutes per side until browned.
Add the shoyu, sugar and mirin and simmer for 1–2 minutes, turning, until the slices are glazed.
Lay a half sheet of nori on the board, set a musubi mold (or the cleaned Spam can) on it, press in rice, sprinkle with furikake and top with a slice of Spam.

1.5 litres (6 cups) dashi or chicken stock

2 eggs, made into a thin omelette and sliced
steps: Simmer the stock with the dried shrimp, ginger, shoyu and salt for 20–30 minutes; strain.

ingredients: 1.5 litres (6 cups) chicken stock or water
170 g (6 oz) bean thread (mung bean glass) noodles, the "long rice"
4 green onions, cut into 2.5 cm (1 in) lengths
steps: Simmer the chicken with the stock, ginger and garlic for 35–40 minutes until cooked through and tender.
Meanwhile soak the noodles in warm water for 20 minutes, drain and cut into 10 cm (4 in) lengths.
Remove the chicken, shred the meat and discard skin and bones; strain the broth back into the pot.

2 tbsp hoisin sauce and 1 tbsp oyster sauce
1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 120 ml (1/2 cup) water
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, warm water and oil into a smooth dough, knead for 8 minutes and let rise covered for 1 hour until doubled.
Simmer the hoisin, oyster sauce, shoyu, sugar and cornstarch slurry for 2 minutes until thick, stir in the char siu and cool.
Divide the dough into 12 pieces, roll each into a 10 cm (4 in) round, add 2 tbsp filling and pleat closed; set each on a square of parchment and rest for 20 minutes.
Steam over boiling water for 15 minutes until puffy and cooked through.
Serve warm; manapua is Hawaii's version of Cantonese char siu bao.

ingredients: 2 cans (425 g / 15 oz each) kidney beans, drained
1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper
steps: Simmer the ham hock in the water for 1 hour; remove, shred the meat and return it to the pot.
Brown the sausage in a skillet for 5 minutes and add to the pot with its fat.
Add the onion, carrots, celery, potatoes and tomato sauce and simmer for 30 minutes.
Add the beans and cabbage and simmer another 15–20 minutes until everything is tender.
Season and serve hot with rice or Portuguese sweet bread.

ingredients: 60 g (1/4 cup) Hawaiian or coarse sea salt
steps: Rub the salmon all over with the salt, cover and cure in the fridge overnight (at least 8 hours); use previously frozen, sushi-grade salmon since it is not cooked.
Rinse off the salt, soak in cold water for 1 hour to remove excess saltiness (taste a piece), and pat dry.
Dice the salmon into small cubes.
Gently "lomi" (massage) the salmon with the tomatoes and onions with your hands, keeping it cold, and chill until serving.

ingredients: 900 g (2 lb) taro corms (kalo); fresh Hawaiian taro is best
steps: Scrub the taro (wear gloves; raw taro irritates skin), cover with water and boil or steam for 1–1 1/2 hours until completely soft; raw taro must never be eaten.
Peel while warm and cut into chunks.
Pound with a poi pounder or blitz in a food processor, adding water a little at a time until it becomes a smooth, sticky paste.
Eat fresh and sweet, or leave covered at room temperature for 1–3 days to develop the traditional tangy "sour poi".
Serve in a bowl alongside kalua pig, laulau or lomi lomi salmon, eaten with the fingers.

ingredients: 900 g (2 lb) beef flank or round, sliced 1 cm (1/2 in) thick along the grain
steps: Mix the shoyu, salt, sugar, garlic, ginger and chili and marinate the beef overnight in the fridge.
Drain and lay the strips on racks; dry in a 80°C (175°F) oven or dehydrator for 3–4 hours until dry outside but slightly chewy inside.

Slice and serve as pūpū or with rice and poi, the Hawaiian "beef rope" jerky.

steps: Warm the lemon juice, honey and sugar until dissolved, then stir in the li hing powder, salt and spices.

Store in a sealed jar and nibble as a sweet-salty-sour snack, the way crack seed shops in Hawaii sell it.

180 ml (3/4 cup) guava nectar or guava concentrate
240 ml (1 cup) guava nectar thickened with 2 tbsp cornstarch, for glaze
480 ml (2 cups) heavy cream, whipped with 3 tbsp sugar

Frost with whipped cream and spread the guava glaze on top; chill and serve.

ingredients: 190 g (1 1/2 cups) all-purpose flour, 60 g (1/2 cup) macadamia nuts finely chopped and 115 g (1/2 cup) melted butter, for the crust
680 g (1.5 lb) purple Okinawan sweet potatoes (beni imo)
1 can (400 ml / 13.5 fl oz) coconut milk

steps: Mix the flour, macadamia nuts and melted butter, press into a 23 x 23 cm (9 x 9 in) pan and bake at 175°C (350°F) for 15 minutes until golden.

ingredients: 900 g (2 lb) Copper River sockeye or king salmon fillet, skin on, cut in 4 portions (substitute any wild Alaska salmon)
1 tsp kosher salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper
1 tbsp birch syrup or brown sugar (optional glaze)
steps: Heat a grill to medium-high, about 220°C (425°F), and scrape and oil the grates well.
Pat the salmon dry, brush with oil and season with salt and pepper; mix the butter, lemon juice, garlic, dill and birch syrup for basting.
Grill skin-side down with the lid closed for 6 to 8 minutes until the skin is crisp and releases easily; Copper River fish is rich in fat, so it stays moist.
Baste with the butter, flip briefly for 1 to 2 minutes if you like, and take off the grill when the centre reaches 52 to 57°C (125 to 135°F) and just flakes, or 63°C (145°F) for fully cooked.
Rest 3 minutes and serve with lemon wedges, wild rice and grilled vegetables.

ingredients: 1.8 kg (4 lb) frozen cooked red king crab legs, thawed overnight in the fridge
1 lemon, halved, plus wedges to serve
steps: Alaska king crab is cooked and flash-frozen on the boat, so you only need to reheat it; cut long legs at the joints to fit your pot.
Bring the water, lemon halves and bay leaf to a boil in a large pot fitted with a steamer basket, add the crab legs, cover and steam 6 to 8 minutes until hot through and fragrant.
Meanwhile melt the butter with the garlic over low heat for 3 minutes and stir in the parsley.
Split the shells lengthwise with kitchen shears and serve with the garlic butter and lemon wedges for dipping.

ingredients: 700 g (1 1/2 lb) skinless Pacific halibut fillet, cut in 8 strips
900 g (2 lb) russet potatoes, cut in 1 cm (1/2 in) batons
160 g (1 1/4 cups) all-purpose flour plus 30 g (1/4 cup) for dredging
1 tsp baking powder and 1 tsp salt
300 ml (1 1/4 cups) cold Alaskan amber ale or sparkling water
2 litres (8 cups) vegetable oil for frying
Tartar sauce, malt vinegar and lemon wedges, to serve
steps: Soak the potato batons in cold water 15 minutes, dry well, and fry in oil at 160°C (325°F) for 5 minutes until soft but pale; drain.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, salt and pepper with the cold ale into a batter like thick cream.
Raise the oil to 190°C (375°F), pat the halibut dry, dust in flour, dip in batter and fry in batches for 4 to 5 minutes until deep golden and the fish is opaque and flaky inside (63°C / 145°F).
Return the potatoes to the hot oil for 2 to 3 minutes until crisp and golden, drain and salt.
Serve the fish on the chips with tartar sauce, malt vinegar and lemon, as at Homer and Seward harbour shacks.

ingredients: 680 g (1 1/2 lb) halibut cheeks, trimmed of any membrane (substitute thick halibut or cod loin pieces)
1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp black pepper
steps: Pat the cheeks dry and dust lightly with flour seasoned with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering and sear the cheeks for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden and just firm, then move to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium, add the butter and garlic and cook 1 minute until the butter foams and smells nutty, then add capers and lemon juice.
Return the cheeks to the pan, spoon the sauce over for 30 seconds until hot through and opaque, sprinkle with parsley and serve with rice or potatoes.

ingredients: 4 skin-on sablefish (black cod) fillets, about 170 g (6 oz) each
Sliced green onion and steamed rice, to serve
steps: Warm the miso, mirin, sake and sugar in a small pan over low heat for 2 minutes until smooth, then cool and stir in the soy sauce and ginger.
Pat the fish dry, coat with the marinade in a zip bag and refrigerate 24 hours (at least 6) so the rich, buttery Alaska sablefish absorbs the flavour.
Heat a grill or broiler to high, wipe off excess marinade so it does not burn, and oil the grates or a foil-lined tray.
Grill skin-side down 6 to 8 minutes, then turn carefully and cook 2 to 3 minutes until the surface is caramelised in spots and the flesh flakes (63°C / 145°F).
Serve with steamed rice, green onion and pickled vegetables.

ingredients: 2 sheets frozen puff pastry or 1 double pie crust (about 500 g / 1 lb), thawed
600 g (1 1/3 lb) skinless salmon fillet, cut in 2 cm (3/4 in) pieces
1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper
steps: Melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion and cabbage for 10 minutes until soft and sweet, then season and cool; this Russian-Alaskan pie (from pirog) is a Kodiak and Kenai staple.

Roll one pastry sheet into a 25 x 35 cm (10 x 14 in) rectangle on a lined baking sheet and layer the rice, cabbage-onion mix, salmon, sliced eggs and dill, seasoning each layer and leaving a 2.5 cm (1 in) border.
Cover with the second sheet, crimp the edges firmly, cut a few slits in the top and brush with beaten egg.
Bake at 200°C (400°F) for 40 to 45 minutes until the pastry is deep golden and the salmon inside is cooked through (63°C / 145°F at the centre).
Rest 10 minutes, slice into squares and serve warm with sour cream or ketchup, as Alaskans often do.

ingredients: 900 g (2 lb) moose stew meat, cut in 3 cm (1 1/4 in) cubes (substitute beef chuck or venison)
30 g (1/4 cup) all-purpose flour, 1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper
3 tbsp vegetable oil or bacon fat
2 bay leaves and 1 tsp dried thyme
450 g (1 lb) potatoes and 3 carrots, cut in chunks
steps: Toss the moose in seasoned flour and brown in batches in hot fat in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat, 5 minutes per batch, until well crusted; lean moose needs this browning for flavour.
Add the onion and garlic and cook 5 minutes, then stir in the tomato paste for 1 minute and pour in the stock, scraping up the browned bits.
Add the bay leaves and thyme, cover and simmer very gently for 1 1/2 hours until the meat is almost tender.
Add potatoes, carrots and celery and simmer 40 to 45 minutes more until the vegetables are soft and the meat is fork-tender.
Adjust the seasoning and serve hot with sourdough bread or pilot bread.

ingredients: 700 g (1 1/2 lb) ground reindeer or caribou meat (substitute ground venison)
225 g (8 oz) ground pork fat or fatty ground pork
1 tsp black pepper and 1 tsp ground coriander
1 tsp sweet paprika and 1/2 tsp smoked paprika
1/2 tsp garlic powder and 1/2 tsp ground allspice
steps: Keep everything very cold, then mix the reindeer, pork fat, salt, spices and ice water with your hands for 2 minutes until the mixture turns sticky and well bound.
Fry a small test patty to check the seasoning, then shape the rest into 12 patties about 1.5 cm (1/2 in) thick, or stuff into hog casings if you have a sausage stuffer.
Cook in the oil in a skillet over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes per side until browned and cooked through to 71°C (160°F).
Serve with eggs, sourdough pancakes and coffee, a classic Alaskan diner breakfast (fully cooked bought reindeer links just need browning for 8 minutes).

ingredients: 2 tbsp vegetable oil or melted butter
1 tsp baking soda dissolved in 1 tbsp warm water
Butter, birch syrup or maple syrup, to serve
steps: The night before, mix the starter, flour and warm water in a large bowl, cover and leave at room temperature 8 to 12 hours; return 240 ml (1 cup) of this sponge to your starter jar, as Alaska "sourdoughs" have done since the Gold Rush.
In the morning beat the egg, sugar, oil and salt into the remaining sponge.
Just before cooking, fold in the dissolved baking soda; the batter will foam and double.
Ladle 60 ml (1/4 cup) portions onto a hot greased griddle over medium heat and cook 2 minutes until bubbles break on top, then flip and cook 1 minute until golden.
Serve stacked with butter and birch syrup alongside reindeer sausage.

ingredients: 1.4 kg (3 lb) skin-on king or sockeye salmon fillet, cut lengthwise into 2.5 cm (1 in) strips
120 ml (1/2 cup) birch syrup, maple syrup or honey, plus extra for basting
1 tsp garlic powder and 1 tsp black pepper
steps: Stir the salt, brown sugar, syrup, soy sauce, garlic and pepper into the water until dissolved, submerge the salmon strips and brine in the fridge 8 to 12 hours.
Rinse the strips, pat dry and lay them skin-side down on oiled racks in a cool, breezy place or in front of a fan for 2 to 3 hours until a tacky glaze (pellicle) forms.

Smoke over alder at 65 to 80°C (150 to 175°F), raising the heat gradually, for 5 to 6 hours, brushing with syrup every hour, until the strips are firm, glossy and dark and the internal temperature has reached at least 63°C (145°F).
Cool completely and refrigerate in sealed bags up to 2 weeks or freeze; this chewy "squaw candy" or "Indian candy" is a favourite trail snack.

ingredients: 4 fresh whole chum or sockeye salmon, about 2.5 kg (5 1/2 lb) each, just caught
Coarse salt (about 3 tbsp) for a light salting (optional, used by some families)
A shaded, breezy fish rack or drying shed
Seal oil or butter, to serve (substitute olive oil)
steps: Yukola is traditional Yup'ik, Athabascan and Iñupiaq air-dried salmon prepared in summer fish camps on the Yukon and Kuskokwim rivers; most people buy it from Alaska Native producers or receive it as gifts.

To prepare, the fish are gutted, the heads removed, and each side is filleted down to but not through the tail so both fillets hang joined; the flesh is scored crosswise down to the skin so air reaches it.
The split fish are hung skin-side out over poles in a shaded, windy spot, often with a smudge fire nearby to keep flies off, and dried for 2 to 4 weeks until hard and leathery throughout.
Store fully dried fish in a cool dry place or freezer, and to eat, break off pieces and dip them in seal oil or butter as a snack or with tea.

ingredients: 500 g (1 lb) bowhead or beluga whale muktuk (skin with attached blubber), harvested through Alaska Native subsistence
Soy sauce or seal oil, to serve
steps: Muktuk is the skin and underlying blubber of bowhead or beluga whale, a prized Iñupiat and Yup'ik food shared at whaling festivals such as Nalukataq; under US law it can only be harvested by Alaska Natives for subsistence and is not sold commercially, so it is eaten when shared by a whaling community.

Traditionally it is cut into small cubes and eaten fresh, frozen or aged; for the safest way to serve it today, bring the salted water to a boil, add the cubes and simmer 15 to 20 minutes until the skin is tender and the blubber is translucent.
Drain, cool slightly and eat in small bite-size pieces with a dip of soy sauce or seal oil; it has a firm, chewy skin and a rich, nutty-oily blubber that is very high in vitamin C.

ingredients: 450 g (1 lb) fresh or brined herring roe on kelp (or roe on hemlock branches)
Seal oil or melted butter, to serve (traditional)
steps: Herring roe on kelp is gathered each spring in Southeast Alaska (Sitka) when Pacific herring spawn on kelp fronds or on hemlock branches set in the water by Tlingit families; buy brined roe-on-kelp from licensed seafood shops if not harvested locally.
If brined, soak in cold water 1 to 2 hours, changing the water twice, to remove excess salt; if fresh, rinse well.
Dip the kelp sheets briefly in boiling water for 30 to 60 seconds until the roe turns opaque and pale, then plunge into cold water.
Cut into bite-size pieces and serve with soy sauce, a drizzle of seal oil or melted butter, and lemon; the eggs give a crisp, popping crunch.

ingredients: 225 g (1 cup) reindeer or caribou back fat, finely grated (traditional), or 200 g (1 cup) vegetable shortening (Crisco), which most Alaskan cooks use today
60 ml (1/4 cup) seal oil or vegetable oil
120 ml (1/2 cup) cold water or fresh snow
300 g (2 cups) mixed wild berries: salmonberries, blueberries, crowberries or lowbush cranberries
225 g (8 oz) cooked whitefish, flaked and squeezed dry (optional, Yup'ik style)
steps: Akutaq (Yup'ik for "something mixed") is a traditional whipped dessert; put the fat in a large, cold bowl and beat it with your hand or a mixer for 5 minutes until soft and creamy.
Gradually beat in the oil and the cold water or snow a little at a time, whipping continuously for 10 to 15 minutes until the mixture turns white, light and fluffy like frosting.
If using fish, beat in the cooked flaked whitefish, then stir in the sugar.
Gently fold in the berries and serve chilled or frozen, as at potlatches and holiday gatherings.

ingredients: 900 g (2 lb / about 6 cups) ripe salmonberries (Rubus spectabilis), picked over (substitute raspberries or cloudberries)
1 packet (50 g / 1.75 oz) powdered fruit pectin
steps: Lightly crush the salmonberries in a wide heavy pot, stir in the pectin and lemon juice, and bring to a full rolling boil over high heat, stirring.
Add all the sugar at once with the butter, return to a hard boil that cannot be stirred down, and boil exactly 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Skim off foam, ladle into hot sterilized jars leaving 6 mm (1/4 in) headspace, seal and process in a boiling water bath for 10 minutes, or refrigerate and use within 3 weeks.
Spread the bright orange-gold jam on pilot bread, sourdough pancakes or biscuits.

ingredients: 40 litres (about 10 gallons) fresh birch sap, tapped in early spring from paper birch trees (Betula papyrifera)
A wide evaporating pan or several large stockpots
steps: Alaska birch syrup is made in April when sap runs; strain the freshly collected sap through cheesecloth and keep it cold, using it within 2 days.
Boil the sap in a wide pan outdoors over steady high heat, adding more sap as it reduces; birch needs about 100 parts sap to 1 part syrup, far more than maple, and its sugars scorch easily.
When the volume is low, move to a smaller pot and finish gently over low heat until it reaches 104°C (219°F) and coats a spoon; this yields about 400 ml (1 2/3 cups).

Filter while hot, bottle in sterilized jars and refrigerate; the dark, tangy, molasses-like syrup is used in glazes for salmon, dressings and on pancakes (buy from Alaskan producers if you cannot tap trees).

ingredients: 100 g (2 cups) fresh young Sitka or white spruce tips, papery husks removed, rinsed
steps: Harvest only the soft, bright green new tips in late spring, a few from each tree so it is not harmed, and make sure you have positively identified spruce (avoid yew, which is toxic).
Bring the water and sugar to a boil over medium heat, stirring until dissolved, then remove from the heat and add the spruce tips and lemon juice.
Cover and steep 24 hours at room temperature or in the fridge, then simmer gently for 5 minutes, strain through a fine sieve and press the tips to extract the flavour.
Bottle in a sterilized jar and refrigerate up to 1 month; the citrusy, resinous syrup is used on pancakes, ice cream, in lemonade or in cocktails.

ingredients: 3 tbsp (45 g) vegetable shortening or butter
steps: Pilot bread (hardtack, the Sailor Boy brand is an Alaskan pantry staple) is a large, long-keeping cracker; whisk the flour, salt, sugar and baking powder and rub in the shortening until sandy.
Mix in the water to make a stiff dough, knead 5 minutes until smooth, then roll out 8 mm (1/3 in) thick.
Cut into 9 cm (3 1/2 in) rounds, place on a baking sheet and prick each all over with a fork in a neat pattern.
Bake at 190°C (375°F) for 25 to 30 minutes until pale golden and completely dry, turning once; cool fully and store airtight for months.
Serve with butter, peanut butter, salmonberry jam, smoked salmon or alongside moose stew.

ingredients: 1 small handful (about 8 g / 1/4 cup) dried Labrador tea leaves (Rhododendron groenlandicum or tomentosum, "Hudson's Bay tea")
steps: Positively identify the plant (rusty-woolly undersides on the leaves) before picking, and use it sparingly: the leaves contain ledol, which is harmful in large amounts, so brew it weak and do not drink it in quantity or during pregnancy.
Bring the water to a boil, add the leaves, then lower the heat and steep just below a simmer for 5 to 10 minutes, without a long hard boil, until pale gold and aromatic.
Strain into cups, sweeten with sugar or honey and add lemon if you like; it is drunk across Alaska Native villages as a warming, piney tundra tea.

ingredients: 4 tbsp ketchup, mustard and dill pickle chips, to serve

Heat a cast-iron skillet or grill over medium-high heat until very hot; season both sides of the patties with salt and pepper just before cooking.
Cook the patties 3 to 4 minutes per side, flipping once, until well browned and an instant-read thermometer reads 71°C (160°F) in the center.

steps: Score each hot dog lightly on the diagonal so it does not burst.

steps: Heat the oil in a deep heavy pot to 180°C (350°F); insert a skewer two-thirds of the way into each dry hot dog and dust lightly with flour.

Unwrap, brush with barbecue sauce and cook 15 to 20 minutes uncovered until the sauce sets into a sticky glaze; the meat should register at least 88°C (190°F).
Rest 10 minutes, slice between the bones, and serve with coleslaw, baked beans and cornbread.
